domain-scanners.notCheckable:
The following could not be checked from this sandbox.

- **Google, Bing and DuckDuckGo results pages:** none could be read directly. Google returned 'Your browser isn't supported anymore.', DuckDuckGo html and lite returned a captcha ('Unfortunately, bots use DuckDuckGo too.'), and Bing returned decoy results (chase.com for site:beastlyfacts.com, Microsoft pages through WebFetch). The brand-search finding therefore rests on the WebSearch tool, whose underlying engine is not identified. Knowledge-panel presence on Google itself is unverified.
- **Wayback Machine CDX:** unreachable (https connection reset, http 'Blocked by egress policy', WebFetch refused). The earliest capture date could not be read; only the availability API was used.
- **ScamDoc:** blocked. scamdoc.com returned a Cloudflare 'Sorry, you have been blocked' page and WebFetch 403, and scam-doc.com failed with a proxy 502 on CONNECT.
- **IsLegitSite:** only a captcha: 'Please complete the captcha to view the report for Beastlyfacts.com.'
- **Web Paranoid:** the scanner no longer exists. webparanoid.com/check/beastlyfacts.com serves a parked page titled 'webparanoid.com - This website is for sale!'.
- **Norton and Sucuri:** both results pages are JavaScript-only, so their JSON APIs were used instead. Norton's 'g' code was decoded from Norton's own app bundle. The Sucuri API call triggered a fresh scan (14:00 today), so the Sucuri result is current, not a cached one.
- **ScamAdviser:** the visible score renders as '0' before JavaScript runs, so the 71 comes from the page's embedded JSON and FAQ JSON-LD. The page gives no exact check date, only 'Last Update: 3 weeks ago'. Whether its crawler executes JavaScript, which decides whether the obfuscated email matters, is not documented.
- **Gridinsoft 'Clothing' tag:** traced only as far as the homepage text, which has no apparel words. Other pages were not searched.
- **Scoring formulas:** neither Gridinsoft nor ScamAdviser publishes weights, so no score change is forecast.
- **Not attempted:** VirusTotal (needs an API key) and Spamhaus DBL (the public resolver answer 127.255.255.254 means the query was refused, not a listing). urlscan.io shows 0 public scans.

findings.title: Every security engine reached reports the domain clean
findings.claim: No malware, phishing or blocklist engine flags beastlyfacts.com. URLVoid shows 0 of 36 engines, Google Safe Browsing returns its clean status with all threat flags false, Norton rates it Safe, Gridinsoft reports 0 detections, ScamAdviser cites DNSFilter as safe, and Sucuri's security check passes 6 of 6. McAfee is the only scanner with no verdict: it shows 'Unknown'.
findings.evidence: URLVoid https://www.urlvoid.com/scan/beastlyfacts.com/ : 'Detections Counts 0/36', 'First Seen 22 days ago', 'Last Analysis 22 days ago'. Counting with grep -c '^Nothing Found$' on the extracted text gave 36, and 0 rows read Detected, Suspicious or Malicious. Google Safe Browsing: curl https://transparencyreport.google.com/transparencyreport/api/v3/safebrowsing/status?site=beastlyfacts.com returned [["sb.ssr",1,false,false,false,false,false,1790763986924,"beastlyfacts.com",false]]. For comparison, Google's own phishing test page testsafebrowsing.appspot.com/s/phishing.html returns [["sb.ssr",2,false,false,true,...]]. The unlabeled timestamp field decodes to 2026-09-30 10:26:26 UTC (Sep 30, 6:26). Norton: https://safeweb.norton.com/safeweb/sites/v1/details?url=beastlyfacts.com&insert=0 returned {"rating":"g","categories":[0],"communityRating":0.0,"reviewCount":0}. Norton's own app bundle (static.nortoncdn.com/safeweb/prod/21/main.57884f22ddeee28f.js) maps that code with case"g":case"r":this.translate.get("COMMON.RATING_TEXT.SAFE"). Gridinsoft: 'Warning Cleanliness: 0 detections', '0 No external provider warnings', 'no major malware/phishing detections'. ScamAdviser positive highlight: 'This website is safe according to DNSFilter'. Sucuri API https://sitecheck.sucuri.net/api/v3/?scan=beastlyfacts.com: "security":{"rating":"B","passed":"6/6"}, and the response has no malware or blacklist warning keys. McAfee https://www.siteadvisor.com/sitereport.html?url=beastlyfacts.com: 'Website status: Unknown', 'We don’t have anything to share right now.'
findings.scope: Whole domain. People see this when they look the site up on a scanner or use a scanner's browser extension (Norton, McAfee, ScamAdviser app). Nothing shows on the site itself.

repro.correctedClaim: No malware, phishing or blocklist engine I could reach flags beastlyfacts.com. URLVoid shows 0/36 detections (36 of 36 engine rows read "Nothing Found"), Google Safe Browsing returns status 1 with all five threat flags false, Norton returns rating "g" (Safe in Norton's own bundle), Gridinsoft shows 0 detections and "No external provider warnings", ScamAdviser lists "This website is safe according to DNSFilter" as a positive highlight, and Sucuri's live scan today shows security passed 6/6 with no malware or blacklist keys in the response. McAfee SiteAdvisor gives no verdict ("Website status: Unknown"). Two details the finding leaves out: most of these verdicts are 3 weeks old, not live (URLVoid last analysis 22 days ago, Gridinsoft "Last checked September 27, 2026", ScamAdviser "Last Update: 3 weeks ago", Safe Browsing timestamp Sep 30 6:26); only Sucuri scanned today. And Gridinsoft's overall verdict is "Trusted but Verify" at 63/100 with "Safety Level: 0 negative tags, 1 warning signal". That warning signal is not an engine detection: the Cleanliness axis is at its maximum. A visitor sees none of this on the site itself. It shows only to people who look the domain up on a scanner or run a scanner's browser extension, on desktop or mobile alike. None of it is structured data that Google reads from the site.

For the control, testsafebrowsing.appspot.com/s/phishing.html returned [["sb.ssr",2,false,false,true,false,false,1792429311060,...]]. It reads "Detections Counts | 0/36", "First Seen | 22 days ago", "Last Analysis | 22 days ago", "Domain Registration | 2026-05-18". It also has "Safety Level: 0 negative tags, 1 warning signal", "0 / No external provider warnings", "no major malware/phishing detections", "Trusted but Verify" and "Last checked September 27, 2026 at 9:14 AM".

In the control, malware.testcategory.com comes back 0.0.0.0 with EDE(16) Censored. AdGuard DNS also resolves it normally. I could not check Spamhaus DBL or URIBL from here. Through Google DNS, the DBL listed test entry dbltest.com returns NXDOMAIN, so a clean answer from that path proves nothing. Cloudflare DNS returns 127.255.255.254, the public-resolver refusal. URIBL returns 127.0.0.1, its refusal code, for google.com and wikipedia.org too. Quad9 DoH reset the connection, and the URLhaus API returned Unauthorized.
repro.fix: No fix needed. This is a strength and nothing is wrong. If the report wants to sound fully precise, it should say "every engine that returned a verdict" (McAfee returned none). It should also state that most of these verdicts date from Sep 27 to Sep 30, with only Sucuri scanned live today. Optionally, the owner could ask McAfee for a rating through its site-owner request form so that "Unknown" changes, but nothing requires it.

findings.title: Gridinsoft 63/100 is unclaimed and has not been rechecked since Sep 27
findings.claim: Gridinsoft scores the site 63/100 'Trusted but Verify', the fourth of its five tiers, from a single automated check on Sep 27. The owner has not claimed the profile. Gridinsoft's published method names a claimed profile and verified contacts as inputs that can raise the score, and its reevaluation is free. The report also tags the site 'Clothing', which nothing on the homepage supports.
findings.evidence: https://gridinsoft.com/online-virus-scanner/url/beastlyfacts-com : title 'Beastlyfacts.com - Safe or Scam? (63/100 Trust Score)'. 'First checked September 27, 2026 at 9:14 AM' and 'Last checked September 27, 2026 at 9:14 AM'. The JSON-LD has "dateModified":"2026-09-27T09:14:06Z", which is 5:14 owner time. Tiers listed: 'Danger Zone, Risky Territory, Caution Advised, Trusted but Verify, Safe & Secure'. Positives: 'no major malware/phishing detections', 'a verified profile linked to this domain', 'business infrastructure', 'an active SSL certificate (3 months)'. Negative: 'a relatively new domain (5 months)'. Radar: 'Popularity: Estimated low traffic without Tranco or social profile data'. 'On-page mentions: Pets, Guides, Clothing'. On the extracted live homepage text, grep for clothing|shirt|apparel|merch|hoodie|sweater|costume|wear|outfit|hat|tee|jacket|coat returned 0 matches. The page shows no user reviews: 'User's review for' does not occur in the extracted text. Method, from https://gridinsoft.com/website-reputation-checker : 'Positive indicators (claimed profile, verified contacts, stable reputation sources, and high-volume credible reviews) can raise the score when supported by data.' Report page: 'Every website owner can claim their profile for free', 'please submit a review request via portal.gridinsoft.com. There you can claim your profile and add verified company/contact details.', 'We never charge website owners for reviews or reconsideration requests.'
findings.scope: One third-party report. Anyone who looks up the domain on Gridinsoft sees it, and it shows the 'Trusted but Verify' label.
findings.fix: Claim the profile at portal.gridinsoft.com, add the contact details (hello@beastlyfacts.com and the /contact/ page), ask Gridinsoft to drop the 'Clothing' tag, then press 'Flag for Reevaluation'. These are documented inputs. Gridinsoft publishes no weights, so the size of any score change cannot be predicted.

repro.correctedClaim: Gridinsoft scores beastlyfacts.com 63/100, "Trusted but Verify", the fourth of five tiers. The score comes from one automated check: first and last checked September 27, 2026 at 9:14 AM as the page prints it, which is 09:14:06Z in the JSON-LD, so 5:14 owner time. That is 22 days without a recheck as of Oct 19. The report page marks the profile "Unclaimed profile" and links to portal.gridinsoft.com/register. One correction to the finder's evidence: the positive signal "a verified profile linked to this domain" is not a Gridinsoft profile. It is the owner's verified YouTube channel (@beastlyfactsofficial, 19 subscribers). So no claimed profile or verified contacts are counted yet. Gridinsoft's method page names "claimed profile, verified contacts" as positive inputs, and reevaluation is free. The report tags the site "Clothing" in three places: On-page mentions, Digital Footprints and Detection Signatures. Today's live homepage visible text has no clothing terms (0 matches in 1,677 words). The raw HTML does have one: a script-only alt string, "Illustrated bearded dragon wearing sunglasses and a scarf" (index.html:191). It only renders in standalone PWA mode. A classifier reading the source could have picked it up. I could not check whether that string was live on Sep 27. The only negative signal is domain age (5 months, registered May 18, 2026), and claiming the profile cannot change that. A real visitor sees this only by looking the domain up on Gridinsoft, on mobile or desktop. Nothing shows on beastlyfacts.com itself.
repro.evidence:
