Trusted but Verify
`, then "Safe & Secure". The active class is on item 4 of 5. - "Method: automated checks." "First checked September 27, 2026 at 9:14 AM" and "Last checked September 27, 2026 at 9:14 AM". JSON-LD: "dateModified":"2026-09-27T09:14:06Z","datePublished":"2026-09-27T09:14:06Z". `TZ=America/New_York date -d '2026-09-27T09:14:06Z'` gives 2026-09-27 05:14 EDT. - Claim status: `` with tooltip "Every website owner can claim their profile for free and engage with reviewers." - Positive signals block: "a verified profile linked to this domain / YouTube / BeastlyFacts / @beastlyfactsofficial · 19 subscribers". Footprints: "Verified YouTube Channel: Ownership verification confirms that beastlyfacts.com controls the YouTube channel BeastlyFacts (@beastlyfactsofficial) (19 subscribers, 6 videos, 5,268 total views...)". So the "verified profile" is the YouTube channel, not a claimed Gridinsoft profile. - Negative signals: only "a relatively new domain (5 months)". Radar: "Popularity: Estimated low traffic without Tranco or social profile data", "Positive Signals: 2 positive signals". - "On-page mentions: Pets, Guides, Clothing". "Clothing" also appears under Digital Footprints and Detection Signatures. - Owner section: "please submit a review request via portal.gridinsoft.com. There you can claim your profile and add verified company/contact details." and "We never charge website owners for reviews or reconsideration requests." There is a "Flag for Reevaluation" button. - `grep -c "User's review for"` returned 0 in both the HTML and the text. I ran curl on https://gridinsoft.com/website-reputation-checker (200). It says: "Positive indicators (claimed profile, verified contacts, stable reputation sources, and high-volume credible reviews) can raise the score when supported by data." No weights are published. I ran curl on https://beastlyfacts.com/ (200, 230,601 bytes). With scripts, styles and tags stripped, a word-bounded regex for clothing, clothes, shirt(s), apparel, merch, hoodie, sweater, costume, wear(ing), outfit, hat(s), tee(s), jacket, coat(s), fashion, garment, dress and sock(s) found 0 matches in 1,677 words. In the raw HTML, the same regex found one: `img.alt = 'Illustrated bearded dragon wearing sunglasses and a scarf, the BeastlyFacts loading screen';`. That line is repo index.html:191, inside an isStandalone branch. The live /contact/ page decodes Cloudflare's cfemail to hello@beastlyfacts.com (src/pages/Contact.jsx:85). Not checkable: the homepage as of Sep 27. The clone is shallow (80 commits, boundary at 002cfba, Oct 12), and the Wayback API returned 429 and then a connection reset.
repro.fix: The owner can claim the profile at portal.gridinsoft.com, the "Unclaimed profile" link points to /register. Add the verified contacts: hello@beastlyfacts.com and https://beastlyfacts.com/contact/. In the same request, ask Gridinsoft to drop the "Clothing" tag. The site is an animal facts and pet care site; the one clothing-like string in its source is the loading-screen alt text, which describes a mascot illustration. Then press "Flag for Reevaluation". No site code change is needed. Don't edit the alt text to chase the tag: it is accurate, and nothing shows it caused the tag. Claiming adds documented positive inputs, but Gridinsoft publishes no weights. The one negative signal, domain age, only improves with time, so the size of any score change can't be predicted.

impact.correctedClaim:
Gridinsoft scores beastlyfacts.com 63/100, "Trusted but Verify". Its five tiers run from worst to best: Danger Zone, Risky Territory, Caution Advised, Trusted but Verify, Safe & Secure. So this is the second-best tier, not a middling one. The score comes from one automated check on Sep 27 at 5:14 owner time (09:14 UTC), and it has not been rechecked since. The profile is marked unclaimed in the page markup. Gridinsoft's method page names claimed profiles and verified contacts as inputs that can raise a score.

The one existing "verified profile" positive is the owner's YouTube channel (@beastlyfactsofficial), not a claimed Gridinsoft profile. The only negative signal is domain age (5 months). Claiming the profile cannot change that, and it improves on its own over time.

The finding says "nothing on the homepage supports" the "Clothing" tag. That is overstated. The visible homepage text has no clothing words. But the raw HTML of every page has an inline script with the alt text "Illustrated bearded dragon wearing sunglasses and a scarf" (index.html:191), and the footer links "Recommended gear". A crawler reading the raw HTML could plausibly pick up either.

Real visitors never see any of this on the site itself, on mobile or desktop. Only someone who looks the domain up on Gridinsoft sees it. Google does not act on it. Severity is low, not medium.
impact.evidence:
I fetched https://gridinsoft.com/online-virus-scanner/url/beastlyfacts-com with curl (HTTP 200, 182109 bytes).

What the page says:
- Title: "Beastlyfacts.com - Safe or Scam? (63/100 Trust Score)".
- Tier list: "Danger Zone / Risky Territory / Caution Advised / Trusted but Verify / Safe & Secure".
- Check dates: "First checked September 27, 2026 at 9:14 AM" and "Last checked September 27, 2026 at 9:14 AM".
- JSON-LD: "dateModified":"2026-09-27T09:14:06Z". So the displayed 9:14 is UTC, which is 5:14 EDT.
- Raw HTML has aria-label="Unclaimed profile", which confirms the profile is unclaimed.
- Positives: "no major malware/phishing detections", "a verified profile linked to this domain", "YouTube BeastlyFacts @beastlyfactsofficial · 19 subscribers", "business infrastructure", "an active SSL certificate (3 months)".
- The footprint section explains that verified profile: "Verified YouTube Channel: Ownership verification confirms that beastlyfacts.com controls the YouTube channel BeastlyFacts (@beastlyfactsofficial)". So it is the YouTube channel, not a Gridinsoft claim.
- Only negative: "a relatively new domain (5 months)".
- "On-page mentions: Pets, Guides, Clothing".
- The summary paragraph says the site "appears to be generally safe overall".
- "Flag for Reevaluation" links to https://portal.gridinsoft.com/tickets?create=domain-review&domain=Beastlyfacts.com. That is the same portal the owner box points to: "submit a review request via portal.gridinsoft.com. There you can claim your profile and add verified company/contact details", "We never charge website owners".
- The page has no robots meta tag, so it is indexable.

Method page https://gridinsoft.com/website-reputation-checker (HTTP 200), line 79 of the extracted text: "Positive indicators (claimed profile, verified contacts, stable reputation sources, and high-volume credible reviews) can raise the score when supported by data." Line 81 adds "approved profile ownership" as a positive. No weights are published.

Clothing tag:
- I fetched https://beastlyfacts.com/ (HTTP 200) and extracted the visible text: 368 lines, 1677 words.
- A word-boundary grep for clothing|clothes|shirt|t-shirt|apparel|merch|hoodie|sweater|costume|wear|wearing|outfit|hat|tee|jacket|coat|socks|fashion|store|shop|buy returned 0 hits in that visible text.
- Grepping the raw HTML found one hit, at line 95 of the live homepage: img.alt = 'Illustrated bearded dragon wearing sunglasses and a scarf, the BeastlyFacts loading screen'. It sits in a script that only runs in standalone PWA mode. The source is /home/user/beastlyfactss/index.html:191, so it ships on every page.
- A grep for gear terms also found the footer link "Recommended gear" (href="/gear/").

Contact details: hello@beastlyfacts.com appears 15 times across src/ and public/, and https://beastlyfacts.com/contact/ returns 200.

Reach: a web search for "beastlyfacts.com safe or scam" did not return the Gridinsoft beastlyfacts report. It only returned reports on lookalike domains.

What I could not check: https://portal.gridinsoft.com/ is a login page ("Sign in to your Account ... helps website owners verify domains"). Neither it nor a web search showed how ownership is verified (DNS TXT, meta tag or file).
impact.fix:
This is an optional external task, low priority, and it needs no repo change by default.

1. Create an account at portal.gridinsoft.com and open the domain-review ticket. That is the same link the "Flag for Reevaluation" button uses: https://portal.gridinsoft.com/tickets?create=domain-review&domain=Beastlyfacts.com. One ticket covers claiming the profile and asking for a rescore, so these are not separate steps.
2. In the ticket, add hello@beastlyfacts.com and https://beastlyfacts.com/contact/ as verified contacts.
3. Optionally, in the same ticket, note that the site sells no clothing.

Points for the owner to weigh:
- If ownership verification asks for a DNS TXT record, add it in Cloudflare DNS, which leaves the repo untouched. If it needs a meta tag or an uploaded file, that is a repo change and a main deploy, which the owner should decide on first.
- Do not change the splash alt text to shake the "Clothing" tag. The alt text accurately describes the image, and the tag only appears as a neutral detection signature.
- Expect a modest effect at most. The only negative signal, domain age, cannot be fixed by a claim. The site is already in the second-best tier. Gridinsoft publishes no weights.

findings.title: The shared negative is a 5-month-old, low-traffic domain, which only time fixes
findings.claim: Every scanner that explains its score names domain youth as the main negative, and ScamAdviser adds low traffic. The domain was registered on May 18, 2026 and does not appear in the Tranco top-sites list. No site change affects either input.
findings.evidence: RDAP via curl https://rdap.verisign.com/com/v1/domain/beastlyfacts.com : ('registration', '2026-05-18T17:33:24Z'), ('expiration', '2027-05-18T17:33:24Z'), registrar 'Tucows Domains Inc.'. Gridinsoft: 'Negative signals: a relatively new domain (5 months)' and 'This site was registered recently, which limits historical reputation data and long-term trust signals.' ScamAdviser https://www.scamadviser.com/check-website/beastlyfacts.com : 'This website is (very) young.' and 'According to Tranco this site has a low rank'. ScamAdviser body text: 'You can expect this from a small, starting or niche website.' Tranco API: curl https://tranco-list.eu/api/ranks/domain/beastlyfacts.com returned {"ranks": [], "domain": "beastlyfacts.com"}. URLVoid: 'Domain Registration 2026-05-18 | 5 months ago'.
findings.scope: Whole domain, on Gridinsoft, ScamAdviser and URLVoid. Visible to anyone who looks the site up there.
findings.fix: Nothing to change on the site. Ask Gridinsoft (free reevaluation) to recheck once the domain is older. Do not buy traffic to move Tranco.

repro.correctedClaim: The domain was registered on May 18, 2026, 154 days (about 5 months) before today, and it has no Tranco rank. Of the two scanners I could reach that explain their score, both list domain youth as a negative. Gridinsoft (63/100, "Trusted but Verify") lists it as its only negative signal. ScamAdviser (71, "legit") lists three negatives with no ranking: WHOIS privacy (listed first), a low Tranco rank, and a very young domain. So youth is not shown as "the main negative" on ScamAdviser, and the finding leaves out the WHOIS item. URLVoid gives no score and no explanation. It shows 0/36 detections and prints the registration date as a plain fact, not as a negative. WOT shows N/A. I could not check ScamDoc or Scam Detector because both returned 403 to curl and WebFetch. No change to the site can affect domain age or Tranco rank. None of this appears on beastlyfacts.com itself, on mobile or desktop. A visitor sees it only by looking the domain up on one of these scanners, and Google does not see it as structured data or meta.
repro.evidence: RDAP: `curl -sS https://rdap.verisign.com/com/v1/domain/beastlyfacts.com` returned events [('registration','2026-05-18T17:33:24Z'),('expiration','2027-05-18T17:33:24Z'),('last changed','2026-05-22T19:29:26Z')] and registrar fn 'Tucows Domains Inc.'. Running `python3 date(2026,10,19)-date(2026,5,18)` gave 154 days. Tranco: `curl -sS https://tranco-list.eu/api/ranks/domain/beastlyfacts.com` returned {"ranks": [], "domain": "beastlyfacts.com"}. ScamAdviser (https://www.scamadviser.com/check-website/beastlyfacts.com, HTTP 200): - Negatives: under "Negative highlights" the page lists, in this order, "The owner of the website is using a service to hide their identity on WHOIS", "According to Tranco this site has a low rank" and "This website is (very) young." - Score: the raw HTML says "beastlyfacts.com review resulted in a trust score of 71", "we think beastlyfacts.com is legit" and "Last Update: 3 weeks ago". - Body text: "You can expect this from a small, starting or niche website." - Owner option: the page links to https://www.scamadviser.com/claim-your-site, which says you can "register your website for free" and be "listed as verified" with "name, address, email, phone number (after company verification)". Gridinsoft (https://gridinsoft.com/online-virus-scanner/url/beastlyfacts-com, HTTP 200): - Score: the title says "63/100 Trust Score" and the page says "Last checked September 27, 2026". - Negatives: the page says "Negative signals: a relatively new domain (5 months)". That is the only negative listed, and the page also says "Safety Level: 0 negative tags, 1 warning signal". - Young Domain tag: "This site was registered recently, which limits historical reputation data and long-term trust signals." - Owner options: "Flag for Reevaluation", plus "If you own Beastlyfacts.com and want to challenge the trust score, please submit a review request via portal.gridinsoft.com. There you can claim your profile and add verified company/contact details." URLVoid (https://www.urlvoid.com/scan/beastlyfacts.com/, HTTP 200): - Raw HTML: `Domain Registration2026-05-18 | 5 months ago`, with no warning class. - Detections: `0/36`. - The page has no trust score and no list of negatives. Other scanners: - WOT (https://www.mywot.com/scorecard/beastlyfacts.com): "Website security score N/A" and "Unknown website". - ScamDoc and Scam Detector: 403 Cloudflare "Attention Required!" to curl, and 403 to WebFetch, so I could not verify them. - I grepped the repo for scamadviser, gridinsoft, urlvoid and tranco and found no matches, so no site file feeds these inputs.
repro.fix: Make no change to the site. The age signal fixes itself with time. Gridinsoft's free "Flag for Reevaluation" (or claiming the profile at portal.gridinsoft.com) is worth trying once the domain is older. Do not buy traffic to move Tranco. Leave WHOIS privacy on. ScamAdviser's free "Claim your Website" would clear its WHOIS item, but it requires company verification and lists the site with name, address, email and phone. For a solo hobby site that is a poor trade for a slightly better score, so it is optional and the owner's call. Correct the finding's scope: drop URLVoid as a scanner that "names" youth as a negative, and add WHOIS privacy as ScamAdviser's third negative.

impact.correctedClaim:
The core is real. The domain was registered 2026-05-18 and Tranco does not rank it. Domain youth is Gridinsoft's only listed negative. On ScamAdviser it is one of three negatives, listed third. WHOIS privacy is listed first, which the finding leaves out, and low Tranco rank is second. Gridinsoft also flags low traffic ("Estimated low traffic without Tranco or social profile data"), so ScamAdviser is not the only scanner that does. URLVoid explains no score and flags nothing as negative: it shows 0/36 detections and states the registration date as a plain fact.

The resulting scores are favorable:
- ScamAdviser: 71, "Likely Safe", light green, "we think beastlyfacts.com is legit".
- Gridinsoft: 63/100, "generally safe overall".
- URLVoid: 0/36 detections.

This is low severity, not medium. Nobody sees it on the site itself, on mobile or desktop. It is visible only to someone who looks the domain up on these scanners, and Google gets nothing from it. Time fixes the youth signal only. The low-traffic signal moves only with real traffic growth.
impact.evidence:
All checks were run by me on 2026-10-19. Scratch files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-beastlyfactss/c6c3a501-5606-5a8b-b8c9-191dbbf9547e/scratchpad/verify-domainage/.

1. RDAP. curl https://rdap.verisign.com/com/v1/domain/beastlyfacts.com returned ('registration', '2026-05-18T17:33:24Z'), ('expiration', '2027-05-18T17:33:24Z') and registrar 'Tucows Domains Inc.'. Confirmed.

2. Tranco. curl https://tranco-list.eu/api/ranks/domain/beastlyfacts.com returned {"ranks": [], "domain": "beastlyfacts.com"}. Confirmed.

3. ScamAdviser. curl of https://www.scamadviser.com/check-website/beastlyfacts.com returned HTTP 200. Stripped text, lines 55-70:
   - "Why does beastlyfacts.com have a reasonable trust score?"
   - "Negative highlights", then three items in this order: "The owner of the website is using a service to hide their identity on WHOIS", "According to Tranco this site has a low rank", "This website is (very) young."
   - "In summary, we think beastlyfacts.com is legit as we found few indicators which might point to a scam."
   - The page JSON has "ratingScore":71, "trustScoreColor":"light-green" and hero "title":"Likely Safe".
   - Line 102 explains the WHOIS penalty: "websites hiding their identity get a slightly lower score."
   - The finding drops this third negative.
   - The free claim page (https://www.scamadviser.com/claim-your-site) says verified listing needs "company registration documents and ID of at least one of the shareholders".

4. Gridinsoft. https://gridinsoft.com/online-virus-scanner/url/beastlyfacts-com returned HTTP 200.
   - Line 1: "Beastlyfacts.com - Safe or Scam? (63/100 Trust Score)".
   - Lines 152-153: "Negative signals: a relatively new domain (5 months)". This is the only negative listed.
   - Line 128: "Popularity: Estimated low traffic without Tranco or social profile data".
   - Line 184: "appears to be generally safe overall".
   - Lines 321-328: owners can claim the profile at portal.gridinsoft.com, and Gridinsoft says "We never charge website owners for reviews or reconsideration requests".
   - Line 465 has the "Flag for Reevaluation" button.
   - It shows "Last checked September 27, 2026".

5. URLVoid. https://www.urlvoid.com/scan/beastlyfacts.com/ returned HTTP 200. Lines 44-51 show "Detections Counts 0/36" and "Domain Registration 2026-05-18 | 5 months ago". A grep for young, negative, warning, suspicious and risk found no text calling youth a negative, and there is no score explanation.

6. Other scanners. ScamDoc and Scam-Detector returned HTTP 403 and were not checked. The webparanoid.com check URL returned only a domain-for-sale page.

7. Impact context. The site sells Gumroad care packages (src/lib/data/carePackages.js, 9 beastlyfacts.gumroad.com links) and links a Stripe donation (src/lib/data/donationLinks.js), so a cautious buyer could look the site up. They would land on "Likely Safe" or "generally safe". The site already links six social profiles (src/components/layout/Navbar.jsx:349-354). Gridinsoft verified only the YouTube one.
impact.fix:
Nothing changes in the repo. The finding's fix holds, with three additions.

1. Keep WHOIS privacy on. It is ScamAdviser's other negative, but turning it off would publish a solo owner's personal contact details for a "slightly lower score" penalty.
2. Optionally claim the free Gridinsoft profile at portal.gridinsoft.com. This is in addition to the free reevaluation request, and both are worth sending once the domain is older. The Gridinsoft report is dated September 27, so a recheck also refreshes stale data.
3. Skip ScamAdviser business verification unless the owner has company registration documents.

Do not buy traffic. Tranco rank, and Gridinsoft's popularity reading with it, rises only with real visitor growth, not with time alone.

findings.title: Ownership and infrastructure signals are already recognized
findings.claim: The scanners already credit a verified YouTube channel, Google and Zoho domain verification, a valid TLS certificate and a clean security-header setup. Sucuri grades the domain A and the TLS A. Those positives are in place and need no work.
findings.evidence: Gridinsoft: 'Ownership verification confirms that beastlyfacts.com controls the YouTube channel BeastlyFacts (@beastlyfactsofficial) (19 subscribers, 6 videos, 5,268 total views, since 2026, country: US).' Its 'Verified Services' block lists 'Google Verification Domain ownership verified by Google.', 'Zoho' and 'Zoho Mail SPF'. DNS over HTTPS (cloudflare-dns.com) TXT for beastlyfacts.com returned google-site-verification=..., zoho-verification=zb68078241.zmverify.zoho.com, and an SPF record. _dmarc returned "v=DMARC1; p=none; ...". Sucuri API: "domain":{"rating":"A","passed":"1/1"}, "tls":{"rating":"A","passed":"6/6"}, "cert_issuer":"Google Trust Services", "cert_expires":"17 Dec 2026". ScamAdviser: 'The SSL certificate is valid', 'Website speed Very Fast'. Live headers from curl -I https://beastlyfacts.com/ include 'strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload' and 'x-frame-options: DENY'.
findings.scope: Whole domain. Seen on scanner reports, not on the site.

repro.correctedClaim:
Most of the positives are real and I reproduced them today. Gridinsoft credits a verified YouTube channel and Google, Zoho and Zoho Mail SPF verification. The DNS TXT records are in place. The TLS certificate is valid (Google Trust Services WE1, expires Dec 17 2026). Sucuri grades Domain A (1/1) and TLS A (6/6). ScamAdviser says the SSL certificate is valid and the site speed is Very Fast. The live site sends HSTS with preload and X-Frame-Options DENY on all 3 pages I checked: /, /blog/ and /guides/ball-python/.

One part is wrong: no scanner credits a "clean security-header setup". Sucuri rates Security B and Total B, even though the Security checks show passed 6/6. Its recommendations flag headers_minor csp_unsafe_inline and tls_minor no_stapled_ocsp. Gridinsoft and ScamAdviser do not mention headers at all. The headers exist, but the one scanner that grades them marks them down to B for the CSP's 'unsafe-inline'.

The DMARC record (p=none) is monitor-only, so it is not a positive. Gridinsoft's overall score is only 63/100, with one negative signal: "a relatively new domain (5 months)".

None of this is visible to a visitor on mobile or desktop. It shows only on third-party scanner reports.
repro.evidence:
1. Live headers. I ran `curl -sS -I https://beastlyfacts.com/` and it returned HTTP/2 200 with:
   - "strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload"
   - "x-frame-options: DENY"
   - "x-content-type-options: nosniff"
   - a content-security-policy whose script-src includes 'unsafe-inline'.
   /blog/ and /guides/ball-python/ return the same HSTS and XFO lines. In the repo, HSTS is at public/_headers:2 and XFO at public/_headers:4. A grep of public/ for content-security-policy found nothing, so the CSP is set outside the repo files I checked.

2. DNS. I queried cloudflare-dns.com (DNS over HTTPS) for TXT records.
   - beastlyfacts.com returned "google-site-verification=mrdGIPuw34ODwl6G9fswoDqN4NuDEFwqLSSAGsQG9WI", "v=spf1 +a +mx include:beastlyfacts.com.spf.auto.dnssmarthost.net include:zohomail.com a mx include:_spf.mlsend.com ~all" and "zoho-verification=zb68078241.zmverify.zoho.com".
   - _dmarc returned "v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:...@dmarc-reports.cloudflare.net".

3. Sucuri. `curl https://sitecheck.sucuri.net/api/v3/?scan=beastlyfacts.com` (last_scan 2026-10-19T18:00:59Z) returned:
   - "ratings": {"tls": {"passed":"6/6","rating":"A"}, "total": {"rating":"B"}, "domain": {"passed":"1/1","rating":"A"}, "security": {"passed":"6/6","rating":"B"}}
   - "recommendations": {"tls_minor": {"no_stapled_ocsp": {}}, "headers_minor": {"csp_unsafe_inline": {}}}
   - "cert_issuer": "Google Trust Services", "cert_expires": "17 Dec 2026"

4. Gridinsoft. I fetched https://gridinsoft.com/online-virus-scanner/url/beastlyfacts-com and stripped it to text.
   - The title reads "Beastlyfacts.com - Safe or Scam? (63/100 Trust Score)".
   - "Ownership verification confirms that / beastlyfacts.com / controls the YouTube channel BeastlyFacts (@beastlyfactsofficial) (19 subscribers, 6 videos, 5,268 total views, since 2026, country: US)."
   - "Verified Services ... Google Verification / Domain ownership verified by Google. / Zoho / ... / Zoho Mail SPF / Email authentication for Zoho Mail."
   - "Negative signals: a relatively new domain (5 months)".
   - SSL is listed as "WE1 TLSv1.3 · Valid for: 3 months · from September 18, 2026 ... to December 17, 2026".
   - The page has no text about security headers.

5. ScamAdviser. I fetched https://www.scamadviser.com/check-website/beastlyfacts.com (HTTP 200). It shows "The SSL certificate is valid", "Website speed / Very Fast", "SSL certificate valid" and "SSL type / Low - Domain Validated Certificates (DV SSL)". Grepping its text for "header" found no matches.
repro.fix:
None of the confirmed positives needs any work. Only the finding's wording needs correcting:
- Drop the claim that scanners credit a clean security-header setup.
- State that Sucuri rates Security B and Total B because of CSP 'unsafe-inline' (plus missing OCSP stapling), while Domain and TLS are A.
- Do not count DMARC p=none as a strength.

Whether to tighten the CSP is a separate decision for the owner, not part of this finding.

findings.title: Brand search returns a Britannica book, not the site
findings.claim: In five web searches for the brand, its domain and its social handles, 0 of the 48 results were beastlyfacts.com or any of its social profiles. Every query was dominated by the children's book 'Animal FACTopia!: Follow the Trail of 400 Beastly Facts'. No knowledge panel or entity box appeared anywhere. Google, Bing and DuckDuckGo could not be queried directly from this sandbox, so this is one search index, not Google's ranking.
findings.evidence: WebSearch results (the backend engine is not identified): 'beastly facts' gave 9 results, '"beastlyfacts.com"' 10, 'Beastly Facts animal facts and pet care guides' 10, 'beastlyfacts' 10, and '"beastlyfactsofficial" OR "Beastly_Facts"' 9. None of the 48 URLs is on beastlyfacts.com, youtube.com, instagram.com, x.com, pinterest.com, facebook.com or threads.net. Sample titles: 'Animal FACTopia!: Follow the Trail of 400 Beastly Facts' (toppsta.com, shop.merriam-webster.com), and 'Animal factopia! : follow the trail of 400 beastly facts' (catalog.pascolibraries.org, randolph.ocln.org). Direct engines: Google https://www.google.com/search?q=beastly+facts&gbv=1 returned 'Your browser isn't supported anymore.' DuckDuckGo html and lite returned 'Unfortunately, bots use DuckDuckGo too. Please complete the following challenge'. Bing returned decoy results: site:beastlyfacts.com gave 10 chase.com results, and 'beastlyfacts' gave GroupMe Reddit threads. WebFetch of bing.com/search?q=beastly+facts listed only Microsoft pages and 'There is no entity box for Beastly Facts and no social profile listings.'
findings.scope: Brand and navigational searches, on desktop and mobile. This is the search people run when they check whether the site is legitimate.
findings.fix: From a desktop, open Search Console Performance and filter queries containing 'beastly' to read the real Google position for the brand query. Then run the same query by hand in Bing and DuckDuckGo.

repro.correctedClaim: The tally is real but only for the WebSearch tool's backend, which is not identified. Across the same five queries, 0 of 48 results were beastlyfacts.com or its social profiles, and the Animal FACTopia book filled the lists. That backend does have the site indexed. It just ranks the book higher for the bare brand words. The headline "brand search returns a Britannica book, not the site" does not hold beyond that one tool. Brave Search, the only independent consumer engine that returned real results here, ranks https://beastlyfacts.com/ #1 for both "beastly facts" and "beastlyfacts", with the site's own Instagram (instagram.com/beastly.facts) at #3. For "beastlyfacts.com" in quotes, 13 of 16 Brave results are on the domain. No engine showed a knowledge panel, which is normal for a small site. Google's ranking is still unknown: from this sandbox it returns a JavaScript wall, Bing returns decoy results and DuckDuckGo returns a bot challenge. This is about off-site search results, not anything on the site, so no visitor sees a problem on the page on mobile or desktop. Nothing seen here shows that real brand searchers fail to find the site.
repro.evidence:
1) WebSearch tool, rerun myself. "beastly facts" gave 9 results, "\"beastlyfacts.com\"" 10, "Beastly Facts animal facts and pet care guides" 10, "beastlyfacts" 10 and "\"beastlyfactsofficial\" OR \"Beastly_Facts\"" 9. That is 48 in total, and none is on beastlyfacts.com, instagram, youtube, x, pinterest, facebook or threads. Every list is dominated by 'Animal FACTopia!: Follow the Trail of 400 Beastly Facts' (toppsta.com, shop.merriam-webster.com, catalog.pascolibraries.org/Record/487000, randolph.ocln.org/Record/469552). So the finder's count reproduces exactly.
2) The same tool has the site indexed. WebSearch "beastly facts animal facts" with allowed_domains=[beastlyfacts.com] returned 10 site pages, starting with {"title":"Beastly Facts","url":"https://beastlyfacts.com/"}, then /facts/ and /about/. A second domain-filtered query, "bearded dragon care guide cost", also returned 10 beastlyfacts.com pages.
3) Brave Search via WebFetch of https://search.brave.com/search?q=beastly+facts:
 - #1 "Beastly Facts | Animal Facts and Pet Care Guides": https://beastlyfacts.com/
 - #2 the Merriam-Webster shop page for the book
 - #3 "Beastly Facts": https://www.instagram.com/beastly.facts/
 - beastlyfacts.com pages also appear at #4 /encyclopedia/, #6 /quiz/personality/ and #7 /contact/
 - "Knowledge panel / entity box: None"
4) Brave via WebFetch of ?q=beastlyfacts gave the same order: beastlyfacts.com #1, Instagram beastly.facts #3.
5) Brave via WebFetch of ?q=%22beastlyfacts.com%22: "Count on beastlyfacts.com: 13 (results 1 to 13, out of 16 organic results)", plus instagram.com/beastly.facts/ at #15.
6) The Instagram result is the site's own account: src/App.jsx:202 lists "https://www.instagram.com/beastly.facts" in sameAs, and src/pages/Contact.jsx:103 links it. Brave's #11 'Beast Facts Hub - YouTube' (channel UCYbt77cn_Y_9svANlX4o0jQ) is NOT the site's channel, which is @BeastlyFactsOfficial (src/App.jsx:203, src/lib/data/author.js:35).
7) Direct engines are unusable from here:
 - Google: curl of google.com/search?q=beastly+facts&gbv=1 returned HTTP 200, 92729 bytes, a JavaScript redirect page ("Please click here if you are not redirected within a few seconds") with 0 occurrences of beastlyfacts.com. WebFetch of Google got "If you're having trouble accessing Google Search, please click here".
 - Bing (all decoys): curl of bing.com/search?q=beastly+facts listed only Carnival CCL stock sites; site:beastlyfacts.com listed openai.com/ChatGPT pages; WebFetch of the same query listed Indiana Medicaid portals.
 - DuckDuckGo: curl to html.duckduckgo.com reset the connection. WebFetch got "Unfortunately, bots use DuckDuckGo too... Select all squares containing a duck".
 - Others: curl to search.brave.com returned 429, mojeek and ecosia 403, yahoo 500, startpage 303.
Not checked: Google's real ranking (impossible from this sandbox), and mobile result layouts.
repro.fix: The site needs no change on this evidence. Drop the framing that the brand query is lost to the book. The one consumer engine that returned real results (Brave) puts beastlyfacts.com first and the Instagram third, and the WebSearch tool's ordering is one unidentified index. As a low-priority check from a desktop, the owner can open Google Search Console, go to Performance, filter queries containing "beastly", and read the average position for "beastly facts" and "beastlyfacts". The owner can also type the same two queries into Google and Bing by hand. Revisit this only if Google shows the site below the FACTopia book listings.

impact.correctedClaim: In the Claude WebSearch tool's index (engine not identified), 7 queries returned 66 results, and none of them was on beastlyfacts.com or any of its four social profiles. The queries were the five brand and handle queries plus "site:beastlyfacts.com" and a content query. Most results were Animal FACTopia!, a Britannica Books children's book. Because even "site:beastlyfacts.com" returned no page from the domain, this index appears not to hold the site at all. It shows a gap in this index's coverage. It is not evidence of where Google ranks the site for its brand, and it is not evidence that the book outranks the site there. The repo's own Google Search Console export shows Google does index the site and serves it for 165 queries, but none of those 165 queries contains "beastl". So, at least as of 2026-08-10, almost nobody was searching the brand on Google. The domain was registered on 2026-05-18, so it is five months old, and having no knowledge panel at that age is normal. Who sees it: only a person who types the brand into a search engine, on both desktop and mobile. The GSC export suggests that group is close to zero right now. Severity is low, not medium.
impact.evidence:
1. I reproduced the core result with WebSearch. "beastly facts" gave 9 results, "beastlyfacts.com" 10, "Beastly Facts animal facts and pet care guides" 9 (the finding says 10), "beastlyfacts" 10, and "\"beastlyfactsofficial\" OR \"Beastly_Facts\"" 9. That is 47 results, with 0 on beastlyfacts.com, youtube, pinterest, instagram or x. Titles included "Animal FACTopia!: Follow the Trail of 400 Beastly Facts" (toppsta.com, shop.merriam-webster.com, catalog.pascolibraries.org, randolph.ocln.org). Two more queries test whether the domain is in this index at all. "site:beastlyfacts.com" returned 10 results, 0 of them on the domain, and the tool's summary said "The search didn't return any pages from beastlyfacts.com. The `site:` operator didn't filter the results." A content query, "\"Beastly Facts\" axolotl care guide", returned 9 results, 0 on the domain. Total: 0 of 66.

2. Google does index the site. tools/keyword-finder/gsc-keyword-analysis.md:3-5 says the export is "real Google Search Console data". tools/keyword-finder/gsc-keywords-2026-08-10.csv has 166 lines, which is 165 query rows plus a header. Its positions run from 5.00 ("parakeet vs cockatiel", line 2) to 99.00 (line 166). `grep -i -n "beastl"` on that CSV printed only line 72, where "beastl" appears in the beastlyfacts.com URL column, not the query ("platypus mammal"). That is 0 of 165 query rows containing "beastl". The analysis doc at line 10 notes "0 clicks ... expected for ... a young site".

3. The site is young. `curl https://rdap.verisign.com/com/v1/domain/beastlyfacts.com` returned "registration 2026-05-18T17:33:24Z".

4. On-site brand signals are in place. `curl -sS https://beastlyfacts.com/` gave "<title>Beastly Facts | Animal Facts and Pet Care Guides</title>", Organization "name":"Beastly Facts", and "sameAs":["https://www.pinterest.com/BeastlyFacts","https://x.com/beastly_facts","https://www.instagram.com/beastly.facts","https://www.youtube.com/@BeastlyFactsOfficial"]. robots.txt has "Allow: /" with only /cdn-cgi/ disallowed. One small inconsistency: the WebSite schema in src/App.jsx:181 uses "name": "BeastlyFacts" (no space) while Organization uses "Beastly Facts", and neither has an alternateName. Only Google sees this (structured data).

5. The social profiles exist. curl gave HTTP 200 for the YouTube @BeastlyFactsOfficial, Pinterest BeastlyFacts and x.com/beastly_facts URLs, and 429 for Instagram (rate-limited, so I could not confirm it).

6. I could not reach the direct engines. Bing via curl with a browser user agent returned 200, but "beastlyfacts.com" appeared 0 times on the page, and the result links decode to support.google.com/earth and reddit r/askgis pages. That is decoy output, as the finding said. DuckDuckGo html returned "curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer". I could not check Google's live brand ranking.
impact.fix: Lower the severity to low and retitle the finding to "Third-party search index has no beastlyfacts.com pages". The current title asserts a brand-ranking problem that no Google evidence supports. The proposed diagnostic is right and proportionate as an owner-decision step, with one point to add. The repo's 2026-08-10 GSC export already shows 0 brand queries out of 165, so the owner only needs a fresh date range: GSC Performance, filter "Query contains beastly", last 3 months. A by-hand check in Google, Bing and DuckDuckGo from the desktop still applies. Do not make content or code changes on the strength of this evidence. One optional, cheap step Google would see: make the WebSite schema name in src/App.jsx:181 match the Organization name "Beastly Facts", and add "alternateName": "BeastlyFacts". Google's site-name feature reads that field. It is a one-line edit and stays within the owner's rules.

findings.title: ScamAdviser 71 'Likely Safe': the only negative the owner controls is WHOIS privacy
findings.claim: ScamAdviser scores the site 71, in its 'Likely Safe' band (61 to 80), and concludes 'we think beastlyfacts.com is legit'. Its three negatives are WHOIS privacy, a low Tranco rank and a young domain. Only WHOIS privacy is in the owner's hands, and removing it would publish the owner's personal details. The 'verified' badge needs company registration papers, and the site names no business entity.
findings.evidence: https://www.scamadviser.com/check-website/beastlyfacts.com : hero 'Likely Safe', 'Last Update: 3 weeks ago' (no exact date shown). Embedded page JSON: "ratingScore":71. FAQ JSON-LD: 'beastlyfacts.com review resulted in a trust score of 71. This rating has been given by an algorithm based on public sources such as WHOIS, the IP address of the server, the location of the company and if the website has been reported on spam and phishing lists.' Negatives: 'The owner of the website is using a service to hide their identity on WHOIS', 'According to Tranco this site has a low rank', 'This website is (very) young.' Body text: 'As a result, websites hiding their identity get a slightly lower score.' FAQ https://www.scamadviser.com/faq : '61 to 80 - Likely Safe' and '81 to 100 - Very Likely Safe: ... They usually belong to recognized organizations or established companies.' Claim page https://www.scamadviser.com/claim-your-site : 'Get listed as verified (company registration documents and ID of at least one of the shareholders is required).' Repo: grep -rln '\bLLC\b' src/pages returned nothing, and src/pages has only Privacy.jsx and Terms.jsx as legal pages. ScamAdviser also tags the site 'Subscriptions - General Services', which does not describe it.
findings.scope: One third-party report, visible to anyone who checks the site on ScamAdviser or through its app.
findings.fix: Keep WHOIS privacy. ScamAdviser itself says it costs only 'a slightly lower score', and the alternative publishes a solo owner's personal details. Pursue the verified badge only if a business entity is ever formed.

findings.title: No reviews on any review platform
findings.claim: There is no Trustpilot page for the domain, and Gridinsoft and Norton show zero user reviews. Both Gridinsoft and ScamAdviser name reviews as a scoring input, so this input currently contributes nothing.
findings.evidence: WebFetch https://www.trustpilot.com/review/beastlyfacts.com and https://www.trustpilot.com/review/www.beastlyfacts.com both returned 'HTTP 404 Not Found'. A control fetch of https://www.trustpilot.com/review/www.chewy.com through the same tool returned 'TrustScore of 3.3 and 13,345 reviews', so the 404 means no profile exists, not that the tool was blocked. Plain curl got an AWS WAF 'Verifying Connection' page (HTTP 403). Norton API: "communityRating":0.0,"reviewCount":0. Gridinsoft report: no 'User's review for' entries. Method text: Gridinsoft (https://gridinsoft.com/website-reputation-checker) lists 'public review feedback' and 'high-volume credible reviews'. ScamAdviser (https://www.scamadviser.com/about-scamadviser) lists 'ratings on review sites'.
findings.scope: Domain-level reputation on Gridinsoft, ScamAdviser and Norton.
findings.fix: Owner decides whether to open a free Trustpilot business profile and link it from /contact/. Never solicit or reward reviews.

findings.title: Contact email reaches scanners as '[email protected]'
findings.claim: The source code renders hello@beastlyfacts.com on /contact/ and /about/. Cloudflare's email obfuscation rewrites it in the served HTML, so any fetcher that does not run JavaScript sees '[email protected]' and no address. ScamAdviser names 'the availability of contact details on the website' as a scoring input. Visitors with JavaScript see the address normally, on mobile and desktop. Whether ScamAdviser's crawler runs JavaScript is not documented.
findings.evidence: Source: src/pages/Contact.jsx:85 href="mailto:hello@beastlyfacts.com" and src/pages/Contact.jsx:97 renders hello@beastlyfacts.com. Live HTML from curl https://beastlyfacts.com/contact/ : and [email protected], plus the injected
findings.scope: /contact/ and /about/ as seen by non-JavaScript fetchers: scanners and some crawlers.
findings.fix: In the Cloudflare dashboard, turn off Scrape Shield Email Address Obfuscation, or add a Configuration Rule that disables it for /contact/ and /about/, so the plain address is in the HTML.

findings.title: Site name differs between WebSite and Organization schema, and sameAs omits two linked profiles
findings.claim: The WebSite structured data, the input Google says it uses for the site name, says 'BeastlyFacts'. The Organization schema, the <title> and og:site_name all say 'Beastly Facts'. The Organization sameAs lists 4 social profiles, but the site visibly links 6: Facebook and Threads are missing. Google only, not visible to visitors. On a brand search crowded by a similarly named book, consistent entity signals are the part the owner controls.
findings.evidence: src/App.jsx:181 "name": "BeastlyFacts" (WebSite). src/App.jsx:196 "name": "Beastly Facts" (Organization). src/App.jsx:199-204 sameAs lists only pinterest, x, instagram and youtube. src/components/shared/SocialIcons.jsx:47-48 add Facebook (profile.php?id=61590767090597) and Threads (@Beastly.Facts). The live homepage confirms the JSON-LD names, plus <title>Beastly Facts | Animal Facts and Pet Care Guides and og:site_name "Beastly Facts". Google https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/site-names : 'To indicate your site name preference, add WebSite structured data to your home page.', 'Providing an alternative name using the alternateName property allows Google to consider other options', and 'Use your site name consistently across your home page.'
findings.scope: Site-wide structured data, injected from App.jsx on every page. Google only.
findings.fix: In src/App.jsx set the WebSite name to "Beastly Facts" with "alternateName": "BeastlyFacts", and add the Facebook and Threads URLs from SocialIcons.jsx to the Organization sameAs.

findings.title: Sucuri grades the site B overall over two hardening notes
findings.claim: Sucuri's overall rating is B, not A, because of two minor recommendations: a CSP that allows 'unsafe-inline', and no OCSP stapling. Neither is a detection. The CSP is set by a Cloudflare Transform Rule, not by the repo. One of the four inline scripts on the homepage is injected by Cloudflare per request, so a hash-only CSP cannot cover it.
findings.evidence: Sucuri API (scan run 2026-10-19T18:00:59Z, 14:00, triggered by this audit's fetch): "recommendations":{"headers_minor":{"csp_unsafe_inline":{}},"tls_minor":{"no_stapled_ocsp":{}}}, "ratings":{"total":{"rating":"B"},...}. Live header: content-security-policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' ... style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' .... .gitignore:87-88: 'Cloudflare's Content-Security-Policy (set via a Transform Rule on the zone, not read from anything here).' grep for unsafe-inline in the repo outside node_modules returned no matches. The live homepage has 4 inline <script> blocks: theme toggle (127 chars), gtag (841), PWA standalone check (595), and Cloudflare's challenge injector beginning '(function(){function c(){var b=a.contentDocument' (921).
findings.scope: Header-level, whole site. Visible only on Sucuri, not to visitors.
findings.fix: Optional: move the three site-owned inline scripts into /assets, then replace 'unsafe-inline' in the Transform Rule's script-src with a per-request nonce, or accept the B as a hardening note.

findings.title: DNSSEC is switched on at Cloudflare but the DS record was never published
findings.claim: Cloudflare is publishing DNSSEC keys for the zone, but the .com registry has no DS record, so resolvers treat the domain as unsigned. Gridinsoft displays 'DNSSEC: UNSIGNED'. No scanner documents DNSSEC as a weighted input.
findings.evidence: DNS over HTTPS (cloudflare-dns.com): the DNSKEY query returned 2 keys ('256 3 13 oJMRES...' and '257 3 13 mdsswU...'). The DS query returned no answer, and AD=False on every query. RDAP: secureDNS {'delegationSigned': False}. Gridinsoft Domain Information: 'Domain Status Ok DNSSEC: UNSIGNED'.
findings.scope: Domain-level DNS. Invisible to visitors.
findings.fix: Copy the DS record from Cloudflare DNS > Settings > DNSSEC into the DNSSEC panel at the domain's registrar (Tucows Domains Inc. is the registrar of record).

findings.title: The Wayback Machine reports no captures of the site
findings.claim: The Internet Archive's availability API returns no snapshot for beastlyfacts.com, for the root URL as of Oct 19, or for www.beastlyfacts.com. robots.txt does not block archive crawlers. The CDX index could not be queried from this sandbox, so the earliest capture date is unconfirmed. No scanner documents archive history as an input. Gridinsoft lists 'historic behavior' without defining it.
findings.evidence: curl http://archive.org/wayback/available?url=beastlyfacts.com returned {"url": "beastlyfacts.com", "archived_snapshots": {}}. ...?url=beastlyfacts.com/&timestamp=20261019 returned {"url": "beastlyfacts.com/", "archived_snapshots": {}, "timestamp": "20261019"}. ...?url=www.beastlyfacts.com returned {"archived_snapshots": {}}. CDX attempts: over https 'curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' (3 tries); over http 'Blocked by egress policy' (403); WebFetch 'Claude Code is unable to fetch from web.archive.org'. public/robots.txt:1-6 has only 'User-agent: *', 'Allow: /', 'Disallow: /cdn-cgi/' and the Sitemap line. A curl with the archive.org_bot user agent got HTTP 200 on the homepage.
findings.scope: Domain history as seen by anyone checking the Wayback Machine.
findings.fix: From a desktop, submit the homepage, /about/ and /contact/ to https://web.archive.org/save so a dated public record begins.

domain-infra.notCheckable: Direct TLS inspection with openssl s_client is not possible here. The sandbox's egress proxy presents its own certificate (issuer \"Anthropic Egress Gateway SDS Issuing CA\"), so I used Certificate Transparency (Cert Spotter API) and the SSL Labs API for the real chain and grade instead. RDAP does not expose the Tucows reseller's identity or whether auto-renew is on, so I could not confirm the renewal setting. I could not see the Cloudflare DMARC aggregate reports, so I cannot say whether tightening to p=quarantine would break any current sender. I also could not confirm whether MailerLite or the SiteGround-linked include are still in use: the repo never mentions them, but the owner may send through them outside the codebase. I probed the beehiiv sending-domain alignment with the common DKIM selectors (s1, s2, bh, k1, mail, selector1, on the apex and the newsletter subdomain) and found none, so I cannot say whether beehiiv mail aligns to beastlyfacts.com. I wanted to check whether the Cloudflare email rewrite triggers a React hydration mismatch, since src/main.jsx:86 uses hydrateRoot and Terms.jsx:62 embeds the address mid-sentence. I tried to mirror the live page to localhost for a headless browser check, but the sandbox policy refused it, so that impact is unverified. I did not test whether the security@beastlyfacts.com mailbox actually accepts mail. crt.sh returned 502, so CT data comes from Cert Spotter only (31 issuances, first page).

findings.title: Cloudflare Email Obfuscation hides the contact address in the served HTML of every trust page
findings.claim: The zone's Email Address Obfuscation setting rewrites hello@beastlyfacts.com in the prerendered HTML to the text "[email protected]" and the mailto link to /cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#..., and that endpoint returns 404. The literal address appears 0 times in the served HTML of all 5 pages that carry it. Visitors with JavaScript see the decoded address after Cloudflare's decoder runs, on mobile and desktop alike. Visitors without JS, reader views, link previews, trust scanners and any crawler that reads raw HTML without rendering see "[email protected]", and a no-JS click on "Email Me" lands on a 404. Googlebot renders JS, so Google most likely sees the decoded address, but the raw HTML it fetches first does not contain it.
findings.evidence: Contact page raw HTML text: "Email Me [email protected] I read every message." About: "[email protected] . I read everything, and I answer." Decoding the data-cfemail values with Cloudflare's XOR scheme gives hello@beastlyfacts.com on about (1), contact (1), privacy (2), terms (3), how-guides-are-made (1). Command: grep -c 'hello@beastlyfacts.com' on the 5 fetched pages returned 0 for each. Each page loads /cdn-cgi/scripts/5c5dd728/cloudflare-static/email-decode.min.js. curl -D - https://beastlyfacts.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection returned HTTP/2 404. Source has the plain address: src/pages/Contact.jsx:85 (href="mailto:hello@beastlyfacts.com") and :97, src/pages/About.jsx:192, src/pages/Terms.jsx:62,64,88, src/pages/Privacy.jsx:106,119, src/pages/HowGuidesAreMade.jsx:328. public/robots.txt:3-4 already notes "Cloudflare-injected email obfuscation endpoint - 404s when crawled directly" and disallows /cdn-cgi/.
findings.scope: 5 of 5 pages that publish the address: /about/, /contact/, /privacy/, /terms/, /how-guides-are-made/. The 41-page sitemap sample and the home page carry no obfuscated email (0 of 42).
findings.fix: In Cloudflare, turn off Scrape Shield > Email Address Obfuscation, or add a Configuration Rule that disables it for the zone, so the prerendered address ships as written.

findings.title: Published contact email is on the domain and backed by working mail records
findings.claim: Every page that publishes a contact address uses hello@beastlyfacts.com, an address on the site's own domain rather than a free webmail account. The domain has live MX records for Zoho Mail, a published Zoho DKIM key, and a DMARC record with aggregate reporting. A visitor emailing the address reaches a real, authenticated mailbox on the same domain as the site, which matches the About and Contact pages. Visible to visitors on all devices, subject to the obfuscation finding above.
findings.evidence: DoH MX: "10 mx.zoho.com.", "20 mx2.zoho.com.", "50 mx3.zoho.com.". TXT: "zoho-verification=zb68078241.zmverify.zoho.com". zmail._domainkey.beastlyfacts.com TXT: "v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=MIGfMA0...". Decoded addresses on all 5 pages = hello@beastlyfacts.com. Source: src/pages/Contact.jsx:85, src/components/shared/ContactForm.jsx:161. public/.well-known/security.txt:1 adds security@beastlyfacts.com on the same domain.
findings.scope: Site-wide contact identity (About, Contact, Privacy, Terms, How Guides Are Made, contact form fallback)

findings.title: DMARC is monitor-only (p=none), so the published address can be spoofed
findings.claim: The DMARC policy is p=none. Receiving mail servers are told to deliver mail that fails SPF and DKIM alignment for beastlyfacts.com. Anyone can send mail as hello@beastlyfacts.com, the address the Terms page tells buyers to use for refunds, and receivers are not asked to quarantine or reject it. Reports already flow to Cloudflare DMARC Management, so the data needed to tighten the policy is being collected. Not visible on the site; affects inbox trust for subscribers and buyers.
findings.evidence: DoH _dmarc.beastlyfacts.com TXT: "v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:9a0ac9d0518d4745a1297c60d31a4ac7@dmarc-reports.cloudflare.net". src/pages/Terms.jsx:62: "If you would like to request a refund, email hello@beastlyfacts.com".
findings.scope: All mail using the beastlyfacts.com From domain
findings.fix: Check the Cloudflare DMARC Management reports to confirm Zoho (DKIM selector zmail) and any newsletter sender pass aligned. Then move the record to p=quarantine, and to p=reject after a clean month.

findings.title: Young domain on a 1-year term with no registrar transfer lock
findings.claim: The domain was registered 154 days ago for a single year, so it expires in 211 days. Its registry status is only "active": it has no clientTransferProhibited lock. Automated trust scanners score young domains with short registration terms as riskier. Without a transfer lock, a compromised registrar account or social engineering could move the domain with fewer checks. Registrant data is privacy-redacted through Tucows' tiered-access service (individual, VA, US), which is normal and fine. Not visible to visitors or Google directly; read by trust scanners and WHOIS/RDAP lookups.
findings.evidence: curl https://rdap.verisign.com/com/v1/domain/beastlyfacts.com: "status": ["active"]; registration "2026-05-18T17:33:24Z"; expiration "2027-05-18T17:33:24Z"; registrar "Tucows Domains Inc." (IANA 69). Registrar RDAP https://opensrs.rdap.tucows.com/domain/BEASTLYFACTS.COM: status ['active'], registrant vcard fn "", adr cc US region VA, contact-uri https://tieredaccess.com/contact/133cd36b-.... Python date math: age 154 days, 211 days to expiry.
findings.scope: Domain-wide
findings.fix: At the registrar (Tucows/OpenSRS reseller), turn on the transfer lock and extend the registration to several years with auto-renew on.

findings.title: DNSSEC is half-configured: zone is signed but no DS record at .com
findings.claim: Cloudflare is signing the zone and serving DNSKEY and RRSIG records, but no DS record was published at the .com parent. The chain of trust is broken and no resolver validates the answers. The signing gives no protection against DNS spoofing until the DS record is added. Invisible to visitors and Google; DNS and security scanners report it.
findings.evidence: DoH DNSKEY: "257 3 13 mdsswUyr3DPW..." and "256 3 13 oJMRESz5...". A query with do=1 returns an RRSIG "A 13 2 300 ... 34505 beastlyfacts.com." but "AD":false on both cloudflare-dns.com and dns.google. DS query at dns.google returns only an NSEC3 denial from the .com zone (no DS). Verisign RDAP: "secureDNS": {"delegationSigned": false}. Tucows RDAP: {'zoneSigned': False, 'delegationSigned': False}.
findings.scope: Domain-wide (all hostnames)
findings.fix: Copy the DS record from Cloudflare (DNS > Settings > DNSSEC) into the registrar's DNSSEC panel, then confirm the AD flag turns true.

findings.title: TLS and security headers grade A+ on every page type checked
findings.claim: All four Cloudflare edge IPs score A+ on SSL Labs with only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 enabled. Certificates are Cloudflare Universal SSL from Google Trust Services and Let's Encrypt, renewed automatically: the newest apex and wildcard cert was issued 2026-10-06 and is valid to 2027-01-04. HTML pages carry HSTS (1 year, includeSubDomains, preload), X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP, CORP, and a CSP with object-src 'none', base-uri 'none', form-action 'self' and upgrade-insecure-requests. http:// goes to https:// on the apex with a single 301. Visible to every visitor as a clean padlock on mobile and desktop.
findings.evidence: SSL Labs API (analyze?host=beastlyfacts.com, status READY): 172.67.165.33, 104.21.11.39, 2606:4700:3033::6815:b27, 2606:4700:3033::ac43:a521 all "grade A+", protocols ['TLS 1.2','TLS 1.3']; served leaf CN=beastlyfacts.com issued by CN=WR1, O=Google Trust Services. Cert Spotter CT: 31 issuances, latest "2026-10-06T02:41:25Z -> 2027-01-04T01:37:25Z ... WE1 | *.beastlyfacts.com,beastlyfacts.com". curl -sSI on /, /guides/bearded-dragon/, /blog/bearded-dragon-cost-guide/, /contact/ each returned "strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload", "x-content-type-options: nosniff", "x-frame-options: DENY", "referrer-policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin", "permissions-policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=(), usb=()" and a content-security-policy. Source: public/_headers:1-6, 15-16. http://beastlyfacts.com/ gave "1 redirects, final 200 https://beastlyfacts.com/".
findings.scope: Site-wide (4 of 4 page types checked: home, guide hub, article, contact)

findings.title: No mixed content and only one third-party script on first paint
findings.claim: The served HTML references no http:// resources, loads no external stylesheets or iframes, and self-hosts its fonts. The only third-party script tag at first paint is Cloudflare's Web Analytics beacon (defer), which Cloudflare injects. GA4 (googletagmanager.com) and Ahrefs analytics are added after the load event via requestIdleCallback, and AdSense is commented out. Visitors on every device get a page that does not wait on third-party hosts to render.
findings.evidence: Script over 41 pages (every 33rd sitemap URL, 41 of 41 returned 200 with content) plus /, /guides/bearded-dragon/, /blog/bearded-dragon-cost-guide/: "http:// resource refs: {}", "external script hosts (pages): {'static.cloudflareinsights.com': 41}", "external stylesheet hosts: {}", "iframe hosts: {}". The home page's only external <script src> is 'https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js' (defer). The inline snippet injects 'https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-L0T3V8PPP7' and 'https://analytics.ahrefs.com/analytics.js' inside window.addEventListener('load') with requestIdleCallback. Fonts are preloaded from /fonts/*.woff2. index.html:17-25 keeps the AdSense loader commented out. The beacon is not in the repo (grep for cloudflareinsights in index.html, src, public returned nothing), so Cloudflare injects it.
findings.scope: Site-wide (44 pages checked)

findings.title: SPF record is near the lookup limit and authorizes senders the site never mentions
findings.claim: The SPF record needs 9 of the 10 DNS lookups RFC 7208 allows. Two more includes would cause a permerror that breaks SPF for all mail. It lists a and mx twice, and +a authorizes the apex A records, which are Cloudflare's shared proxy IPs. It also includes dnssmarthost.net (resolving to _spf.mailspamprotection.com, which a third-party SPF guide ties to SiteGround hosting) and MailerLite (_spf.mlsend.com, with a litesrv DKIM CNAME). No file in the repo mentions SiteGround, dnssmarthost or MailerLite, and the newsletter subdomain points at beehiiv. Not visible to visitors.
findings.evidence: TXT: "v=spf1 +a +mx include:beastlyfacts.com.spf.auto.dnssmarthost.net include:zohomail.com a mx include:_spf.mlsend.com ~all". Recursive count script (scratchpad/domain-infra/scripts/spfcount.py) output: "TOTAL DNS-querying SPF terms: 9 of RFC 7208 limit 10". beastlyfacts.com.spf.auto.dnssmarthost.net -> "v=spf1 include:_spf.mailspamprotection.com ~all". A records: 104.21.11.39, 172.67.165.33 (Cloudflare). newsletter.beastlyfacts.com CNAME "cname.beehiiv.com.". Repo grep counts: mailerlite 0, mlsend 0, siteground 0, dnssmarthost 0 files. WebSearch: autospf.com SiteGround guide shows "include:_spf.mailspamprotection.com" as an example.
findings.scope: All outbound mail for the domain
findings.fix: Once the owner confirms which services still send as beastlyfacts.com, rewrite SPF to only those, e.g. "v=spf1 include:zohomail.com include:_spf.mlsend.com ~all" if MailerLite is still live, dropping +a, +mx, the duplicate a mx and the dnssmarthost include.

findings.title: CSP allows inline script, lives outside the repo, and contradicts X-Frame-Options
findings.claim: The live CSP is set by a Cloudflare zone Transform Rule, not by public/_headers, so it cannot be diffed or reviewed with the code. Its script-src includes 'unsafe-inline', which removes most of its value against injected script. Its frame-ancestors 'self' allows same-origin framing while _headers sends X-Frame-Options: DENY. Modern browsers obey frame-ancestors, so DENY is silently overridden. The same rule also lands on Worker responses such as /feed.xml, which get none of the _headers protections (no HSTS, no nosniff). Visible only to security scanners, not to visitors or Google.
findings.evidence: Live header on /, /guides/bearded-dragon/, /blog/bearded-dragon-cost-guide/: "content-security-policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://www.googletagmanager.com ... frame-ancestors 'self'; ...". public/_headers:1-22 contains no Content-Security-Policy, and :4 sets "X-Frame-Options: DENY". docs/STOREFRONT.md:292-294: "The CSP is not in this repo. It is set as a Transform Rule on the Cloudflare zone; cloudflare-csp.txt is a local reference copy and is gitignored" (.gitignore:89). /feed.xml headers: content-security-policy present, no strict-transport-security or x-content-type-options. The home page carries a per-request Cloudflare inline script ("window.__CF$cv$params={r:'a4d1b084d882e9bf',...}"), so hashes alone cannot replace 'unsafe-inline' while JS Detections is on.
findings.scope: Site-wide header policy
findings.fix: Change frame-ancestors to 'none' in the Transform Rule to match X-Frame-Options DENY, and commit the CSP text to docs so it is versioned with the code.

findings.title: HSTS header says preload, but the domain is not on any preload list
findings.claim: Every HTML response sends the preload token, and hstspreload.org reports the domain as preloadable with no errors or warnings, but it was never submitted. A first-ever visit typed as http:// is still unprotected until the 301 arrives. Not visible to visitors.
findings.evidence: curl https://hstspreload.org/api/v2/status?domain=beastlyfacts.com: "status": "unknown". /api/v2/preloadable: {"errors": [], "warnings": []}. SSL Labs hstsPreloads: [('Chrome','absent'), ('Edge','absent'), ('Firefox','absent'), ('IE','absent')]. public/_headers:2 "Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload". CT shows valid certs for every subdomain seen (www, newsletter, elinkddf.newsletter, pins).
findings.scope: Domain and all subdomains
findings.fix: Submit beastlyfacts.com at hstspreload.org, after the owner accepts that includeSubDomains preload is slow to undo and forces HTTPS on every future subdomain; otherwise drop the preload token.

findings.title: www and http variants take 2 to 3 redirect hops
findings.claim: http://www goes to https://www and then to the https apex: 2 hops, where 1 would do. A www URL without its trailing slash takes 3 hops. Each hop adds latency for visitors on old or typed links (worst on mobile networks) and dilutes link signals Google follows. The https://www to apex hop alone is a clean single 301.
findings.evidence: curl -L -w: "http://www.beastlyfacts.com/ -> 2 redirects, final 200 https://beastlyfacts.com/" (301 to https://www.beastlyfacts.com/, then 301 to https://beastlyfacts.com/); "http://www.beastlyfacts.com/about -> 3 redirects"; "http://www.beastlyfacts.com/guides/bearded-dragon -> 3 redirects"; "http://beastlyfacts.com/guides/bearded-dragon -> 2 redirects" (301 then 308 to /guides/bearded-dragon/); "https://www.beastlyfacts.com/ -> 1 redirects".
findings.scope: Inbound links to www or http variants
findings.fix: Add one Cloudflare Single Redirect rule matching host www.beastlyfacts.com on any scheme that sends a 301 straight to https://beastlyfacts.com with the same path, so it runs before Always Use HTTPS.

findings.title: security.txt points to a Policy page that 404s
findings.claim: The site publishes a valid security.txt, a good trust signal, but its Policy field links to /security-policy, which returns 404. Visible to security researchers and scanners that read the file, not to ordinary visitors.
findings.evidence: public/.well-known/security.txt:5 "Policy: https://beastlyfacts.com/security-policy". Live https://beastlyfacts.com/.well-known/security.txt returned 200 text/plain with that line. curl https://beastlyfacts.com/security-policy -> "HTTP/2 404"; /security-policy/ -> 404; grep in src/lib/routeRegistry.jsx and public/_redirects found no security-policy route.
findings.scope: 1 file
findings.fix: Delete line 5 of public/.well-known/security.txt (the Policy field is optional), or point it at an existing page such as /contact/.

eeat-articles.notCheckable: I could not open pages in a browser: headless Chromium fails TLS here. So visual prominence (font size, how far down the byline sits on a phone screen) is judged from Tailwind classes and byte offsets in the prerendered HTML, not from screenshots. Mobile and desktop share one main-column DOM for these elements, which is why I say "both". I curled 22 live pages: 6 hubs, 8 care deep dives, 5 wild-animal articles, /about/, /how-guides-are-made/ and /sitemap.xml. The 857-article counts come from frontmatter and MDX scans, and I am assuming the deterministic render code holds for the pages I did not fetch. I could not tell whether the clustered lastUpdated dates (275 articles on 2026-09-25) reflect substantive edits, because the local clone is shallow (80 commits). I also could not check how Google actually chooses a date or author for these pages: there is no Search Console or rich-results access from here. The "41 wild" figure counts articles whose category or categories frontmatter includes Wild Animals; 32 have it as the primary category.

findings.title: Care guide hubs carry no author, no date and no sources, and their schema names only the Organization
findings.claim: None of the 108 species hubs at /guides/<id>/ shows a byline, a published, updated or reviewed date, or a sources list. Their Article JSON-LD gives author as the Organization, with no datePublished or dateModified. The hub data has no date or author field at all, and none of the 108 hubs gets a sitemap lastmod. Blog articles on the same subject get a Person author, two visible dates and a Sources block, so the most important page per species is the least attributed page on the site.
findings.evidence: Code: src/pages/GuideDetail.jsx:302-311 emits {"@type":"Article", "author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Beastly Facts"}} with no date keys. The header (GuideDetail.jsx:368-392) renders the emoji, name, petType, difficulty, tagline and an optional firsthand line, with no byline or date. The file never renders <Sources>. Data census (node script over all 11 files in src/lib/data/guides): 108 hubs. Key counts: id 108, layout 84, firstWeek 84, faqs 108, and so on. Keys matching /date|updat|review|author|source|publish|verified|written|by/: [] (none). Dates exist only in code comments, e.g. turtles.js:23 "Rewritten to the template shape 2026-09-16". Live curl of 6 hubs (bearded-dragon, ball-python, rabbit, leopard-gecko, dog-labrador, cat-persian): every one has LD {"@type":"Article",...,"author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Beastly Facts"...}} and no datePublished. The visible text has 0 date strings, 0 "Written by" and 0 "Last reviewed". Live sitemap.xml: 108 /guides/<id>/ URLs, 0 with <lastmod>. On 9 hubs (bearded-dragon, rabbit, budgie, cockatoo, lovebird, dog-golden-retriever, hermit-crab, chinchilla, guinea-pig) the only person signal is an unlinked firsthand line, e.g. "Written from Mike's own two dragons, Dex and Cera." (GuideDetail.jsx:381). The only /about/ link on each hub is the footer's (1 per page).
findings.scope: All 108 hubs (84 router, 24 legacy dog/cat). Visitors see it on mobile and desktop; Google sees it in the Article JSON-LD and sitemap.
findings.fix: Add hub-level `author`, `lastReviewed` and `lastUpdated` fields to the guide data. Render a byline and dates under the H1 using the same AUTHOR card the articles use. Emit authorSchema(), datePublished and dateModified in the hub Article JSON-LD, and feed lastUpdated into the sitemap lastmod for /guides/<id>/.

repro.correctedClaim: All 108 species hubs at /guides/<id>/ (84 router, 24 legacy dog/cat) carry no byline, no publish, update or reviewed date, and no external Sources list. Their Article JSON-LD names the Organization as author and has no datePublished or dateModified. The guide data has no top-level date, author or review field, and none of the 108 hub URLs in the live sitemap has a lastmod. Blog articles on the same species do get a Person author (Michael Ryan), a visible publish date plus a visible "Last reviewed" date, and a "Sources & Further Reading" block. Two details in the finding are wrong. First, the hubs are not uniquely "the least attributed page on the site": the 103 encyclopedia entries (/encyclopedia/animal/<id>/) have the same gap, with an Organization author at EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:149, no dates, no byline, no sources and 0 of 103 with a sitemap lastmod. Second, the hub data is not free of source fields. firstWeek.rows[].source appears 1,345 times and emergencyCard.source appears 84 times. These hold slugs of the site's own articles, and 84 of 108 hubs show a visible "From <article title> →" link to the article the advice came from. Those are internal attribution links, not citations, so the core gap still stands. Every hub also links once to /about/ and once to /how-guides-are-made/, both in the footer. Visitors see the gap on mobile and desktop. Google sees it in the Article JSON-LD and in the sitemap.
repro.evidence:
Code: src/pages/GuideDetail.jsx:304 is "@type": "Article" and :309 is "author": { "@type": "Organization", "name": "Beastly Facts", ... }. The Article object has no date keys. The header runs from :362 ("{/* Header */}") through about :392 and renders the emoji, h1 name, petType, difficulty, tagline and, at :381, the optional firsthand line. findings.title: Corrections never appear on the corrected page and do not move its dates
findings.claim: The public corrections log (41 entries) is rendered only on /how-guides-are-made/. A reader on a corrected article or hub gets no correction note. On 8 of the 36 corrected /blog/ pages the logged correction is dated after both the page's dateModified and its visible "Last reviewed" date, so neither the page nor its schema shows that it changed. Three of those 8 are dated 2026-10-16, after the log went live on 2026-10-15, so those dates are definitely when the fix shipped.
findings.evidence: grep: CORRECTIONS is imported only by src/pages/HowGuidesAreMade.jsx:7. Sources.jsx:4 imports REVIEWS only. Live /blog/budgie-feeding-guide/ contains the corrected "75 to 80%" figure, shows "Last reviewed 16 Sep 2026" and has dateModified 2026-10-03.
