findings.title: authorSchema() turns 87 'Mike' bylines into a separate, unlinked Person
findings.claim: authorSchema() links a byline to the /about/ Person only when the frontmatter author is exactly 'Michael Ryan'. 87 published articles declare author: "Mike", so their BlogPosting JSON-LD carries a bare Person named 'Mike' with no @id, url or sameAs. Google sees that as a second, unconnected author. The visible author box on those same pages says 'Written by Michael Ryan'.
findings.evidence: src/lib/data/author.js:53-57: const isKnown = !name || name === AUTHOR.name; otherwise it returns { '@type': 'Person', name }. find content -name '*.mdx' -not -path '*/_scheduled*' finds 857 files: 87 have author: "Mike", 770 have author: "Michael Ryan", 0 have no author. Live https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/border-collie-enrichment-guide/ and /blog/hedgehog-enrichment-guide/: BlogPosting author = {"@type": "Person", "name": "Mike"}, while the visible text reads 'Written by Michael Ryan'. Live /blog/a-rhino-horn-is-made-of-keratin/ (author Michael Ryan): author = {"@type":"Person","@id":"https://beastlyfacts.com/about/","name":"Michael Ryan","url":...,"sameAs":[4 URLs]}. src/pages/Blog.jsx:727 always renders AUTHOR.name, which is why readers never see the mismatch.
findings.scope: 87 of 857 published articles (about 10%). Google only.
findings.fix: In author.js:54, treat 'Mike' as an alias of the known author (name === AUTHOR.name || name === 'Mike'), or change the 87 frontmatter lines to "Michael Ryan".

findings.title: State legal pages: every entry cites the rule, links the source and shows its check date
findings.claim: Every state legal page shows, for each entry: the section cited (for example '§ 671(c)(7)(A)'), the quoted rule text, a link to the agency or statute, and 'Checked against the published text on <date>'. Each page also opens with a summary of when the entries were verified and a 'Not Legal Advice' box. This is the strongest trust pattern on the site, and it is exactly what the risk of stale legal claims calls for.
findings.evidence: I fetched all 52 /exotic-pet-laws/state/<slug>/ URLs in the sitemap (52/52 HTTP 200) and parsed them with scratchpad/eeat-other/scripts/states.py. All 1,978 entry rows (counted by 'Link to this row') carry a 'Checked against the published text on <date>' line. The dates run from 5 Aug 2026 to 8 Oct 2026: 1,951 in October, 9 in September, 18 in August. The oldest is 75 days before today. All 52 pages have at least one outbound statute or agency link, and all 52 show 'Not Legal Advice'. California page: 'Read against the published rules, verified 1 October 2026 for 78 of 82 animals; the other 4 last checked between 2 October and 8 October 2026.' Each row ends with a link such as 'California Code of Regulations Title 14 § 671, via CDFW Restricted Species Laws and Regulations Manual →'. Code: src/pages/ExoticPetLawsState.jsx:251-253 and 360-362.
findings.scope: 52 state and jurisdiction pages. Visible on mobile and desktop.

findings.title: Owner identity: the byline photo is a lizard and sameAs lists only brand accounts
findings.claim: There is no photo of the owner anywhere on the site. The Person entity's image, and the author box on every article, show Dex, a bearded dragon. The Person sameAs lists only the four brand accounts that the Organization also lists, so no personal profile confirms 'Michael Ryan' as a real individual. Credentials are honestly disclaimed and the outside-review list is empty. The name itself is consistent: 'Michael Ryan' in the schema and bylines, and 'I go by Mike' on About.
findings.evidence: src/lib/data/author.js:18-22: 'Dex for now, at Michael's request, until he picks a photo of himself', with image '/assets/images/about/dex-portrait.jpg'. I viewed the file: a bearded dragon's head in grass. On live https://beastlyfacts.com/about/, the ProfilePage Person image is https://beastlyfacts.com/assets/images/about/dex-portrait.jpg and sameAs is [instagram.com/beastly.facts, pinterest.com/beastlyfacts/, x.com/beastly_facts, youtube.com/@BeastlyFactsOfficial]. The visible About photo caption reads 'Dex. He came to me in February 2022 at four years old.' The live article author box shows beside 'Written by Michael Ryan'. Curl of those profiles returns brand pages: YouTube 'BeastlyFacts - YouTube', Pinterest 'Beastly Facts (BeastlyFacts) - Profile', Threads 'Beastly Facts (@beastly.facts)'. src/pages/HowGuidesAreMade.jsx:177 says 'I am a keeper, not a veterinarian, a biologist or a lawyer' and line 254 says 'No outside reviews yet.'
findings.scope: The About page, the author box on every article, and the Person schema site-wide. Mobile and desktop.
findings.fix: The owner decides. Options: add a real photo of the owner to AUTHOR.image (with Dex in it is fine), and add any personal profile the owner is willing to link, such as a personal Instagram or LinkedIn, to AUTHOR.sameAs. Keep the brand accounts on the Organization only.

findings.title: Organization schema: two brand names, a scenic photo as the logo, and incomplete sameAs
findings.claim: The site-wide brand entity is inconsistent in four ways. (1) The WebSite node is named 'BeastlyFacts' and the Organization 'Beastly Facts', and page titles also use both spellings. (2) The Organization logo is og-default.jpg, a 1200x630 landscape photo of a bearded dragon, a lorikeet and a kangaroo, not the BF logo the site already has. (3) sameAs leaves out Facebook and Threads, which every page links in the footer, and spells the Pinterest and Instagram URLs differently from the Person sameAs. (4) No Organization node has an @id, so Google cannot merge the site-wide Organization, the article publisher and the Person's worksFor into one entity.
findings.evidence: src/App.jsx:180 has "name": "BeastlyFacts" (WebSite) and line 195 has "name": "Beastly Facts" (Organization). Line 197 sets the logo to og-default.jpg. Lines 198-203 set sameAs to [https://www.pinterest.com/BeastlyFacts, https://x.com/beastly_facts, https://www.instagram.com/beastly.facts, https://www.youtube.com/@BeastlyFactsOfficial]. src/lib/data/author.js:31-36: the Person sameAs uses https://instagram.com/beastly.facts and https://www.pinterest.com/beastlyfacts/. Lines 39-47: PUBLISHER has no @id. The live footer on /, /about/ and /contact/ links https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61590767090597 and https://www.threads.net/@Beastly.Facts; both resolve with the page title 'Beastly Facts'. PIL: public/assets/og-default.jpg is 1200x630 (viewed: an outback scene). public/pwa/icon-512.png is a 512x512 BF logo and returns HTTP 200 live. Head <title> across 237 fetched live pages: 185 'Beastly Facts', 47 'BeastlyFacts' (all 43 Beastlypedia entries use '| BeastlyFacts'), 5 neither. The About page H1 reads 'About BeastlyFacts'.
findings.scope: Every page, through the site-wide JSON-LD. Google only, except the title and H1 spelling split, which visitors see.
findings.fix: In App.jsx: rename the WebSite to 'Beastly Facts' (alternateName 'BeastlyFacts'). Give the Organization the @id https://beastlyfacts.com/#organization and the logo https://beastlyfacts.com/pwa/icon-512.png. Add the Facebook and Threads URLs to sameAs. Then reference that @id from PUBLISHER and worksFor in author.js.

findings.title: Beastlypedia entries: no byline, date or on-page sources; 14 of 43 have no route to any source
findings.claim: Beastlypedia entries carry no byline, no date and no sources on the page. 29 of 43 link to a related Fact File card that shows a source count. The other 14 have no path to any source at all. Unsourced fun facts sit beside the researched text, for example 'They've even been seen crying.' on the elephant page.
findings.evidence: I fetched all 43 entry URLs from the sitemap (43/43 HTTP 200) and parsed them with scripts/entries.py. JSON-LD is @type Thing on 43/43, with no author or date keys (code: src/pages/BeastfileDetail.jsx:117-126). Visible byline 0/43, the word 'Sources' 0/43, outbound non-social links 0/43. A '<n> sources Read the evidence' related-file card appears on 29/43. The 14 entries without one: aye-aye, bald-eagle, blue-poison-dart-frog, capybara, cuttlefish, fennec-fox, humpback-whale, leafy-sea-dragon, manta-ray, sea-otter, serval, shoebill, thorny-devil, victoria-crowned-pigeon. A node import shows beastfiles has 43 entries and no sources field. Fun Facts block on https://beastlyfacts.com/beastlypedia/african-elephant/: 'Elephants hold funerals for their dead... They've even been seen crying.' (src/lib/data/facts.js:14, fact id 13). Contrast: the live /fact-files/ hub lists each file with the claim it overturns and a source count ('4 sources', '5 sources').
findings.scope: 43 Beastlypedia entries. Visitors see it on mobile and desktop; Google sees no author or dates.
findings.fix: Render a Sources list and a 'last reviewed' date on each Beastfile, drawn from a new sources array in src/lib/data/beastlypedia/*.js or from its related Fact File's sources. Add a source to each unsourced fun fact shown there, or remove it.

findings.title: CC BY and CC BY-SA photos are shown with no credit, and no credits page exists
findings.claim: Photos licensed CC BY and CC BY-SA appear on the site without the attribution those licenses require. The public credits page that the owner's own rules call for does not exist.
findings.evidence: IMAGE_CREDITS.md:3: 'CC BY and CC BY-SA require visible credit wherever the photo is shown, so every row here must also appear on the site's public credits page'. Its table lists 8 such photos in public/assets/facts/: flamingo, flamingo-2, quokka, shoebill, leafy-sea-dragon, thorny-devil, glass-frog and coconut-crab. They are wired up in src/lib/data/factImages.js:42, 126-130, 187 and 204. Live https://beastlyfacts.com/gallery/ renders (Bob Owen, CC BY 2.0) and flamingo.jpg (JeffreyGammon, CC BY 4.0), and the page has 0 matches for credit, CC BY or wikimedia. curl of /credits/, /photo-credits/ and /image-credits/ returns 404 for all three, and src/App.jsx:91-170 has no credits route. Grepping src, public and content for the photographers' names (JeffreyGammon, Giles Laurent, Pikuan, Rosindell, Drew Avery, Bob Owen) matches 0 files.
findings.scope: 8 photos, in the gallery, the fact lightboxes and anywhere else those images appear. Visible on mobile and desktop.
findings.fix: Build a /credits/ page from the IMAGE_CREDITS.md table (author, license with link, source) and link it from the footer. Show a one-line credit in ImageLightbox for any image that has a credits entry.

findings.title: Legal hub and per-animal legal pages: weak freshness signals and no named checker
findings.claim: Outside the state pages, the legal section gives weaker signals of freshness and accountability. The hub /exotic-pet-laws/ makes time-bound federal claims ('currently covering close to 800 species') with no visible date, and its summaries had drifted from the matrix until a 16 October correction. The 82 per-animal pages show their verified date only in a 'Cite this page' box near the bottom; the restriction rows show no date until a visitor clicks a state. No legal page names who checked it, and none carries a dateModified in its JSON-LD.
findings.evidence: Live https://beastlyfacts.com/exotic-pet-laws/: grep for last updated, last checked, last reviewed, verified or 'as of' finds nothing, and the only date is '© 2026'. The text says 'a front-end list currently covering close to 800 species'. The hub links 6 outbound sources (fws.gov x3, cdc.gov, fda.gov, animallaw.info). src/pages/ExoticPetLawsHub.jsx has no ld+json and no date. Corrections log on live /how-guides-are-made/, Oct 16: 'Exotic Pet Legal Hub ... the hub blurbs had not been updated with them.' Live /exotic-pet-laws/hedgehog/: 'Checked against the published text on' appears 0 times in the static HTML. The only date is 'Beastly Facts, "Hedgehog laws by state", verified 1 October 2026 (Maine 4 August 2026).' at line 218 of 269 text lines. src/pages/ExoticPetLaws.jsx:525-527 renders the per-entry date only in the selected-state detail card. JSON-LD on all 52 state pages is WebSite, Organization and BreadcrumbList only. Visible 'Michael Ryan', 'Written by' or 'Reviewed by': 0 of 52 state pages, and none on the hub, map, hedgehog or ferret pages.
findings.scope: The legal hub (1 page) and 82 per-animal pages for dates; the map and all 52 state pages for the missing byline and schema.
findings.fix: Under the H1 of the hub, map, per-animal and state pages, add 'Last reviewed <date> by Michael Ryan' with a link to /how-guides-are-made/. Use the newest verifiedOn as the date, or a LAST_REVIEWED constant for the hub. Emit a WebPage node with dateModified and author: authorSchema() next to the existing BreadcrumbList.

findings.title: About, How guides are made and Contact: real experience and unusual transparency
findings.claim: These three pages give real first-hand experience and unusual transparency: a named owner, a concrete keeping history, an honest statement of no credentials, a disclosure of AI use, an outside-review section that admits there is none yet, a public corrections log with was/now/source for each fix, a funding and affiliate disclosure, and three ways to get in touch.
findings.evidence: Live https://beastlyfacts.com/about/: 'My name is Michael Ryan. I go by Mike.', 'In February 2022 a friend of my sister's was moving and could not take her bearded dragon... His name is Dex.', 'In 2024 my aunt's bearded dragon needed a home too. I named her Cera', 'The vet diagnosed heart disease', 'Some articles contain affiliate links, marked on the page.' Live /how-guides-are-made/: 'Last updated: October 15, 2026', 'I use AI tools to draft and organize. I check every claim against a source I have opened myself', 'No outside reviews yet.', and a corrections log headed 'October 2026 18 entries', each entry with Page, Was, Now and Source. Live /contact/: a form with the options 'I spotted an error on a page' and 'I can review a guide for accuracy', an email address, and 6 social accounts. In the raw HTML the email is Cloudflare-obfuscated as /cdn-cgi/l/email-protection, decoded for visitors with JavaScript; the source address is hello@beastlyfacts.com (src/pages/HowGuidesAreMade.jsx:328). One polish item: HowGuidesAreMade.jsx:9 LAST_UPDATED='2026-10-15' also serves as the 'log opened on' date, so 'Last updated: October 15, 2026' sits above five Oct 16 entries (src/lib/data/corrections.js:31-67).
findings.scope: About, How guides are made and Contact. Visible on mobile and desktop.

findings.title: The homepage never says who runs the site
findings.claim: The homepage does not say who is behind the site. Its hero speaks as 'We looked it up. So you don't have to.', while About says 'It's just me'. There is no owner name, photo or one-line keeper intro, and About is reached only through the menu and the footer. The site's trust case rests on one named keeper, and the most visited page hides the owner.
findings.evidence: Live https://beastlyfacts.com/: the hero reads 'Wild facts. Pet care. We looked it up. So you don't have to.' (src/components/home/HeroSection.jsx:202-204). The homepage text has 0 matches for 'Michael Ryan' or 'Mike'. Its only first-person line is in the Otis teaser: 'Otis is my sister's rabbit'. The About page says 'It's just me.' The top bar text on the live page is 'Guides Articles Facts Beastle Laws Donate'. About sits in the menu's 'The site' group (src/components/layout/Navbar.jsx:342) and in the footer (src/components/layout/Footer.jsx:88).
findings.scope: Homepage, on mobile and desktop.
findings.fix: Add a short keeper strip to the homepage: a photo, a line such as 'I'm Mike. I keep two rescued bearded dragons and write every guide here.', and links to /about/ and /how-guides-are-made/. Change the hero voice from 'We' to 'I'.

content-dates-claims.notCheckable: 1) Whether any page existed before 2026-05-18 (for example on another domain), and the true first-deploy dates of the 148 articles dated 2026-09-04: web.archive.org was unreachable. curl's CDX query failed with a connection reset, and WebFetch said it could not fetch from web.archive.org. Git history is shallow: the first commit is 2026-10-12 10:31 UTC, so frontmatter dates cannot be checked against commits. 2) I made no rendered or mobile screenshots, since an external browser cannot load the live site here. My statements about what visitors see come from the prerendered HTML text and component class names, not from viewing pages. 3) I did not reconcile the /blog/ sidebar category counts (they total 931 because articles sit in several categories) or the sitemap's 802 /blog/ URLs against 821 non-story articles; that belongs to the SEO lane. 4) I did not audit per-article numeric claims, such as the '30 Bans, 9 Permit States' title counts, against legalStatus.json. 5) The corrections log says its entries before 2026-10-15 are dated to when a working doc recorded them, so for 5 of the 8 date-lag cases I could not establish the exact day each fix went live.

findings.title: Five articles are dated before the domain existed
findings.claim: Five published articles carry a publish date earlier than the registration of beastlyfacts.com, and they show that date to visitors in the byline and to Google as datePublished. Six articles also predate the site's own welcome post, which is dated 2026-06-01.
findings.evidence: RDAP: `curl https://rdap.verisign.com/com/v1/domain/beastlyfacts.com` returned eventAction registration, eventDate 2026-05-18T17:33:24Z (May 18, 13:33 owner time). The frontmatter scan (my script over all 857 files in content/ outside content/_scheduled-*) found 5 dates before 2026-05-18: content/guides/reptile-shedding-complete-guide.mdx:5 date "2026-04-05", uvb-lighting-complete-guide.mdx:5 "2026-04-12", ball-python-feeding-guide.mdx:6 "2026-04-26", leopard-gecko-temperature-guide.mdx:5 "2026-05-03", crested-gecko-humidity-guide.mdx:5 "2026-05-10". Live https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/reptile-shedding-complete-guide/ shows the visible byline "Apr 5, 2026" and serves "datePublished":"2026-04-05" and article:published_time content="2026-04-05". https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/uvb-lighting-complete-guide/ serves "datePublished":"2026-04-12". The welcome post content/blog/main-blog-post.mdx:4 is dated "2026-06-01", while content/guides/the-incredible-axolotl-nature-s-smiling-salamander.mdx is dated 2026-05-23. docs/RULES.md:23 says "`date` is the day the article ships: never backdated". scripts/check-publish-dates.mjs checks only for future dates and has no lower bound.
findings.scope: 5 articles (each visible to visitors on mobile and desktop, plus JSON-LD and OG meta), and the welcome-post timeline sitewide
findings.fix: Re-date the five articles to their real ship date, which can be no earlier than 2026-05-18, and add a lower bound of 2026-05-18 to scripts/check-publish-dates.mjs so it cannot happen again.

repro.correctedClaim: The claim reproduces as stated. Five of the 857 published MDX files (all of content/ except content/_scheduled-*) carry a frontmatter date earlier than the 2026-05-18 registration of beastlyfacts.com. They are reptile-shedding-complete-guide 2026-04-05, uvb-lighting-complete-guide 2026-04-12, ball-python-feeding-guide 2026-04-26, leopard-gecko-temperature-guide 2026-05-03 and crested-gecko-humidity-guide 2026-05-10. Visitors see each date in the article byline on both mobile and desktop, and it also shows on related-article cards on other pages. Google gets the same date as JSON-LD datePublished and article:published_time. Six articles are dated before the welcome post's 2026-06-01: those five plus the axolotl article (2026-05-23). That count is correct, but it is weak evidence of a defect on its own. The welcome post itself says the site was "a handful of care guides and some fun facts" when it was first written, and the axolotl date is later than the domain registration. The five dates have a stronger origin than the finding states. All five files first entered the repo on June 19 at 02:12 (2026-06-19T06:12:16Z) with dates in 2025 ("2025-04-05" and so on). Commit 733c3bd on Sept 7 at 11:10 changed only the year to 2026. So the dates are converted placeholders, not real ship dates.
repro.evidence:
1) RDAP: `curl -sS https://rdap.verisign.com/com/v1/domain/beastlyfacts.com` returned {'eventAction': 'registration', 'eventDate': '2026-05-18T17:33:24Z'}, which is May 18, 13:33 owner time.
2) Frontmatter scan: my own script (scratchpad/predate-verify/scan.py) walked content/ and skipped _scheduled-*. It printed: total 857, no-date files 0, "before 2026-05-18: 5", "before 2026-06-01: 6". The earliest dates match the finder's files and lines exactly: guides/reptile-shedding-complete-guide.mdx:5, uvb-lighting-complete-guide.mdx:5, ball-python-feeding-guide.mdx:6, leopard-gecko-temperature-guide.mdx:5, crested-gecko-humidity-guide.mdx:5, then axolotl 2026-05-23 at line 5, then blog/main-blog-post.mdx:4 at 2026-06-01.
3) Live site: I fetched all 5 pages with curl (all returned 200). Each serves one datePublished matching its frontmatter, for example "datePublished":"2026-04-05" and article:published_time" content="2026-04-05" on reptile-shedding. The visible text reads "Reptiles Apr 5, 2026 8 min read", and likewise "Apr 12, 2026", "Apr 26, 2026", "May 3, 2026" and "May 10, 2026". The byline span has class "text-xs text-muted-foreground font-body flex items-center gap-1", which has no hidden or breakpoint class, so the date shows on mobile and desktop. "Apr 26, 2026" also appears on a related card on the reptile-shedding page.
4) docs/RULES.md:23 reads: "- `date` is the day the article ships: never backdated, never future-dated." scripts/check-publish-dates.mjs only flags `m[1] > today` and has no lower bound.
5) History: the local clone is shallow (first local commit is 2026-10-12), so I used the GitHub API. `gh api repos/mrd1030/beastlyfactss/commits?path=...` shows all five files first added in c1c9afc at 2026-06-19T06:12:16Z ("Add 5 converted MDX guide articles"). At 953ce60 the frontmatter of reptile-shedding read date: "2025-04-05", and the other four were also dated 2025. Commit 733c3bd (2026-09-07T15:10:38Z, "Fix five article dates and blog data entries stamped 2025 to 2026") changed them to 2026 and kept the month and day. The repo was created 2026-06-01T05:38:09Z. The axolotl file first appeared in 4cac532 ("Migrate off Sanity to MDX") already dated 2026-05-23.
6) I could not confirm whether any of these articles was live on an earlier Base44-hosted version of the site before June 19. The Wayback availability API returned no snapshots, and the CDX and crt.sh queries failed (connection reset and 502).
repro.fix: This is the owner's decision. Re-date the five articles to when they actually went live. The best evidence is the date they entered the repo, 2026-06-19 (or the deploy after it), not merely "no earlier than 2026-05-18". Their dates were 2025 placeholders that were later bumped to 2026, so they have no real basis. Re-dating leaves the URLs unchanged. lastUpdated stays later than date because the latest is 2026-09-25 or after. Leave the axolotl article and the welcome post alone: neither predates the domain, and articles dated before the welcome post are consistent with what that post says. Optionally add a floor to scripts/check-publish-dates.mjs, such as a minimum of 2026-05-18 for date, so placeholder years like 2025 fail the build.

impact.correctedClaim: The core fact holds. Five of the 857 live articles (content/ outside content/_scheduled-*) are dated before beastlyfacts.com was registered on 2026-05-18 (17:33 UTC). Visitors see that date at the top of each article. It has no responsive hide class, so it shows on both mobile and desktop. It is also on related-article cards on other posts, and Google gets it as datePublished and article:published_time. The five dates are 2026-04-05, 04-12, 04-26, 05-03 and 05-10. They are not real ship dates: they match, value for value, the leftover seed data in the unused file src/lib/data/blog.js. Four of the five fall on Sundays a week apart. The second half of the finding does not hold up. The welcome post says the site already had "a handful of care guides" when it was written, so the sixth article (axolotl, 2026-05-23) being older than the welcome post is not a problem, and it postdates the domain registration. Severity is low, not high. It breaks the RULES.md "never backdated" rule on 5 of 857 pages (0.6%). A visitor would only notice by looking up when the domain was registered. Google sets its own first-seen date and does not penalize a datePublished that is a few weeks too early. dateModified (2026-09-25 or 2026-10-02) and the sitemap lastmod are current, and the feed does not list these articles.

impact.fix: This is the owner's call: only the owner knows when these five actually went live. If the owner does not know, use a defensible floor, such as the site's launch date, rather than the registration timestamp. Change only `date` in those five MDX frontmatters, using a US Eastern date. Leave lastUpdated and lastReviewed alone. Then run sync-articles so the generated meta follows. Rotation numbers are unaffected. Backdating to any date after May 18 would still pass, and a real check against first-commit dates is not reliable in shallow cloud clones. If the owner wants a guard, a launch-date floor is the cheapest one, but it is not required to fix the issue.

impact.correctedClaim: The corrections log appears only on /how-guides-are-made/. CORRECTIONS (src/lib/data/corrections.js) has 41 entries on 40 distinct pages: 36 entries on 35 /blog/ pages, plus /facts/ and 4 /guides/ hubs. The byline shows only the publish date, and the one other visible date is "Last reviewed" (lastReviewed) in the Sources block at the bottom. That date is earlier than the logged correction on 30 of the 34 pages, not just the 8. Beyond the logged pages, budgie-tank-setup-guide was changed in the same Oct 16 commit and still serves dateModified 2026-10-03. Severity is medium, not high.
impact.evidence:
1. Counts. `node` import of corrections.js gives: total 41, blog entries 36, distinct blog pages 35, distinct pages 40. Non-blog pages: /facts/, /guides/millipede/, /guides/axolotl/, /guides/hamster/, /guides/sulcata-tortoise/.
2. Fetch. I curled all 40 pages at concurrency 4: 39 returned 200 and 1 returned "301 https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/exotic-pet-legal-hub/ -> https://beastlyfacts.com/exotic-pet-laws/". I then fetched /exotic-pet-laws/ (200).
3. No notes or links. On the body before `<footer`, href="/how-guides-are-made/" appears 0 times on all 40 pages and exactly once on each full page (the footer). A regex for correct/corrected/correction found only "(Virginia Myth Corrected)" link titles, the axolotl guide's "The Virginia Correction" section and "unless it's actively corrected" in flying-squirrel. None is an errata note.
4. Stale dateModified. Live dateModified is earlier than the newest correction on 8 of 34 blog pages, e.g. axolotl-legal "dateModified":"2026-10-08" against log 2026-10-16, and chinchilla-tank-setup "2026-09-25" against 2026-10-06. The repo frontmatter gives the same 8 of 35 (scratchpad fm.mjs). Live sitemap lastmod is the same stale value for all 8, e.g. `<loc>https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/chinchilla-tank-setup-guide/</loc><lastmod>2026-09-25</lastmod>`.
5. Visible dates. The chinchilla page body shows "Jul 19, 2026 5 min read" in the byline and "Last reviewed 19 Jul 2026 · 4 sources" in the Sources block. There is no "Updated" date. Blog.jsx:947 sets dateModified to lastUpdated, falling back to lastReviewed. Sources.jsx:93-99 renders only lastReviewed. Parsing "Last reviewed" on the live pages gives 30 of 34 dated before the newest correction.
6. The Oct 16 fixes are verifiable. Commit 93ec3d1 (2026-10-16 06:01 UTC, 02:01 Eastern) changed the axolotl and sugar glider legal guides without touching lastUpdated. Commit 2822067 changed budgie-feeding and budgie-tank-setup the same way. budgie-tank-setup-guide.mdx:7 still reads lastUpdated "2026-10-03", and the live page serves "dateModified":"2026-10-03".
7. The 5 older fixes are only partly verifiable. The clone is shallow: 80 commits, root 002cfba on 2026-10-12. The working doc records the dates: archive/docs-completed/FIX_PLAN_COMPLETED_2026-09-25.md:12 says "Fixed 2026-10-06 (owner)" for chinchilla, :120 "Resolved 2026-10-04" for platy and :124 "Resolved 2026-10-04" for neon tetra.
8. Owner's rule. docs/RULES.md:186-187 says navigation-only edits do not bump lastUpdated or lastReviewed: "Only a fact added or reviewed does." So the 8 stale dates break the owner's own rule.
9. No broken promise. The site promises only that "the fix is logged above" (HowGuidesAreMade.jsx:331), and it is. Nothing on the site promises per-page notes. The "noted on the page they changed" line (HowGuidesAreMade.jsx:318) renders only when CORRECTIONS is empty.
10. Severity reasoning. Google treats dateModified and lastmod as hints. The understatement is 1 to 14 days on 8 of the 802 sitemap lastmod entries, and understating is not the abuse case. The missing on-page note is a transparency best practice, not a ranking factor. It does matter for a returning reader on pages where safety figures changed (temperatures, quarantine), so the severity is medium.
impact.fix:
1. Now, as a content-only change: set lastUpdated on the 8 MDX files and on budgie-tank-setup-guide.mdx to their correction dates. Use the log's date, not today, and do not touch lastReviewed, because a correction is not a source review. This follows RULES.md:186. The sitemap and dateModified follow on the next deploy.
2. Note on articles: extend the pattern Sources.jsx already uses for REVIEWS. It filters by pathname at src/components/mdx/Sources.jsx:105-108; do the same with CORRECTIONS. Render a short "Corrected <date>" next to "Last reviewed", linking to the log. Do not print the log's `now` text verbatim: it is written for the log and refers to other pages ("The map already said both", "matching the other parrot guides").
3. Deep links: to link a specific entry, log items need ids. HowGuidesAreMade.jsx:111 has none, and only the first month's `<details>` opens by default (line 99). So add ids and open the month on hash, or link with a filter query the page reads.
4. Hubs and facts: /guides/ hubs (GuideDetail.jsx) and /facts/ need their own render path, because Sources.jsx only covers MDX articles.
5. Build check: a check that fails when a /blog/ page's lastUpdated is earlier than its newest correction is proportionate and fits the existing check-publish-dates.mjs. It only covers the page an entry names, though, so pages changed alongside it (budgie-tank-setup) still rely on the RULES.md:186 habit.

findings.title: 108 guide hubs carry no date anywhere
findings.claim: Every species care guide hub under /guides/<id>/ ships Article JSON-LD with no datePublished or dateModified and shows no updated or reviewed date to readers. That includes hubs the corrections log lists as corrected.
findings.evidence: I fetched all 108 /guides/<id>/ URLs from the live sitemap. 108 of 108 contain "@type":"Article" and 0 of 108 contain datePublished or dateModified. 0 of 108 show any visible 'Last updated', 'Last reviewed' or 'Reviewed' text. Source: src/pages/GuideDetail.jsx:302-312 builds the Article object with headline, description, image, url, author, publisher and mainEntityOfPage only. The sitemap entries for /guides/ (120 URLs) have no <lastmod>, for example /guides/hamster/ has only changefreq and priority. The log records corrections to /guides/hamster/ and /guides/axolotl/ (2026-10-02), /guides/millipede/ (2026-10-04) and /guides/sulcata-tortoise/ (2026-09-25), and none of those pages shows when it changed.
findings.scope: All 108 care guide hubs, the site's main pages; affects visitors (no freshness signal) on mobile and desktop and Google (no Article dates, no sitemap lastmod)
findings.fix: Add a reviewed/updated date field to each guide object, render it under the hub title, emit it as datePublished/dateModified in the GuideDetail Article JSON-LD, and write it as <lastmod> in generate-sitemap.js.

findings.title: Homepage counts call breeds and generic hubs 'species', and '108+' overclaims
findings.claim: The homepage's guide and profile counts include dog and cat breeds and five generic dog and cat hubs under the word 'species'. GuideSpotlight also appends '+' to an exact count, so '108+ species guides' overstates what exists.
findings.evidence: Live https://beastlyfacts.com/ body: "A rotating pick from 108+ species guides." (src/components/home/GuideSpotlight.jsx:80, `${guidesIndex.guides.length}+`), "103 species profiles , 100+ care guides , and 400+ deep dives" (src/components/home/FactsToGuidesBanner.jsx:33), and "100+ species care guides, plus 400+ deep dives" (src/components/home/HeroSection.jsx:238). The meta, og and twitter descriptions repeat "100+ species care guides" (src/pages/Home.jsx:43, 46, 55). My node script importing all 11 files in src/lib/data/guides/ counted 108 guides (108 unique ids): 84 non-dog/cat hubs, 14 dog hubs (including dog-universal, dog-small-breed, dog-medium-breed and dog-large-breed) and 10 cat hubs (including cat-universal). src/lib/generated/encyclopedia-index.json has 103 animals, 10 of them dogs and 9 cats (all breeds). Distinct species therefore come to at most 86 (84 plus dog plus cat). The repo's own comment at FactsToGuidesBanner.jsx:10-13 says the generic size hubs "cannot inflate this number", yet GuideSpotlight counts them.
findings.scope: Homepage: 4 visible sentences (mobile and desktop) and 3 meta tags that Google uses for the snippet
findings.fix: Change GuideSpotlight to "A rotating pick from 108 care guides" (no '+'), and say "care guides" / "animal profiles" rather than "species" wherever the count includes breeds.

findings.title: 'Last reviewed' dates are bulk-stamped, which contradicts the public definition
findings.claim: The site publicly defines the review date as the last day the owner reread the whole piece against its sources. The data shows the date stamped in batches and, at least once, aligned to match a set rather than an actual reread.
findings.evidence: /how-guides-are-made/ live text: "The review date at the foot of an article is the last day I read the whole piece against its sources again." My scan found 837 of 857 articles with lastReviewed, spread over 93 distinct days. The top four days carry 350 articles: 2026-09-24 (158), 2026-09-15 (77), 2026-09-14 (67) and 2026-09-16 (48). Visitors see these at the article foot, for example "Last reviewed 24 Sep 2026 · 4 sources" on /blog/uvb-lighting-complete-guide/. docs/READER_REVIEWS.md:9119-9121 reads: "The feeding guide's cold-stress figure moved ... with no date bump. lastUpdated and lastReviewed now 2026-09-14, matching the rest of the set." READER_REVIEWS_2026-09-24.md:3 records a same-day run of "95 reader reviews" grading 972 pages, and scripts/reader-extract.mjs:4 says "A reader agent gets these files". I could not establish which of the 158 pages the owner personally reread.
findings.scope: 837 articles show the line (visible on mobile and desktop); lastReviewed is not used for dateModified while lastUpdated is present (docs/RULES.md:15-16)
findings.fix: Either stamp lastReviewed only when the owner has reread the whole page, or change the /how-guides-are-made/ wording to say what the date actually records, for example the last full check, including agent-assisted passes.

findings.title: 148 articles share one publish date, and at least one was re-dated backward
findings.claim: Publish dates come in large bursts that the owner's own 4 to 5 per day rule forbids. One article in the largest burst is on record as carrying a different, later date after the date it now shows.
findings.evidence: Of 857 articles, 148 are dated 2026-09-04 (75 of them category Enrichment). 37 of 125 distinct publish dates carry more than 5 articles, covering 628 of the 857 articles; examples are 2026-07-31 (21), 2026-08-29 (20) and 2026-09-16 (27). docs/RULES.md:26 says "Spread a batch by shipping 4 to 5 per day". The live byline on /blog/border-collie-enrichment-guide/ shows "Sep 4, 2026" and "datePublished":"2026-09-04". docs/READER_REVIEWS.md:11559 (heading "Parrotlet (2026-09-15 ...)") and :11737-11739 record that on 2026-09-15 "the enrichment guide `2026-10-31`" was its date. content/guides/parrotlet-enrichment-guide.mdx now has date "2026-09-04", which is earlier than the day the note was written. Git history starts 2026-10-12 10:31 UTC (`git log --reverse`), so the real ship dates cannot be checked from commits.
findings.scope: 148 articles in one day and 628 in burst days; visible in bylines and /blog/ listings (mobile and desktop) and in datePublished
findings.fix: Record each article's true first-deploy date. If the 2026-09-04 batch genuinely shipped that day, note the batch in the docs; otherwise correct the dates. Either way, keep future batches in content/_scheduled-* and release 4 to 5 per day.

findings.title: '400+ deep dives' undercounts by 100 or more

findings.title: Public corrections log with was/now/why and a permanent-entry policy
findings.claim: The site keeps a real, dated corrections log and an honest outside-review register. Both are reachable from every page through the footer and from About.
findings.evidence: src/lib/data/corrections.js holds 41 correction entries (2026-09-03 to 2026-10-16, on 40 distinct pages) with fields was, now, why and reportedBy. Its header says "Entries are permanent: never edit or remove one". REVIEWS is empty except a commented template, and live /how-guides-are-made/ says "No outside reviews yet." findings.title: Legal data cites a primary source and a check date for all 4,264 entries
findings.claim: Every one of the 4,264 animal-by-jurisdiction legal entries has a sourceId that resolves and a verifiedOn date. 3,953 also quote the operative wording verbatim. Most of the 276 sources are official government or legislature URLs, and the state pages tell visitors so in plain words.
findings.evidence: Script over src/lib/data/legalStatus.json: "entries 4264 ... noSourceId 0 dangling 0 noQuote 311 noVerifiedOn 0"; verifiedOn months "[('2026-08', 37), ('2026-09', 11), ('2026-10', 4216)]". Host tally: 218 of 276 sources on government or legislature hosts, plus law.cornell.edu 21. 0 homepage URLs. The README in the same file says "Primary sources only: the regulation, the statute, or the enforcing agency own page. Never a secondary summary." Live: https://beastlyfacts.com/exotic-pet-laws/state/tennessee/ renders "Read against the published rules, verified 1 October 2026 for 66 of 82 animals; the other 16 last checked 8 October 2026. Every entry below quotes the statute or regulation it comes from and carries the date it was last checked."
findings.scope: The legal hub, map, 50+ state pages and per-animal legal pages. Visible on mobile and desktop, and in the crawled HTML.

findings.title: Most sources are high quality, and no dead links turned up in a 165-URL sample
findings.claim: Two thirds of all linked sources are papers, government, university or museum pages, statutes, or veterinary references. No article cites the same URL twice. Seeded random samples of 15 and then 150 distinct source URLs found no 404s. The only dead source found came from the product-page check above, not from the samples.
findings.evidence: Tiering script over 3,368 linked entries: journal/paper 611, gov/univ/museum/law 760, vet/welfare org 863 (together 2,234, 66%); other hobby/husbandry 926; retail 143; affiliate/content sites 65. Top domains: merckvetmanual.com 187, vcahospitals.com 165, petmd.com 164, pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov 143, lafeber.com 127, reptifiles.com 125, doi.org 100, sciencedirect.com 95, animaldiversity.org 82. Wikipedia has only 15 entries in 15 articles, which RULES.md does not ban. Duplicate check: "dup within article: 0". 15-URL seeded sample (random.seed 20261019): all 15 returned HTTP 200. 11 were specific pages whose titles match the citation, for example reptifiles boa handling redirecting to /boa-constrictor/care-guide/boa-constrictor-handling, title "Boa Constrictor Handling: Safe Techniques & Behavior | ReptiFiles". 2 were bare homepages (zenhabitats.com, merckvetmanual.com). 2 were bot walls whose content could not be read (avma.org Incapsula, veterinarypartner.vin.com TSPD challenge). 150-URL sample of 1,988 distinct linked URLs: "133 200, 3 203, 13 403, 1 406", 0 x 404. The 403s are Cloudflare or Akamai challenges ("Just a moment...", "Access Denied"). One sampled redirect lands on a different page: cpw.state.co.us/wildlife-arent-pets goes to /wildlife-possession.
findings.scope: Site-wide, 815 sourced articles. Visible on mobile and desktop.

findings.title: About 287 legal entries rest on third-party copies of the law, not the official text
findings.claim: Despite the primary-sources-only rule, the sources for whole states point at copies of the law hosted by others: animallaw.info, oregon.public.law, lawserver, FindLaw and Onecle. This covers Arizona, Tennessee, Delaware, Wisconsin, Michigan, Nevada and Oregon. Some official sites block automated access, but Delaware's official code page loaded fine from here.
findings.evidence: Script, entries per source: az-r12-4-406 (animallaw.info) 71, tn-70-4-403 (animallaw.info) 62, de-903 (animallaw.info) 58, wi-169 (animallaw.info) 38, mi-large-carnivore (animallaw.info) 20, nv-nac-503 (animallaw.info) 16, or-609-305 (oregon.public.law) 14, tn-70-1-101 (lawserver.com) 4, ar-20-19-501 (animallaw.info) 2, nj-njsa-23-4-63-3 (law.onecle.com) 1, tn-70-4-208 (codes.findlaw.com) 1, for a total of 287. curl https://regulations.delaware.gov/AdminCode/title3/900/903.shtml returned 200 with title "Delaware Regulations". apps.azsos.gov returned 403 and docs.legis.wisconsin.gov reset the connection, so for those two the reproduction may be the only text reachable from this container. Live Tennessee page shows the source link https://www.animallaw.info/statute/tn-exotic-pet-part-4-exotic-animals.
findings.scope: About 287 of 4,264 legal entries across 7 states. The source link is visible to visitors.
findings.fix: Point de-903 at regulations.delaware.gov. For the others, keep the reproduction as a secondary link only, and add the official URL as the primary `url` once it is checked from a desktop browser.

findings.title: 53 articles run over 5 sources without the required note, and the rulebook's overrun list is stale
findings.claim: RULES.md asks for an MDX comment above <Sources> whenever an article goes over the 4 to 5 target. 53 of the 87 articles over 5 links have no such comment, 28 of them legal guides. Meanwhile the five articles RULES.md names as known overruns have since been trimmed to 4 or 5, so the documented list no longer matches the content.
findings.evidence: Rule: docs/RULES.md:89-99. Script: "over 5: 87 with comment above: 34", 53 without, 28 of those legal guides. Non-legal examples: alpha-wolf-myth-what-the-research-actually-says (10), giraffe-heart-myth-what-the-research-shows (10, content/guides/...:107-109 shows "## Sources" then "<Sources>" with no comment), naked-mole-rat-breaks-the-rules-for-mammals (12), immortal-jellyfish-turritopsis-dohrnii-explained (12), ultimate-birdwatching-guide-best-places-times-tips-2026 (10), ball-python-cost-guide (6), sulcata-tortoise-cost-guide (6). Stale list, actual linked counts: bearded-dragon-health-issues-guide 5 (RULES says 9), red-eared-slider-health-issues-guide 4 (says 6), small-mammal-temperature-heat-stress-guide 5 (says 10), small-mammal-grooming-nails-molting-guide 4 (says 8), uvb-lighting-complete-guide 4 (says 7).
findings.scope: 53 articles, plus docs/RULES.md. Only the authors see the comment, but over-long lists are visible to readers (collapsed after 6, per src/components/mdx/Sources.jsx SOURCES_VISIBLE = 6).
findings.fix: Update the overrun list in RULES.md:92-98 to the current counts. Either add the one-line justification comment to the 53 articles, or exempt legal guides by rule, since statute-by-statute citation is their purpose.

nav-surfaces.notCheckable: Two limits on the testing: (1) I could not test real phones. The sandbox browser cannot open external sites, so I served the live HTML, CSS and JS unchanged through a localhost caching proxy and drove them with puppeteer's headless Chrome using touch emulation. iOS Safari and Android Chrome were not tested directly. The toast-overlay result follows from plain CSS (fixed, z-index 100, 32px of padding, no pointer-events rule) and from a measured tap failure, so I expect it to hold on real devices, but I did not watch it happen on one. (2) The 'Back' results used a fake search-results page on another localhost port, not Google itself. The mechanism (history.length counts entries from other sites) is the same. I had no analytics or Search Console data, so I cannot say which nav surfaces or tabs visitors actually use, or how many sessions are on 640 to 767px tablets. Positions in pixels come from rendering the prerendered HTML with JS off, so they can shift slightly once the page is interactive. Two things belong to other lanes and I did not chase them: /care-packages/store/ has no noindex and is left out of the sitemap, although generate-sitemap.js:199-205 says it carries noindex,follow (src/pages/CarePackagesStore.jsx:34-48 has no robots meta; I checked the live header with curl -I and the only x-robots-tag is max-image-preview:large). And /composer/login/ returns HTTP 404 live, which I left alone because it is an admin page no nav surface links to.

findings.title: Invisible toast layer eats taps on the mobile header and on tablet bottom tabs
findings.claim: An empty, invisible toast container sits above the site chrome on every page. On phones (under 640px wide) it covers the top 32px of the screen, so a tap on the center of the menu, search, dark-mode, logo or guide Back button does nothing. Only the bottom 12 to 14px of each control responds. Between 640 and 767px (small tablets in portrait) it moves to the bottom and covers the center of all four bottom tabs. Real visitors on phones and small tablets see this. Desktop users get a dead 420x32 strip at the bottom right.
findings.evidence:
Code: src/components/ui/toast.jsx:6-12 (ToastProvider) and :15-21 (ToastViewport) are both `fixed top-0 z-[100] ... w-full p-4 sm:bottom-0 sm:right-0 sm:top-auto md:max-w-[420px]` with no pointer-events-none, so each empty div is 32px tall. The individual toasts at :25 are already `pointer-events-auto`. src/App.jsx:237 mounts site-wide, above the navbar's z-50 (Navbar.jsx:198). Live: curl https://beastlyfacts.com/ shows the nested pair `
` in the prerendered HTML. Method: the live HTML, CSS and JS were served unchanged through a localhost caching proxy and driven by puppeteer Chrome (scripts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-beastlyfactss/c6c3a501-5606-5a8b-b8c9-191dbbf9547e/scratchpad/nav-surfaces/). At 390x844 the overlays measure [0,0,390,32] and [16,0,390,32]. elementFromPoint at (30,28), (195,28), (278,28) and (356,28) returns the overlay div, and at (356,40) it returns the menu button. Real tap results: a tap on the menu at y=28 left aria-expanded="false", and at y=42 it became "true". A tap on Search at y=28 stayed on /, and at y=42 it went to /search/. The menu button spans y 10 to 46, so 22 of its 36px (61%) are dead. Search spans 12 to 44, so 20 of 32px (62%) are dead. At 700px and 744px: overlays sit at [0,868,744,32] and the centers of the Guides, Facts, Articles and My Pack tabs all return BLOCKED. A tap on the Guides tab 28px above the bottom stayed on /, and 45px above the bottom it went to /guides/. At 1280px: the overlay is [860,868,420,32].
findings.scope: Every page site-wide. Phones: header search, menu, dark mode, the logo (home link) and the guide-hub Back button. 640 to 767px: all 4 bottom tabs. Desktop: a 420x32 strip at the bottom right.
findings.fix: Add `pointer-events-none` to the ToastProvider and ToastViewport class strings in src/components/ui/toast.jsx (lines 9 and 18). Toasts keep `pointer-events-auto`, so they stay clickable.

findings.title: Guide hubs and encyclopedia entries send search visitors back to Google, and mobile guide hubs hide the home link
findings.claim: Someone who lands on a species care-guide hub or an encyclopedia entry from a search result and presses 'Back to Guides', 'Back to Encyclopedia' or the mobile header 'Back' is taken off the site, back to the results page. On phones the guide-hub header also hides the logo, and neither the menu nor the bottom tabs has a Home item, so the only way to the homepage is the footer logo at the bottom of a page about 10,000px tall. Real visitors see this on both desktop (the in-page buttons) and mobile (the buttons plus the missing logo).
findings.evidence: src/pages/GuideDetail.jsx:74-86 and src/pages/EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:58-70 call navigate(-1) whenever `window.history.length > 1`. That count includes the search engine's page. src/components/layout/MobileBackButton.jsx:24 calls navigate(-1) unconditionally. Navbar.jsx:192 and :208 set the logo to `hidden md:flex` on /guides/<id>/. The menu (Navbar.jsx:306-346) and the tabs (BottomTabs.jsx:6-11) contain no '/' link. Articles already solve this: src/pages/Blog.jsx:300 uses `useNavigationType() === 'PUSH'` to tell a cold landing from an in-site click. Test with live JS via the localhost proxy: open a page on another origin, click through to /guides/bearded-dragon/ (history.length 3), then click. All three cases landed back on the external page: 'Back to Guides' at 1280px, 'Back to Guides' at 390px and the header 'Back' at 390px. 'Back to Encyclopedia' on /encyclopedia/animal/bearded-dragon/ did the same. A render of the live HTML at 390px shows only Back, Search, dark mode and menu in the guide-hub header. The footer starts at y=9,121 on that page. Neither page class has a visible breadcrumb (0 aria-label="Breadcrumb" in either live page).
findings.scope: 108 /guides/<id>/ plus 103 /encyclopedia/animal/<id>/ URLs in the live sitemap (211 of 1,327). These are the main search landing pages for pet owners.
findings.fix: Use the Blog.jsx pattern in GuideDetail, EncyclopediaAnimal and MobileBackButton: call navigate(-1) only when the navigation type is PUSH, otherwise navigate('/guides/') or '/encyclopedia/'. Also keep the logo visible on mobile guide hubs, for example by showing the Back button beside it instead of replacing it.

findings.title: Four 'facts' destinations with overlapping names, one of them a legacy duplicate
findings.claim: Facts, Animal facts hub, Fact files, the 'Fun Facts' article topic and Gallery are five nav entries for three different things, and the names do not tell them apart. 'Fun Facts' points to two different places on the same page. /animal-facts/ is a thin legacy page whose title nearly duplicates /facts/ and which shows nine non-clickable keyword chips. Visitors on both desktop and mobile see the overlapping labels. Google sees two near-identical titles.
findings.evidence: What is behind each one (live curl): (1) /facts/, label 'Facts' in header, tab, menu and footer: title 'Fun Animal Facts', page text '347 facts found · Page 1 of 22', short numbered cards in 8 groups. (2) /animal-facts/, label 'Animal facts hub', linked only from the footer (src/components/layout/Footer.jsx:64): title 'Fun Animal Facts & Pet Care Tips', 20 hardcoded bullets in 4 H2 sections, plus visible chips 'pet care tips animal trivia dog facts cat behavior reptile care happy pets exotic animals fun facts pet health' (src/pages/AnimalFacts.jsx:55-58 and :95, rendered as <span>s, not links). It is indexable and in the sitemap. Its bullet 'Ball pythons can go months without eating...' is fact #39 on /facts/. (3) /fact-files/, label 'Fact files': '39 files · Page 1 of 4', long myth-busting features 'checked against 226 primary sources', every one a /blog/ article. (4) The 'Fun Facts' article topic in the menu's Article topics list (Navbar.jsx:318-320, from src/lib/data/categories.js:20 `to: '/fact-files/'`) goes to Fact files. On /categories/ the H2 'Fun Facts' links to /facts/ and the 'Fun Facts' card links to /fact-files/. (5) /gallery/, label 'Gallery': the same 347 fact photos ('All 347 of them are in the gallery' on the homepage), noindex.
findings.scope: Menu 'Learn something wild' group (5 items), footer 'Learn something wild' column (7 items), menu Article topics, and /categories/
findings.fix: 301 /animal-facts/ to /facts/, then drop it from the footer and generate-sitemap.js. Rename the 'Fun Facts' topic label to 'Fact files' so one name means one place. Present Gallery as a view of Facts rather than a separate sibling.

findings.title: Encyclopedia, Care guides and Beastlypedia: two indexes share the 'Care Guides' name
findings.claim: The nav lists 'Care guides' and 'Encyclopedia' as separate siblings. The /encyclopedia/ index, however, is titled 'Encyclopedia & Care Guides' and shares a tab toggle with /guides/, which is titled 'Care Guides'. A third profile set, Beastlypedia, sits in a different nav group. A visitor cannot tell from the labels which '-pedia' covers pets and which covers wild animals, or why a species has two pages. Visitors see this on both desktop and mobile. Google sees two index titles both claiming 'Care Guides'.
findings.evidence: Live curl: /guides/ has title 'Care Guides | Beastly Facts', H1 'Care Guides' and 108 unique species links. /encyclopedia/ has title and H1 'Encyclopedia & Care Guides' and 103 /encyclopedia/animal/ links. Both pages render the same toggle '{Encyclopedia -> /encyclopedia/} {Care Guides -> /guides/}'. /beastlypedia/ has H1 'Beastlypedia' and 43 wild-animal entries ('No care sheets, no difficulty ratings'). The same species has two URLs with different content: /guides/bearded-dragon/ (care: 'The first week', 'Emergency card') and /encyclopedia/animal/bearded-dragon/ (natural history: Overview, Quick Facts, History, 'Compare vs' 100+ animals). Nav placement: Care guides and Encyclopedia sit under 'Keep a pet' (Navbar.jsx:306, Footer.jsx:42-50), Beastlypedia under 'Learn something wild' (Navbar.jsx:324). The /animal-facts/ CTA labels /encyclopedia/ 'Encyclopedia & Care Guides' (AnimalFacts.jsx:142-144).
findings.scope: /encyclopedia/, /guides/ and /beastlypedia/ indexes plus the menu and footer labels; 211 species URLs split across two trees
findings.fix: Retitle /encyclopedia/ as a pet species encyclopedia, without '& Care Guides'. Label the nav items so the split is explicit, for example 'Pet encyclopedia' and 'Wild animals (Beastlypedia)'.

findings.title: Homepage and mobile chrome do not route to the legal tool, the store or quizzes
findings.claim: The homepage body has no link to the exotic pet law tool or the care-package store. On mobile the header 'Laws' link is hidden, so from the homepage the legal tool takes three actions: open the menu, scroll inside it, tap 'Is it legal?'. Quizzes first appear about 10.8 screens down the mobile homepage. Real visitors see this, and it is worst on mobile. On desktop 'Laws' is one click from the header.
findings.evidence: curl https://beastlyfacts.com/: href="/exotic-pet-laws/" appears 2 times, the header 'Laws' (Navbar.jsx:219 `hidden md:flex`, so desktop only) and the footer 'Is it legal?'. /care-packages/ appears once, in the footer. The hero line '...on setup, diet, health, handling, cost, and the law' is not linked. A 390x844 render of the live homepage HTML gives a document 12,012px tall with no body link to /exotic-pet-laws/, /care-packages/ or /search/. The footer starts at 10,975px, the 'Test Yourself' quiz H2 is at 9,148px and 'View all quizzes' at 10,061px. With the menu open at 390px, 13 of 27 links fit above the tab bar (Care guides through Quizzes). 'Is it legal?' (Tools group) and 'Search' need a scroll. The legal section is 137 of 1,327 sitemap URLs. Clicks from the homepage: species hub 1 for the 11 spotlighted species, otherwise 2 (Guides tab, then species). Deep dive 1 ('Today's reads'). Search 1 (header icon, see the overlay finding). Store 2 (menu, then Care packages). Quiz 2 (menu, then Quizzes) or a long scroll.
findings.scope: Homepage on mobile, plus the mobile header and menu on every page
findings.fix: Link 'the law' in the hero line to /exotic-pet-laws/, add a legal and store entry to the homepage 'Beastly Hub' block, and move the Tools group (Is it legal?, Search) to the top of the mobile menu.

findings.title: Mobile bottom tabs spend a slot on an empty My Pack and have no Home or Laws
findings.claim: The four mobile tabs are Guides, Facts, Articles and My Pack. For a first-time visitor My Pack is an empty collection. No tab reaches the homepage or the legal tool, and on guide hubs the logo is hidden too. This affects real visitors on mobile only.
findings.evidence: src/components/layout/BottomTabs.jsx:6-11: /guides/ 'Guides', /facts/ 'Facts', /blog/ 'Articles', /pack/ 'My Pack'. Live /pack/ prerender: H1 'My Beast Pack', then 'Your pack is empty! Go explore some facts and tap the heart...'. A 390px render of / and /guides/bearded-dragon/ shows exactly those 4 tab links. My Pack is also reachable from the menu (Navbar.jsx:336) and the footer (Footer.jsx 'The site' column), so the tab duplicates it.
findings.scope: Every page on mobile (under 768px)
findings.fix: Replace the My Pack tab with Laws or Home, and leave My Pack in the menu and footer.

findings.title: Site search misses multi-word queries and never returns legal pages or facts
findings.claim: Search matches the whole query as one substring, so natural queries like 'octopus hearts' or 'fennec fox legal' return 0 results even though matching pages exist. The index also leaves out all 137 exotic-pet-law pages and the 347 facts. The homepage 'Beastly Hub' box calls itself the place 'Everything on the site starts here' but searches article titles only. Real visitors see this on both devices. Separately, and only Google sees it, the WebSite SearchAction target answers with HTTP 404.
findings.evidence: src/lib/localSearch.js:25-29 `lower.includes(v)` with v = the whole query. Search.jsx:57-59 uses the same logic for articles. localSearch.js:279 returns only guides, encyclopedia, glossary, beastlypedia and articles. Live JS via the localhost proxy at /search/<q>/: 'octopus hearts' gave '0 results', while 'octopus' gave '3 results' including /blog/the-octopus-has-three-hearts-and-uses-all-of-them/. 'fennec fox legal' gave '0 results', while 'fennec fox' found /blog/fennec-fox-legal-guide/. 'texas exotic pet laws' gave '0 results'. No query returned an /exotic-pet-laws/ URL. Homepage box: CategoryBrowse.jsx:116 (heading copy) and :90-94 (submits to /blog/?search=, placeholder 'Search articles by title...'). Google-only: App.jsx:185 targets /search/{q}/, and curl https://beastlyfacts.com/search/gecko/ returns 404 with <title>Page Not Found. The client still renders results after load, so visitors are unaffected by the 404.
findings.scope: /search/ on all devices, the desktop header popover, and the homepage hub search box
findings.fix: Split the query into words and require every word to match (AND) in title, excerpt or tags. Add the /exotic-pet-laws/ animal and state pages to the local index. Point the homepage hub box at /search/.

findings.title: One destination, several labels and nav groups across header, menu, tabs and footer
findings.claim: The same page often has different names depending on where it is linked from, and three items sit in different groups in the menu and the footer. Some page H1s match none of the nav labels. Visitors see this on both devices.
findings.evidence: /guides/: 'Guides' in the header and tab, 'Care guides' in the menu and footer. /blog/: 'Articles' on every nav surface, but the page H1 is 'The Critter Digest' on /blog/ and on /blog/category/wild-animals/, and the homepage also uses 'Critter Digest' as the name of the email newsletter (H2 'Critter Digest', 'An occasional email...'). /exotic-pet-laws/: 'Laws' in the header, 'Is it legal?' in the menu (Tools) and footer (The site, Footer.jsx:86). /donate/: 'Donate' button, 'Support us' in the menu (Navbar.jsx:342). /gear/: 'Gear' in the menu, 'Recommended gear' in the footer (Footer.jsx:47), and 'Product Picks' in Article topics (categories.js:24). /feed/: 'Feed' under Tools in the menu, 'The feed' under Learn something wild in the footer (Footer.jsx:69). /pack/: 'My Pack' in nav, H1 'My Beast Pack'. My Pack sits under Tools in the menu and under The site in the footer.
findings.scope: Header, menu, bottom tabs and footer on every page
findings.fix: Pick one label and one group per destination, use them on all four surfaces, and make the /blog/ H1 match the nav label or the other way round.

findings.title: Homepage first screen splits pet owners from wild-animal readers
findings.claim: The hero names both audiences and gives each a single CTA inside the first phone screen. The daily Beastle game, which serves the kid and player audience, appears about two screens down.
findings.evidence: Live homepage: H1 'Wild facts. Pet care. We looked it up. So you don't have to.' with 'Show me something wild' going to /facts/ and 'Browse care guides' going to /guides/. In a 390x844 render of the live HTML these links sit at y=556 and y=612, inside the first 788px above the tab bar. The 'Today's Beastle' teaser link is at y=1,933.
findings.scope: Homepage, all devices

findings.title: Guide hubs fan out to every deep dive, the matching store package, laws and encyclopedia
findings.claim: A species hub works as a router to its own content cluster. This is how the store and the legal tool are reached from the pages search visitors actually land on.
findings.evidence: Live /guides/bearded-dragon/: 17 rows of 'The first week' link to 10 unique deep dives. 'Where to go next' lists 11 /blog/bearded-dragon-* deep dives. The page also links /care-packages/bearded-dragon/ (plus #sample), /exotic-pet-laws/ (2 times) and /encyclopedia/animal/bearded-dragon/.
findings.scope: /guides/<id>/ hubs (sampled 1 of 108)

findings.title: Every nav destination resolves, and no route is orphaned by accident
findings.claim: Every link on the header, menu, bottom tabs and footer returns 200 with no redirect hop, and so does every Article-topic link. The routes that no nav surface links are all deliberate.
findings.evidence: curl of 29 unique nav destinations (from Navbar.jsx, BottomTabs.jsx and Footer.jsx): all '200 0'. All 18 Article-topic destinations (16 /blog/category/* plus /fact-files/ and /gear/): 200 with 0 redirects. 13 of 41 static routes in App.jsx appear on no nav surface, and each is accounted for. Redirects: /chronicles/ to /chronicles/dex/, /trivia/ to /quiz/trivia/ and /encyclopedia/guides/ to /guides/, each 200 after 1 hop. Transactional: /donate/success, /donate/cancel, /care-packages/thanks. Private: /composer, /composer/login. Reached from their hub: /exotic-pet-laws/map/ and /state/, plus /care-packages/store/, /faq/ and /why-we-exist/ (the /care-packages/ page links /care-packages/store/ 3 times).
findings.scope: All nav surfaces

nav-behavior.notCheckable: Headless Chromium cannot load the live site from this sandbox (TLS interception), so every client-side behavior was derived from code, not observed in a browser. That covers: history.length after a real Google click, what the back buttons actually do, the hydration fallback that turns /blog/<bad-slug>/ into the listing after the 404.html is served, focus movement in the mobile menu, rendered tap-target pixel sizes, and whether the custom edge-swipe in useSwipeBack.js doubles up with iOS Safari's native swipe-back. I did not run a local dev server, because Vite writes its cache into the repo's node_modules and this lane is read-only. I had no Search Console or analytics access, so I could not say what share of guide hub or encyclopedia visits are cold landings from search. Breadcrumb checks covered all 1327 sitemap URLs fetched on Oct 19, 2026 (6 transient connection resets were retried and returned 200). Pages outside the sitemap (noindex routes such as /pack/, /search/ and /donate/success/) were not swept.

findings.title: Back to Guides and Back to Encyclopedia send search visitors back to Google
findings.claim: The labeled in-page back buttons on guide hubs and encyclopedia pages, and the mobile header Back button that replaces the logo on guide hubs, all run history back (navigate(-1)) instead of going to the page they name. For a visitor who clicked a Google result in the same tab, they leave the site. For an in-app arrival they go to whatever page came before, such as Home or an article, not to /guides/. The header Back has no guard at all, so in a fresh tab it does nothing. Visitors see this on both desktop and mobile: the in-page buttons appear on both, the header Back on mobile only.
findings.evidence: src/pages/GuideDetail.jsx:74-86 handleBack: `if (window.history.length > 1) { navigate(-1); return; } navigate('/guides/');` with a static label at :338 `Back to Guides`. src/pages/EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:58-70 has the same logic, with a static label at :164 `Back to Encyclopedia`. src/components/layout/MobileBackButton.jsx:24 `onClick={() => navigate(-1)}` has no check at all. src/components/layout/Navbar.jsx:192 `isChildRoute = /^\/guides\/(?!category\/).+/`, :208 gives the logo `hidden md:flex` on those routes, and :211-213 puts MobileBackButton in its place. MDN (curl developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/History/length/index.json): history.length "returns an integer representing the number of entries in the session history, including the currently loaded page. For example, for a page loaded in a new tab this property returns 1." A Google results page in the same tab is one of those entries, so the check passes and navigate(-1) returns to Google. Live: curl https://beastlyfacts.com/guides/axolotl/ contains `<button aria-label="Go back" ...>Back</button>` and `<button type="button" ...> Back to Guides</button>`, and /encyclopedia/animal/axolotl/ contains `Back to Encyclopedia`. repro.correctedClaim:
The core of the finding is real. A visitor who reaches a guide hub or encyclopedia page from a search result in the same tab and clicks "Back to Guides" or "Back to Encyclopedia" is sent back to the search page. This happens on desktop and on mobile, on all 108 guide hubs and all 103 encyclopedia animal pages. Three details need correcting.

(1) The handlers do not go straight to navigate(-1). They first follow location.state.returnTo (GuideDetail.jsx:75-79, EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:59-63). Visitors who arrive from the /guides/ or /encyclopedia/ lists land on the list URL, which is correct. The wrong destination only affects arrivals with no state: search results, Home's GuideSpotlight, DeepDiveList, Gear, the care package pages and similar. A separate mislabel also exists: the cross-links between the two sections pass returnTo for the other section. As a result, "Back to Guides" after the encyclopedia's care-guide link goes to /encyclopedia/ (EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:297), and GuideDetail.jsx:649 does the reverse.

(2) The mobile header Back calls navigate(-1) with no guard. In a true fresh tab (history.length 1) it does nothing. But it is also mostly covered by the Toaster's ToastProvider, a plain div styled "fixed top-0 z-[100] ... w-full p-4" (toast.jsx:6-12). On mobile this div covers the top 32px of the screen, while the button spans y 10 to 46. Taps at y 14 to 31, which includes the center of the "Back" label, hit the overlay and do nothing. Only taps at y 34 to 40 reach the button and return to the search page. The same overlay blocks the centers of the mobile logo, Search, dark mode and menu buttons.

(3) The in-page buttons fall back to /guides/ and /encyclopedia/ correctly in a fresh tab.
repro.evidence:
I tested the live site through a local mirror: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-beastlyfactss/c6c3a501-5606-5a8b-b8c9-191dbbf9547e/scratchpad/verify-back/proxy.cjs serves the curl'd beastlyfacts.com HTML and JS on localhost:4501, and localhost:4502 is a fake search page linking to it. I drove it with puppeteer headless Chromium (repro.cjs, repro3.cjs, repro4.cjs in the same folder). Results:
- Desktop: search page, then /guides/axolotl/, then "Back to Guides": final URL http://localhost:4502/?q=/guides/axolotl/. On arrival, history.length was 3 and history.state was {"idx":0}, with no returnTo.
- Mobile (390x844): same result for "Back to Guides". "Back to Encyclopedia" on /encyclopedia/animal/axolotl/ also returns to the search page on both desktop and mobile.
- Mobile header Back: elementFromPoint at the button's center gives `DIV.fixed top-0 z-[100] flex max-h-screen w-...`. The button rect is y 10 to 46. Taps at y=14, 22, 28 and 31 left the URL at /guides/axolotl/. Taps at y=34 and 40 went to http://localhost:4502/?q=/guides/axolotl/.
- Mobile home page: the centers (y=28) of BeastlyFacts, Search, Toggle dark mode and Toggle navigation menu all report hit=false.
- True fresh tab (opened with target=_blank, history.length=1): the header Back, fired with a JS click, left the URL at /guides/axolotl/. "Back to Guides" went to /guides/.
- In-app arrivals: Home, then a link to /guides/dog-large-breed/ (state=null), then "Back to Guides" ends at http://localhost:4501/. From the /guides/ list (state {"returnTo":"/guides/"}), "Back to Guides" ends at /guides/. From the /encyclopedia/ list, "Back to Encyclopedia" ends at /encyclopedia/. From the encyclopedia page's care-guide link (state {"returnTo":"/encyclopedia/"}), "Back to Guides" ends at /encyclopedia/.

Code:

- EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:58-70 and label at 164.
- MobileBackButton.jsx:24 `onClick={() => navigate(-1)}`.
- Navbar.jsx:192, 208, 211-212.
- toast.jsx:6-12 (ToastProvider) and 15-21 (ToastViewport). Both are plain divs with `fixed top-0 z-[100] ... w-full ... p-4`, mounted at App.jsx:237. Live HTML for /guides/axolotl/ contains the nested pair.
- returnTo setters: BrowseRow.jsx:110, Guides.jsx:186 and 293, Encyclopedia.jsx:241, 364 and 469, GuideDetail.jsx:649, EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:297. Hub links with no state: GuideSpotlight.jsx:101, DeepDiveList.jsx:132, Gear.jsx:53, CarePackageProduct.jsx:493.

All 108 hubs returned 200. 108 of 108 contain aria-label="Go back", "Back to Guides" and the logo class "hidden md:flex". 103 of 103 encyclopedia animal pages returned 200 and contain "Back to Encyclopedia", and 0 of 103 have the header Go back.

repro.fix:
In GuideDetail.jsx and EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx handleBack, use returnTo only when it points into the section the label names. Otherwise make the label follow returnTo. With no such state, navigate('/guides/') or navigate('/encyclopedia/'), and drop the bare history.length > 1 fallback. Keep navigate(-1) only when location.state proves the list page is the previous entry, so its scroll position is restored.

In MobileBackButton.jsx, call navigate('/guides/') when location.key === 'default'. That value marks the first SPA entry, which covers both a fresh tab and a search arrival. Otherwise call navigate(-1).

Separately, stop the toast container from blocking taps. In toast.jsx, make ToastProvider a fragment, or not a fixed padded div. Add pointer-events-none to the viewport; the toasts already carry pointer-events-auto in toastVariants. Without this the header Back, logo, search and menu buttons stay partly untappable on mobile, whatever the back logic does.

impact.correctedClaim:
"Back to Guides" (all 108 of 108 guide hubs) and "Back to Encyclopedia" (all 103 of 103 encyclopedia animal pages) are in-page buttons that visitors see on both desktop and mobile. When the visitor has no location.state.returnTo, both run navigate(-1) whenever window.history.length > 1. A visitor who opened a Google result in the same tab has that guard pass, so the button takes them back to Google instead of the page it names. That part is real.

Two parts of the finding are overstated.

1. In-app arrivals. Both handlers check location.state.returnTo before anything else. Every row on the guide listing and its category pages, every guide row on the encyclopedia listing, the Care Guides/Encyclopedia tabs and the hub/encyclopedia toggle pass returnTo. Visitors arriving from those go to the listing they came from, not through history. Only arrivals with no returnTo (Home, articles, search, navbar) step back to the previous page, which is a label mismatch but keeps them on the site.

2. The mobile header button. It is labeled only "Back", not with a destination, and appears only on the 108 hubs (md:hidden, mobile only, 0 of 103 encyclopedia pages). Going back through history is the expected behavior for a generic Back, the same as the browser's back. Its one real defect: it is unguarded, so with no earlier entry in the tab (a result opened in a new tab, a direct visit, a shared link) the click does nothing.

Only visitors notice this. Google is unaffected. Severity is medium, not high: it hits only visitors who arrive from another site in the same tab and then press the in-page button, and there is no analytics data to size it.
impact.evidence: Code (read myself): - src/pages/GuideDetail.jsx:74-86 is handleBack. It reads `const returnTo = location.state?.returnTo; if (returnTo) { navigate(returnTo); return; }` first, then `if (window.history.length > 1) { navigate(-1); return; } navigate('/guides/');`. The label is at :338 `Back to Guides`, and :333-337 has no responsive hiding class, so it shows at every width. - src/pages/EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:58-70 has the same shape with returnTo first and the /encyclopedia/ fallback. The label is at :164. - src/components/layout/MobileBackButton.jsx:24 is `onClick={() => navigate(-1)}` with no guard. The visible text is "Back". - src/components/layout/Navbar.jsx:192 is `isChildRoute = /^\/guides\/(?!category\/).+/`. At :208 the logo is `hidden md:flex` on those routes, and :211-213 renders MobileBackButton inside a `md:hidden` wrapper. The finding's evidence quoted handleBack without the returnTo branch. Callers that pass returnTo: - src/components/shared/BrowseRow.jsx:110 ``, used for every guide row at src/pages/Guides.jsx:285-293 with returnTo '/guides/' or the category URL. - src/pages/Encyclopedia.jsx:461 (guide rows) and :364/:469. - The tabs at Guides.jsx:186 and Encyclopedia.jsx:241. - The hub/encyclopedia toggle at GuideDetail.jsx:649 and EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:297. Router: package.json:47 has react-router-dom ^6.26.0, installed as react-router 6.30.6. node_modules/@remix-run/router/dist/router.cjs.js:249 builds the browser location key as `globalHistory.state && globalHistory.state.key || "default"`, so a fresh page load (from Google or in a new tab) has location.key "default". `grep -rn "location.key|history.length" src` returns only useSwipeBack.js:31, GuideDetail.jsx:81 and EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:65, so location.key is used nowhere. MDN via curl of developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/History/length/index.json returned "for a page loaded in a new tab this property returns 1." Legal-pages pattern: src/pages/ExoticPetLawsState.jsx:65 `const backToHub = location.state?.from === 'legal-hub' ? '/exotic-pet-laws/' : null;` feeds Breadcrumbs historyBackFor, and src/components/shared/Breadcrumbs.jsx:57-63 runs navigate(-1) only in that case. Live sweep: - curl of https://beastlyfacts.com/sitemap.xml gave 1327 URLs. Of those, 108 match /guides// excluding category pages, and 103 match /encyclopedia/animal//. - Fetched all 211 with xargs -P4. 208 returned 200 on the first pass and 3 failed with SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL; a retry returned 200 for all 3. - Hubs: 108 of 108 contain both `aria-label="Go back"` and `Back to Guides`. - Encyclopedia pages: 103 of 103 contain `Back to Encyclopedia`, and 0 of 103 contain `Go back`. - Sample snippet from /guides/axolotl/: ``. What I could not check: I did not click through in a real browser (headless Chromium cannot load external pages here), and I have no analytics on how many visitors arrive from Google in the same tab or press these buttons.
impact.fix:
Keep the existing returnTo branch in both handlers. It is deliberate: the hub/encyclopedia toggle forwards it so Back returns to the listing the reader started from.

In src/pages/GuideDetail.jsx:81 and src/pages/EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:65, replace the `window.history.length > 1` guard with `location.key !== 'default'`. That stops history back only on an entry loaded fresh in the tab, which covers Google in the same tab, a new tab and a direct visit. Those cases then fall through to navigate('/guides/') or navigate('/encyclopedia/'). This two-line change removes the site exit, which is the part that matters.

Whether to also stop history back for in-app arrivals without returnTo (from an article or from Home) is a label/UX choice for the owner. Those visitors stay on the site. If the owner wants the label honored literally, drop the navigate(-1) branch entirely and push the named URL. Do not rewrite the handlers as plain "go to the named URL" without keeping returnTo.

In src/components/layout/MobileBackButton.jsx:24, use `onClick={() => (location.key === 'default' ? navigate('/guides/') : navigate(-1))}`. useLocation is already imported. Keep history back otherwise, because a bare "Back" is expected to behave like the browser's back.

Leave src/lib/hooks/useSwipeBack.js alone. An edge swipe is the browser-back gesture, so exiting to the referrer there is expected.

No build or content changes are needed.

findings.title: 1,056 pages declare a breadcrumb trail that visitors never see
findings.claim: Articles, guide hubs, encyclopedia pages and Beastfiles all emit BreadcrumbList JSON-LD, but none shows a visible trail. Visible breadcrumbs appear only on the 136 legal pages. A shared Breadcrumbs component already exists, built to take the same [name, path] array as breadcrumbSchema(), but only the three legal page components use it. Google's structured data policy asks that markup describe content visible to readers. Visitors also miss the 'where am I' cue that Google shows in the result they clicked, for example Care Guides > Ball Python > Feeding guide.
findings.evidence: Sweep of all 1327 sitemap URLs (scratchpad scripts/analyze.py). BreadcrumbList JSON-LD with no visible trail: article 802/802, guide-hub 108/108, encyclopedia-animal 103/103, beastfile 43/43. Visible `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">`: laws-animal 82/82, laws-state 52/52, laws-map 1/1, laws-state-index 1/1, and 0 on every other type. `<Breadcrumbs` is used only at ExoticPetLaws.jsx:329, ExoticPetLawsState.jsx:232 and ExoticPetLawsStateIndex.jsx:96. Trails already built for the schema: GuideDetail.jsx:259-262, EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:118-121, BeastfileDetail.jsx:100-103, Blog.jsx:974-983. Google (curl developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/sd-policies): "Don't mark up content that is not visible to readers of the page." src/components/shared/Breadcrumbs.jsx:7-10 says it takes the same array as breadcrumbSchema() "so ... the row a reader sees and the structured data a crawler reads cannot drift apart".
findings.scope: 1056 of 1327 sitemap URLs. Visitors on mobile and desktop see the gap, and Google reads the markup.
findings.fix: Render <Breadcrumbs trail={...}> from the same trail arrays in GuideDetail, EncyclopediaAnimal, BeastfileDetail and the Blog article view, in place of or above the current Back row.

findings.title: Breadcrumb JSON-LD is clean everywhere it appears
