findings.title: Legal section: three hub URLs and 82 animal pairs share one search intent
findings.claim: Three indexable hubs all open their title with 'Exotic Pet Laws by State:', and two of them share the same H1. Separately, each of the 82 animals in the legal matrix has two indexable, cross-linked pages answering 'is X legal in my state': /exotic-pet-laws/<id>/ and /blog/<id>-legal-guide/. Their body text is distinct, so this is not duplicate content. The risk is that Google splits impressions between near-synonymous titles. findings.evidence: /exotic-pet-laws/: 'Exotic Pet Laws by State: What Is Actually Banned', H1 'Exotic pet laws, state by state' (ExoticPetLawsHub.jsx:48, :76). /exotic-pet-laws/map/: 'Exotic Pet Laws by State: An Interactive US Map', H1 'Exotic pet laws, state by state' (ExoticPetLaws.jsx:249, :333). /exotic-pet-laws/state/: 'Exotic Pet Laws by State: All 50 States Ranked', H1 'Exotic pet laws by state' (ExoticPetLawsStateIndex.jsx:40, :99). findings.fix: Give the three hubs distinct titles and H1s by job (overview, map, pick a state). Lead the map with 'Interactive map' and the state index with 'Pick a state'. Leave the 82 pairs as they are until Search Console shows whether one URL of a pair is suppressing the other.

Visitors on mobile and desktop land on a 'Reptiles' page whose heading reads 'The Critter Digest'. Google gets 16 blog category descriptions that differ by one word. On the Wild Animals page the template reads 'care guides, deep dives, pet laws, wild animals and more', and two slug-derived titles read 'Small And Exotic Pets Articles' and 'Turtles And Tortoises Articles'.

findings.title: Article lastmod tracks editorial changes, not build time
findings.claim: For articles, sitemap lastmod comes from the frontmatter lastUpdated, falling back to the publish date. It matches the page's own JSON-LD dateModified, and it is not restamped on deploy. Static and listing pages deliberately carry no lastmod instead of a fake build date.
findings.evidence: generate-sitemap.js:157 `lastmod: readLastUpdated(post) || post.date || null`, and the comment at :293-296 ('Category and static pages carry no lastmod: stamping them with the build date on every deploy makes the signal meaningless'). Across all 802 blog URLs: 'blog lastmod != frontmatter(lastUpdated||date): 0'. The sitemap holds 60 distinct lastmod values (2026-06-10 to 2026-10-17), not one build date. In a random sample of 20 articles (seed 7, e.g. gerbil-health-issues-guide, caiman-legal-guide, crested-gecko-humidity-guide), 20 of 20 had sitemap lastmod = frontmatter value = live JSON-LD dateModified. Git history is shallow (80 commits, earliest 2026-10-12), so post-edit checking is limited. 2 of the 20 files changed after their lastUpdated, and both changes were non-editorial: '+<CarePackageBlock animal="axolotl" variant="feeding" />' (commit 2ebf67c) and an 'animalDay' frontmatter key (b484f89). That fits docs/RULES.md:185-187 (navigation-only edits do not bump lastUpdated).
findings.scope: 802 article URLs

findings.title: 525 sitemap URLs have no lastmod, including 136 legal pages that do carry real verification dates
findings.claim: Only the 802 article URLs carry lastmod. The 108 guide hubs, 103 encyclopedia profiles, 83 legal animal pages, 53 state pages, 43 Beastfiles and 38 Chronicles parts have none. For the legal pages this wastes a real signal. Every jurisdiction entry has a verifiedOn date, and 52 of 53 state pages already show visitors a 'Last reviewed' line, but Google gets no hint from the sitemap when those time-sensitive pages are re-verified.
findings.evidence: Sitemap parse: with lastmod Counter({'blog': 802}); without lastmod: guides 109, encyclopedia/animal 103, exotic-pet-laws 84, exotic-pet-laws/state 53, beastlypedia 44, chronicles 38, plus listings and statics (525 total). legalStatus.json jurisdiction keys: ['status', 'sourceId', 'cite', 'quote', 'note', 'verifiedOn', 'localOverride']. ExoticPetLawsState.jsx:110-114 builds the visible verified line from verifiedOn. Live /exotic-pet-laws/ferret/ text contains 'verified 1 October 2026'. None of the 108 guide hubs or 103 encyclopedia pages exposes dateModified in JSON-LD (0 of 108, 0 of 103), and src/lib/data/guides/*.js has no date field (0 of 12 files match lastReviewed|lastUpdated). The lastmod emitter only runs for blogCategoryPages, mdxPostPages and chroniclesPages (generate-sitemap.js:329-341). Google-only.
findings.scope: 525 of 1327 URLs; 136 legal pages are the ones with data ready
findings.fix: In generate-sitemap.js, emit lastmod for each /exotic-pet-laws/<id>/ and /exotic-pet-laws/state/<slug>/ URL from the newest verifiedOn among its entries, and for each Chronicles part from its MDX date.

findings.title: Redirects are single-hop and URL normalization is tight
findings.claim: Every redirect rule lands on a 200 in one hop, slashless and index.html URLs reach the canonical in one 308 hop, query strings and double slashes canonicalize to the clean URL, and every internal page link is already lowercase with a trailing slash, so internal navigation never triggers a redirect.
findings.evidence: public/_redirects: 224 rules, all 301. 223 literal sources traced live: '223 hops=1 final=200'. Every final URL equals the declared target, and every target is in the sitemap except /gear/ (noindex by design). Splat /encyclopedia/guides/geckos/ -> 301 -> /guides/category/geckos/ 200. https://beastlyfacts.com/guides/bearded-dragon -> 308 -> .../bearded-dragon/ 200; /index.html -> 308 -> / ; /guides/bearded-dragon/index.html -> 308 -> /guides/bearded-dragon/. '/guides/bearded-dragon/?utm_source=x', '//guides/bearded-dragon/', '/blog/?page=2' and '/facts/?cat=birds' all return canonical to the clean URL. Internal hrefs across the 1327 crawled pages: no uppercase page links, and no slashless page links apart from fonts, assets and /cdn-cgi/l/email-protection. Uppercase variants (/Guides/Bearded-Dragon/, /BLOG/) return 404 rather than redirecting, which is acceptable since nothing on the site links to them.
findings.scope: Site-wide

findings.title: /care-packages/store/ is indexable but left out of the sitemap, contradicting the sitemap's own note
findings.claim: generate-sitemap.js says the store page carries noindex,follow and leaves it out for that reason, but the page component sets no robots tag. The live page is indexable, linked from 21 sitemap pages, and missing from the sitemap. It is the only one of 115 prerendered routes outside the sitemap that is indexable; the other 114 are noindex.
findings.evidence: generate-sitemap.js:199-205: 'the three /care-packages/ subpages (store, why-we-exist, faq). Each carries noindex,follow in its page component.' src/pages/CarePackagesStore.jsx:34-50 Helmet has title, description, canonical and OG tags but no robots meta. Siblings do: CarePackagesFaq.jsx:62 and CarePackagesWhyWeExist.jsx:19 '<meta name="robots" content="noindex,follow" />'. Live: /care-packages/store/ 200, robots meta NONE, header 'x-robots-tag: max-image-preview:large' only. Check of 115 prerendered non-sitemap routes (/gear/*, /gallery/, /feed/, /pack/, /terms/, /privacy/, care-package subpages, etc.): 106 'noindex,follow', 5 'noindex, follow', 1 'noindex, nofollow', 1 NONE (the store). Output: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-beastlyfactss/c6c3a501-5606-5a8b-b8c9-191dbbf9547e/scratchpad/seo-crawl/nonsitemap_check.tsv. Google-only.
findings.scope: 1 page
findings.fix: Add <meta name="robots" content="noindex,follow" /> to the Helmet in CarePackagesStore.jsx, matching the sitemap note and the FAQ and Why We Exist pages.

findings.title: Encyclopedia and Beastfile snippets end mid-sentence; Beastlypedia titles misspell the brand
findings.claim: Most encyclopedia profile and Beastfile meta descriptions are cut at a word boundary with an ellipsis, so search results show a broken sentence. Encyclopedia titles all follow a generic 'X - Encyclopedia' pattern, and every Beastlypedia title spells the brand 'BeastlyFacts' while the rest of the site uses 'Beastly Facts'.
findings.evidence: 61 of 103 /encyclopedia/animal/ descriptions and 32 of 43 Beastfile descriptions end in '…'. Example: /encyclopedia/animal/axolotl/ 'The axolotl is a neotenic salamander - a species that retains larval features (gills, aquatic lifestyle) permanently throughout its adult life, never…'. Cause: src/lib/utils/truncate.js:21-24 falls back to a word cut plus '…' when no sentence ends between 110 and 160 characters; called from EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:115 (bio.overview) and BeastfileDetail.jsx:109. 102 of 103 encyclopedia titles are '<Name> - Encyclopedia | Beastly Facts' (EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:110). 50 of 1327 titles contain 'BeastlyFacts': BeastfileDetail.jsx:108 `${name} | Beastlypedia | BeastlyFacts` and Beastlypedia.jsx:81-82. Google-only (search snippet and tab title).
findings.scope: 93 descriptions, 103 encyclopedia titles, 50 Beastlypedia titles
findings.fix: Add a hand-written metaDescription field (150 to 160 characters, complete sentences) to the encyclopedia and Beastfile data and use it before the truncated overview. Change 'BeastlyFacts' to 'Beastly Facts' in BeastfileDetail.jsx:108 and Beastlypedia.jsx:81-82.

findings.title: Quiz and game pages in the sitemap prerender as near-empty start screens
findings.claim: Measured by words of prerendered <main> text, 38 of 1327 sitemap URLs are under 300 words. Every one is a listing, a quiz or a game, not an article. The weakest are the 8 quiz detail pages, which give Google only a title, a 'Start Quiz' button and a list of study links, because the questions load client-side. Content pages are healthy: articles start at 673 words, guide hubs at 1044, encyclopedia profiles at 1017 and legal animal pages at 1031. Beastfiles are the lightest content type (min 333, median 463).
findings.evidence: Main-text word counts (scripts, styles and SVG removed): quiz detail n 8 min 69 median 76 max 86 (e.g. /quiz/bearded-dragon-boss/ 69, /quiz/knowledge/ 73, /quiz/personality/ 73); /quiz/ 193; /critter-keeper/ 139; /beastle/ 298; /contact/ 196; encyclopedia/category 82 to 142; beastlypedia/group 95 to 345; guides/category 125 to 295. Live main text of /quiz/bearded-dragon-boss/: 'All quizzes | Quiz #1 · Aug 31, 2026 | ... | 8 Questions | Sourced Answers | ... | Start Quiz | Study up first (or after) | ...'. Quiz URLs come from generate-sitemap.js:227-230. Visible to Google only. Visitors get the full interactive quiz.
findings.scope: 8 quiz pages plus 3 app pages; listing pages covered in other findings
findings.fix: Prerender each themed quiz's question list (questions plus the source page each answer comes from) below the start button, so the static HTML carries the substance the description promises.

findings.title: http://www requests take three hops to reach a canonical URL
findings.claim: Host normalization is chained, not direct. http://www goes to https://www, then to the apex, then to the trailing-slash URL. Everything still resolves, but the link equity of old www or http backlinks passes through extra hops.
findings.evidence: Live traces: 'http://www.beastlyfacts.com/guides/bearded-dragon -> 301 https://www.beastlyfacts.com/guides/bearded-dragon -> 301 https://beastlyfacts.com/guides/bearded-dragon -> 308 https://beastlyfacts.com/guides/bearded-dragon/ -> 200'. 'http://www.beastlyfacts.com/ -> 301 https://www.beastlyfacts.com/ -> 301 https://beastlyfacts.com/ -> 200'. 'http://beastlyfacts.com/blog/bearded-dragon-cost-guide -> 301 https://... -> 308 .../bearded-dragon-cost-guide/ -> 200'. Single-hop cases: https://www.beastlyfacts.com/guides/bearded-dragon/ -> 301 -> apex 200, and http://beastlyfacts.com/ -> 301 -> https 200. Neither public/_worker.js nor public/_redirects handles the host (_routes.json sends only /feed.xml, /articles.xml, /subscribed and /api/* to the worker), so this happens at the Cloudflare zone level. Google-only.
findings.scope: Requests to www or http variants
findings.fix: In Cloudflare, make the www rule a Single Redirect that matches both schemes (http and https on www.beastlyfacts.com) and sends them straight to https://beastlyfacts.com with the path kept, so it fires before Always Use HTTPS adds a hop.

seo-structured.notCheckable: Google's Rich Results Test, Search Console enhancement reports and the Facebook Sharing Debugger were not run: a browser cannot load external sites here, and no Search Console access exists. So I could not see which site name Google currently shows ('BeastlyFacts' or 'Beastly Facts') or whether any manual action exists. Whether x.com/beastlyfacts exists is inferred only from HTTP status codes calibrated against a made-up handle; X serves its profile pages through JavaScript. I did not check what a visitor sees at /search/axolotl/ after client-side hydration, only that the server returns 404. Visible store prices were checked on 3 of 20 product pages; the markup price was checked on all 20. For pages outside the 79-page sample, image dimensions were read from the files in public/ rather than downloaded live; 24 live downloads in the sample matched that method. I did not compare hub and encyclopedia descriptions against visible text beyond spot checks.

findings.title: Article dateModified is a date no reader can see
findings.claim: On 533 of 802 live articles, BlogPosting.dateModified differs from the only modified-type date shown on the page (the 'Last reviewed' line in Sources). On 523 of them the structured date is later. The frontmatter lastUpdated feeds dateModified but is never rendered, so Google gets a freshness date that has no visible equivalent. Only Google sees this.
findings.evidence: src/pages/Blog.jsx:947 sets `dateModified: post.lastUpdated || post.lastReviewed || isoPublished`, and the comment at Blog.jsx:942-943 says it is 'the same value the visible date line shows'. But the visible header renders only displayDate from publishedAt (Blog.jsx:1073), and Sources.jsx:93-97 renders lastReviewed. Live example https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/bearded-dragon-handling-guide/: JSON-LD has "datePublished": "2026-07-05", "dateModified": "2026-10-05". The visible text shows 'Jul 5, 2026' and 'Last reviewed 24 Sep 2026'. Frontmatter is date 2026-07-05, lastUpdated 2026-10-05, lastReviewed 2026-09-24. A full crawl of 1327 sitemap URLs compared dateModified with the visible 'Last reviewed' date on all 802 BlogPosting pages: 523 later, 10 earlier, 243 equal, 26 with no visible date. Google (developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/publication-dates): "Ensure that the date (and optional time and timezone) match between the equivalent user-visible and structured values." and "Label your dates appropriately with text like "Publish" or "Last updated"." All 802 datePublished values are date-only, with no time or timezone.
findings.scope: 533 of 802 indexed articles (all page types under /blog/)
findings.fix: Render a labeled 'Updated <lastUpdated>' next to the published date in the Blog.jsx header so the structured date has a visible twin, or set dateModified to lastReviewed. Optionally emit the dates with a -04:00/-05:00 Eastern offset.

findings.title: Guide hubs and encyclopedia: Organization author, no dates
findings.claim: All 108 care guide hubs and all 103 encyclopedia animal pages declare Article with author = Organization 'Beastly Facts' and no datePublished or dateModified. The 802 articles under them credit Person 'Michael Ryan'. These are the site's top species pages, and they give Google no author entity and no freshness date. They also show no byline or date to visitors. On 102 of 103 encyclopedia pages the headline carries the title-tag suffix, and the publisher has no logo. Only Google sees the markup. The missing visible byline and date affect everyone.
findings.evidence: src/pages/GuideDetail.jsx:309 `"author": { "@type": "Organization", "name": "Beastly Facts", ... }`. src/pages/EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:149 has the same author, and :150 has a publisher with no logo. :145 is `"headline": pageTitle`, which renders as "Bearded Dragon - Encyclopedia | Beastly Facts" on https://beastlyfacts.com/encyclopedia/animal/bearded-dragon/. Full-crawl counts: hub Article 108 of 108 Organization author, 108 with no datePublished, 108 with no dateModified, 0 with a visible 'Written by' or date. Encyclopedia Article 103 of 103 Organization author, 103 with no dates, 102 headlines containing '| Beastly Facts', 0 with publisher.logo. By contrast, BlogPosting author is Person on 802 of 802.
findings.scope: 211 pages: 108 /guides/<species>/ hubs and 103 /encyclopedia/animal/<species>/ pages
findings.fix: Use authorSchema() from src/lib/data/author.js for both Article blocks, add datePublished and dateModified from the guide data (with a visible 'Last reviewed' line to match), use PUBLISHER for publisher, and use the bare species title as the encyclopedia headline.

findings.title: 87 articles name a bare 'Mike' as author
findings.claim: 87 articles emit author {"@type":"Person","name":"Mike"} with no @id, url or sameAs. The visible author box on the same pages says 'Written by Michael Ryan'. The structured data therefore contradicts the visible byline and is not tied to the /about/ Person entity that the other 715 articles reference. Only Google sees this.
findings.evidence: src/lib/data/author.js:53-57: `const isKnown = !name || name === AUTHOR.name; return isKnown ? {...'@id': AUTHOR.url...} : { '@type': 'Person', name };`. The comment at author.js:51-52 says every article falls back to the profile, but `grep -rl '^author: "Mike"' content` finds 87 non-scheduled files (e.g. content/guides/border-collie-enrichment-guide.mdx:29). By category that is 75 Enrichment, 8 Dogs, 4 Cats. Full crawl: BlogPosting author names were 715 'Michael Ryan' and 87 'Mike'. All 87 'Mike' pages show 'Written by' and 'Michael Ryan' in visible text (87 of 87). Example: https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/african-grey-parrot-enrichment-guide/. Related: on /about/ the ProfilePage Person.image is a bearded dragon photo (dex-portrait.jpg), and Person.sameAs repeats the brand's four social accounts that Organization.sameAs also uses.
findings.scope: 87 of 802 articles (dog/cat health and enrichment pages, the YMYL-leaning ones)
findings.fix: In authorSchema(), treat 'Mike' as an alias of AUTHOR.name (or change the 87 frontmatter lines to 'Michael Ryan') so every article emits the same @id https://beastlyfacts.com/about/.

findings.title: Organization and publisher logo is a scenery photo
findings.claim: The site-wide Organization.logo, and the publisher.logo on every BlogPosting and hub Article, is og-default.jpg: a 1200x630 landscape photo of a bearded dragon, a lorikeet and a kangaroo with no brand mark. Google uses this image to represent the brand. A real square logo (orange 'BF' bearded dragon roundel, 512x512) is already served at /pwa/icon-512.png. Only Google sees this.
findings.evidence: src/App.jsx:198 and src/lib/data/author.js:45 both point logo at https://beastlyfacts.com/assets/og-default.jpg. GuideDetail.jsx:310 does too. Live dims measured with PIL: (1200, 630). I viewed the image and it shows no logo or wordmark. `curl -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}' https://beastlyfacts.com/pwa/icon-512.png` returned `200 image/png`, and PIL reported (512, 512). Google logo doc: "The image must be 112x112px, at minimum" and "Make sure the image looks how you intend it to look on a purely white background". The landscape meets the size floor but is not a logo. Organization appears on 1327 of 1327 pages, and publisher.logo appears on 802 BlogPosting plus 108 hub Article blocks.
findings.scope: Site-wide: 1327 pages, plus publisher on 910 article and hub pages
findings.fix: Point Organization.logo and PUBLISHER.logo (App.jsx:198, author.js:45, GuideDetail.jsx:310) at https://beastlyfacts.com/pwa/icon-512.png, or at a dedicated square logo file on a white or transparent background.

findings.title: Hero images sit 32 px under Discover's 1200 px minimum
findings.claim: The house hero size of 1168x784 is just below Google Discover's large-image minimum width. 642 of 802 articles have an og:image and BlogPosting.image narrower than 1200 px (626 at 1168x784 and 10 at 512x382), so most articles are ineligible for large Discover cards. That holds even though the max-image-preview:large header is set correctly. Only Google sees this.
findings.evidence: Dimensions of every article's og:image file, read from public/ with PIL for all 802 /blog/ articles in the full crawl: 626 (1168, 784), 34 (1200, 896), 22 (1200, 800), 20 (1600, 1067), 12 (1200, 675), 10 (512, 382) and others. Width under 1200 on 642 of 802 articles. Site-wide, 940 of 1327 pages have an og:image under 1200 wide, including all 137 legal pages (shared 1168x784 hero) and 40 of 49 Beastlypedia pages. Examples at 512x382: https://beastlyfacts.com/assets/images/degu-feeding.jpg and african-grey-parrot-feeding.jpg. Google Discover doc (developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover): large images should be "At least 1200 px wide" and enabled by the "max-image-preview:large setting". CLAUDE.md sets heroes at 1168x784.
findings.scope: 642 of 802 articles; 940 of 1327 pages overall
findings.fix: Owner decision: either move the hero standard to at least 1200 px wide (e.g. 1200x800), or keep the on-page hero and export a 1200 px-wide og/schema variant per article for og:image and BlogPosting.image. Re-shoot or replace the 10 images at 512x382.

findings.title: Animal Days FAQPage marks up text not on the page
findings.claim: /animal-days/ emits a FAQPage with three hard-coded questions and answers that appear nowhere in the visible page. That breaks Google's rule against marking up invisible content. One answer also states a fact (International Rabbit Day is the fourth Saturday in September) that exists only in the markup. FAQ rich results no longer exist, so this gains nothing and carries only manual-action risk. Only Google sees this.
findings.evidence: src/pages/AnimalDays.jsx:227-256 defines the three Questions inline, and :276 outputs them. `grep -rn 'Who decides what becomes' src` matches only AnimalDays.jsx:249. On the live https://beastlyfacts.com/animal-days/ visible text (scripts and styles stripped), 'Who decides' was not found, 'change date' was not found, and there are no 'FAQ' or 'Questions' headings. In a 79-page sample, 134 of 137 FAQPage questions appear in visible text, and the 3 misses are all on this page. Google structured data policies: "Don't mark up content that is not visible to readers of the page."
findings.scope: 1 page
findings.fix: Either render the three Q&As as a visible section on the Animal Days page or delete faqSchema from AnimalDays.jsx.

findings.title: og:image:width/height wrong on 752 pages
findings.claim: 752 of the 1247 pages that declare og:image:width/height declare the wrong size, usually 1200x630 for a 1168x784 image. The pages look up dimensions in a hand-maintained IMAGE_DIMENSIONS map that covers only 135 article images and fall back to 1200x630 for the rest. Meanwhile, accurate per-article dimensions already exist in the generated metadata. Facebook, LinkedIn and Discord share cards see this on mobile and desktop. Google does not.
findings.evidence: src/pages/Blog.jsx:928 `const ogImageDims = (post.image && IMAGE_DIMENSIONS[post.image]) || { width: 1200, height: 630 };` with the same pattern at GuideDetail.jsx:243 and EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:109. A node script over mdx-meta.json found 135 article images in the map and 704 defaulting. Another script found that frontmatter imageWidth/imageHeight (exposed as post.imageWidth at src/lib/mdxPosts.js:92-93) match the real file on 857 of 857 articles. Full crawl, declared size compared with the actual public/ file: 752 wrong out of 1247 declaring. By section: blog 669 of 802, guides 44 of 120, encyclopedia 39 of 115, all other sections 0. Spot-checked live on 24 downloaded images. Example: https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/bearded-dragon-handling-guide/ declares 1200x630, but the served file is 1168x784. Separately, the 20 store pages and 43 Beastlypedia entries omit og:image:alt, and the store pages omit twitter:image.
findings.scope: 752 of 1327 pages, mostly articles
findings.fix: In Blog.jsx use post.imageWidth/post.imageHeight for the og tags. For hubs and encyclopedia pages, generate IMAGE_DIMENSIONS at build time from public/ instead of maintaining it by hand.

findings.title: Markup Google no longer uses: FAQ, HowTo, SearchAction
findings.claim: FAQPage runs on 828 pages and HowTo on 108 hubs, but Google has removed both rich results for every site, not just non-authoritative ones. The hub HowTo is really a table of contents: 554 of its 650 steps are links to other articles. The site-wide WebSite SearchAction points at a URL pattern that returns HTTP 404, for a feature Google retired in 2024. None of this is harmful (the FAQ answers are visible). It is dead weight, and the HowTo mislabels the hubs. Only Google sees this.
findings.evidence: Full crawl counts: FAQPage on 719 of 802 articles, 108 of 108 hubs, and /animal-days/. HowTo on 108 of 108 hubs (GuideDetail.jsx:264-280; the router branch maps guide.routes to steps with url /blog/<slug>/). Steps with a /blog/ url: 554 of 650. developers.google.com/search/updates: May 8, 2026 "This feature will no longer appear in Google Search starting May 7, 2026" (FAQ), and June 15, 2026 "The FAQ rich result feature is no longer shown in Google Search results". September 14, 2023: "Removed the How-to structured data documentation, as this rich result is no longer shown in search results". November 29, 2024: "The sitelinks search box feature is no longer available in Google Search results." SearchAction target at src/App.jsx:185 is https://beastlyfacts.com/search/{search_term_string}/, and `curl https://beastlyfacts.com/search/axolotl/` returned 404 with title 'Page Not Found | Beastly Facts' and robots noindex. /search/?q=axolotl returned 200. Also, the ItemList meant for the 20 'N-surprising-X-facts' posts never renders (0 of 20 live): mdxPosts.js:97 sets `content: ... ? true : null`, so the `typeof post.content === 'string'` check at Blog.jsx:1002 is always false.
findings.scope: 828 FAQ pages, 108 hubs, site-wide WebSite block, 20 listicles
findings.fix: Drop the HowTo block from GuideDetail.jsx and the potentialAction from the WebSite block. Keep or drop FAQPage as the owner prefers (it is harmless where visible). Delete the dead factsListSchema code or feed it real list items.

findings.title: Site-wide identity tags: wrong X handle, split brand name
findings.claim: All 1327 pages set twitter:site to '@beastlyfacts', but the site's X account is @Beastly_Facts, and x.com/beastlyfacts answers like a nonexistent handle, so X cards credit no account. The WebSite JSON-LD names the site 'BeastlyFacts', while the Organization block, og:site_name, the home title and the web manifest all say 'Beastly Facts'. Google's site-name system asks for one consistent name. X sees the handle on mobile and desktop share cards. Only Google sees the WebSite name.
findings.evidence: index.html:101 `<meta name="twitter:site" content="@beastlyfacts" />`. SOCIAL_BIOS.md:31 '## X (@Beastly_Facts)', and src/lib/data/author.js:34 'https://x.com/beastly_facts'. Status check `curl -A Mozilla/5.0 -w '%{http_code}'`: x.com/zzq_nonexistent_handle_8812 404, x.com/beastlyfacts 404, x.com/beastly_facts 200, x.com/nasa 200. src/App.jsx:181 `"name": "BeastlyFacts"` and App.jsx:196 'Beastly Facts'. Full crawl: og:site_name 'Beastly Facts' on 1327 of 1327 pages. The home <title> is 'Beastly Facts | Animal Facts and Pet Care Guides', and the manifest has "name": "Beastly Facts". Google site names doc: "Make sure whatever you use as the site name in structured data is consistent with how you refer to your site in other sources on your home page".
findings.scope: Site-wide, 1327 pages
findings.fix: Change index.html:101 to @Beastly_Facts and App.jsx:181 to 'Beastly Facts' (optionally adding alternateName 'BeastlyFacts').

visitor-privacy.notCheckable: I could not see what cookies are actually set. findings.title: Trackers load for everyone with no consent step, and the policy claims a consent flow that does not exist
findings.claim: Google Analytics (gtag.js), Ahrefs Web Analytics and the Cloudflare beacon run on every page for every visitor with no banner, no consent choice and no Consent Mode default, while the Privacy Policy tells visitors that hashed first-party data goes to Google Analytics 'with your consent' and separately invokes GDPR rights. No code sends hashed user data and no consent mechanism exists, so that bullet describes a practice and a choice the visitor never gets.
findings.evidence: index.html:153-156 queues gtag('js') and gtag('config','G-L0T3V8PPP7') at page start; index.html:157-170 injects https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js and https://analytics.ahrefs.com/analytics.js after the load event or an idle slot. `grep -rn -i consent src public/_worker.js index.html` returns only Privacy.jsx:51 and an unrelated legal note in src/lib/data/stateNotes.js:50, so there is no gtag('consent', ...) call. `grep -rn -E 'user_data|enhanced_conversions|sha256' src` returns nothing relevant. Live curl of https://beastlyfacts.com/ and /contact/ each contain 'G-L0T3V8PPP7' (2x), 'analytics.ahrefs.com/analytics.js' (1x) and 'static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js' (1x). Privacy.jsx:51 (live /privacy/ text line 21): 'User-Provided Data - with your consent, we may securely transmit hashed, first-party data to Google Analytics to improve conversion measurement and audience insights.' Privacy.jsx:107: 'If you are located in the EU/EEA, you have rights under GDPR'. Privacy.jsx:61 says the Site 'uses cookies'. I could not observe the cookies themselves because no browser can load the external site here; gtag.js with no consent default runs with Google's standard cookie behavior.
findings.scope: Site-wide: every page, mobile and desktop. Visitors see no banner; the misleading bullet is visible on /privacy/.
findings.fix: Delete the 'User-Provided Data' bullet at Privacy.jsx:51 now, since nothing sends such data. Then decide whether EEA/UK visitors get Consent Mode with analytics_storage denied by default (a gtag('consent','default',...) line before the config call at index.html:156) or a banner, and word Privacy.jsx:60-69 to match whichever is chosen.

repro.correctedClaim: Google Analytics (gtag.js), Ahrefs Web Analytics and the Cloudflare beacon do load on every page for every visitor. There is no banner, no on-site consent choice and no gtag('consent','default',...) call. Meanwhile the Privacy Policy says hashed first-party data goes to Google Analytics "with your consent" and invokes GDPR rights. That much is true. The part that is wrong is "no code sends hashed user data, so the bullet describes a practice the visitor never gets." The practice is switched on, but in the GA property's Google tag settings rather than in repo code. The live tag for G-L0T3V8PPP7 has automatic user-provided data collection enabled for email, phone and address, attached to form_submit, page_view and conversion events. It also has Google signals ENABLED with no region exclusions. The site has native email forms on the page: contact, newsletter, comments and the care package library. So the bullet describes a practice that is configured to run, and the false part is "with your consent". Google's own User-provided data policy requires end-user consent for this, and the site never asks for it. I could not watch a hashed email actually leave a browser, because no browser can load external sites here. Ahrefs and Cloudflare are cookieless and are disclosed as such, so the cookie-consent part of the problem is mainly GA. Who sees it: the missing banner affects all visitors on mobile and desktop. The misleading bullet is visible on /privacy/ on mobile and desktop. The tag configuration is visible only to Google and in network traffic.
repro.evidence:
Repo: index.html:153-156 sets up dataLayer and gtag, then calls gtag('js') and gtag('config','G-L0T3V8PPP7') with no consent call before them. index.html:157-171 injects googletagmanager.com/gtag/js and analytics.ahrefs.com/analytics.js on load or idle. `grep -rln -i -E "cookieconsent|cookiebot|klaro|osano|iubenda|onetrust|termly|__tcfapi|ad_storage|analytics_storage|ad_user_data" src public/_worker.js public/_headers index.html package.json prerender.mjs` matches only an index.html:18 comment about the removed AdSense FundingChoices popup, a prerender.mjs:570 URL blocklist and false hits in image and date code. There is no CMP and no consent default anywhere. The finder's grep summary was incomplete: `grep -rln -i consent` also hits index.html:18 and legalStatus.json, but the conclusion holds. Privacy.jsx:51 is the "User-Provided Data - with your consent, we may securely transmit hashed, first-party data to Google Analytics" bullet, Privacy.jsx:61 says "This Site uses cookies", and Privacy.jsx:107 is the GDPR line.

Live site: curl of /, /contact/, /privacy/ and /guides/bearded-dragon/ returned 200 for all 4. Each contains G-L0T3V8PPP7 (grep -o: 2), analytics.ahrefs.com/analytics.js (1) and static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js (1), with 0 gtag('consent'. The beacon tag is `<script defer src='https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js' data-cf-beacon='{"token": "0c826c66..."}'>`, injected by Cloudflare, not in the repo. A random sample of 40 of the 1327 sitemap URLs returned 200 for all 40, and all 40 carry the GA, Ahrefs and beacon tags with 0 consent calls. 0 of 42 non-privacy pages contain any cookie or consent banner text. The live /privacy/ text matches the bullet ("Last updated: September 24, 2026").

Live Google tag config: curl https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-L0T3V8PPP7 returned 200 and 620686 bytes. Its data block contains {"function":"__ogt_1p_data_v2",..."vtp_isAutoEnabled":true,..."vtp_autoPhoneEnabled":true,..."vtp_isEnabled":true,"vtp_autoAddressEnabled":true,"vtp_autoEmailEnabled":true,"vtp_isAutoCollectPiiEnabledFlag":true}. It also has __ccd_add_1p_data tag_id 19 with "vtp_acceptAutomatic":true and matching rules on form_submit, page_view and is_conversion. Other settings: "__ogt_google_signals","vtp_googleSignals":"ENABLED", __ccd_ga_regscope with disallowedRegions "", and __ogt_auto_events "vtp_enableForm":true.

Native forms with email inputs: src/components/shared/ContactForm.jsx:99/122, src/components/blog/BeehiivSubscribe.jsx:40/47, src/pages/CarePackageLibrary.jsx:314/316 and src/components/blog/PostEngagement.jsx:543/622.

Google docs: support.google.com/analytics/answer/12131703 says automatic detection will "Automatically inspect the page for strings that match a pattern for email addresses" and "User-provided data will be hashed". support.google.com/analytics/answer/12150158 item 3.2 says "You must obtain consent from your end users for the collection, passing and use of any PII".

Not observed: actual cookies set and actual hashed-data requests, because there is no working external browser here.
repro.fix:
Do not just delete the Privacy.jsx:51 bullet. The practice it describes is switched on in the Google tag, so deleting the bullet would make the policy hide a live practice. The owner should do one of two things:
(a) Turn off user-provided data collection, including automatic detection, in GA4 Admin > Data collection and in the Google tag settings for G-L0T3V8PPP7. Re-curl gtag.js to confirm __ogt_1p_data_v2 is gone or disabled, then delete the bullet.
(b) Keep the feature, add a real consent step that Google's policy requires, and reword the bullet to describe it.
Separately, the owner decides how EEA/UK visitors are handled for GA cookies and Google signals. Options are a Consent Mode default with analytics_storage, ad_storage, ad_user_data and ad_personalization denied for those regions, set by a gtag('consent','default',...) line before index.html:156; a banner; or turning off or region-restricting Google signals. Then reword Privacy.jsx:60-69 and :107 to match. Ahrefs and Cloudflare need no change beyond the existing cookieless disclosure.

impact.correctedClaim:
The core holds. The Google Analytics tag (G-L0T3V8PPP7), Ahrefs Web Analytics and the Cloudflare beacon load on every page I fetched (4 of 4) with no banner, no consent choice and no gtag('consent', ...) default anywhere in the repo. /privacy/ carries the "User-Provided Data - with your consent, we may securely transmit hashed, first-party data to Google Analytics" bullet.

Three details are wrong or overstated:
(1) Only Google Analytics raises a consent question. The policy itself describes Ahrefs and Cloudflare as cookieless (Privacy.jsx:50, 95, 96), so the "trackers" framing inflates the scope.
(2) "No code sends hashed user data" is true of the repo, but that does not prove nothing is sent. GA4's user-provided data collection is switched on in GA Admin, and it can auto-detect user data through a Google tag setting with no site code at all. The site has email fields in 5 components. I cannot see the GA Admin setting from here.
(3) Severity is medium, not high. Nothing breaks for any visitor on mobile or desktop, and Google Search is unaffected. The misleading bullet appears only on /privacy/, which is noindex. The exposure is legal and contractual: ePrivacy/GDPR and Google's EU consent terms for EEA/UK visitors who get the _ga cookies. For US visitors no state law requires opt-in for analytics at this site's scale.
impact.evidence:
Code: index.html:153-156 defines gtag and queues gtag('js') and gtag('config','G-L0T3V8PPP7'). Lines 157-170 inject googletagmanager.com/gtag/js and analytics.ahrefs.com/analytics.js after the load event or an idle slot.

`grep -rn -E "gtag\(|user_data|enhanced_conversions|sha256|..." src index.html public/_worker.js prerender.mjs` returns only App.jsx:83 (a comment), analytics.js:5-19 (gtag 'event' calls) and index.html:141-156. There is no consent call and no user_data. `grep -rln -i "zaraz|cookiebot|onetrust|klaro|cookieconsent"` returns nothing. The only trackEvent payloads are filter labels and search queries (Encyclopedia.jsx:404,436; Guides.jsx:221,259; Search.jsx:144).

Live: curl of /, /contact/, /privacy/ and /guides/bearded-dragon/ all returned 200. Each holds 2x 'G-L0T3V8PPP7', 1x 'analytics.ahrefs.com/analytics.js' and 1x 'static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js'. The beacon tag is `<script defer src='https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js' data-cf-beacon='{"token": ...}'>`, which Cloudflare injects; it is not in the repo. `curl -I https://beastlyfacts.com/` shows no Set-Cookie, so any GA cookies are client-side, and I could not observe them without a browser.

Live /privacy/ text: "User-Provided Data - with your consent, we may securely transmit hashed, first-party data to Google Analytics to improve conversion measurement and audience insights." It also has "you have rights under GDPR" and "This Site uses cookies and similar identifiers". Privacy.jsx:21 sets robots noindex. Privacy.jsx:50 and 95-96 call Ahrefs and Cloudflare cookieless.

Google doc https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/14077171 says: "(Optional) Select Collect automatically detected user-provided data to enable Google Analytics to detect user-provided data on your website automatically. If you select this option, you must also enable automatic collection in the Google tag." It also says "you must link your Google Analytics property to your Google Ads account". The bullet's wording ("consented, first-party data") mirrors this feature's language.

`grep -rln 'type="email"' src` lists ContactForm.jsx, PostEngagement.jsx, BeehiivSubscribe.jsx, CarePackageLibrary.jsx and Composer/Login.jsx, so auto-detection would have email fields to read.

Could not check: the GA Admin and Google tag settings, any Google Ads link, or the share of EEA/UK traffic. git history is shallow (80 commits), so `git log -S` could not show when the bullet was added.
impact.fix:
Owner decision, in this order.

1. Before touching the bullet, open GA4 Admin > Data collection and modification > Data collection. Check whether "User-provided data collection" is on, then check the Google tag's "Allow user provided data capabilities" and automatic detection.
   - If they are on, turn them off. The site runs no ads (Privacy.jsx:64), so the feature has nothing to feed. Then delete the bullet at Privacy.jsx:51.
   - If they are already off, delete the bullet straight away.
   - Do not delete the disclosure while the feature is still on.

2. For EEA, UK and CH visitors, the proportionate minimum is a region-scoped Consent Mode v2 default. Add it right after the gtag function definition at index.html:154 and before gtag('js') and gtag('config'): ad_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization and analytics_storage all 'denied', with a region list. With no banner, those visitors stay denied permanently. GA then gets cookieless modeled pings only for them, and that trade-off is acceptable. A banner is only needed if the owner wants full GA data from those regions. Ahrefs and Cloudflare need no change because they are cookieless.

3. Reword Privacy.jsx:61-63 to match the choice made in step 2.

4. Bump "Last updated" at Privacy.jsx:33 to the ship date in the owner's Eastern time, since section 8 promises an updated date.

5. Keep the new text free of em and en dashes. The existing " - " hyphen separators are fine.

findings.title: Privacy Policy misses web push, game and quiz logging, and Turnstile, and contradicts itself on quiz results
findings.claim: Several data flows in the code are absent from the Privacy Policy, and one statement is false: the policy says quiz results stay on the device and are not sent to the site, but quiz, Beastle and Critter Keeper results are inserted into Supabase and pushed to the owner's phone. Web push subscriptions (endpoint and keys) are stored in Supabase and never mentioned. Cloudflare Turnstile is live on the contact form but Cloudflare is listed only as host and analytics.
findings.evidence: Privacy.jsx:66 (live /privacy/ line 33): 'Local Storage - used to save favorite facts and quiz results locally in your browser. These stay on your device and are not sent to us.' Contradicted by src/lib/siteEvents.js:17-19 (supabase.from('site_events').insert({kind,label})) called from src/pages/Quiz.jsx:84, src/pages/ThemedQuizPage.jsx:167, src/components/encyclopedia/AnimalQuiz.jsx:58, src/pages/Beastle.jsx:1074 and src/pages/CritterKeeper.jsx:629 (label includes the user-typed pet name: 'Someone adopted a beardie named ${born.name}'); supabase/site_events.sql:3 says each row posts to ntfy. src/lib/beastle/results.js:15 inserts every daily Beastle result into beastle_results. Push: src/lib/pushNotifications.js:70-73 inserts endpoint, p256dh and auth into push_subscriptions (schema supabase/push_notifications.sql:24-32); site_events.sql:9 logs push opt-ins by trigger. Live /privacy/ mentions 'notification' only for the contact form (lines 18 and 61). Turnstile: live chunk /assets/TurnstileWidget-osNDfcTc.js contains site key '0x4AAAAAAEor-qnuRu1Jud3W' and loads 'challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js?render=explicit'; Privacy.jsx:96 describes Cloudflare only as 'hosts and serves the Site, and provides cookieless traffic analytics'. These rows carry no user identifier (site_events.sql:23-28, beastle_results.sql:7-12), so the gap is accuracy, not a hidden profile.
findings.scope: /privacy/ (one page, mobile and desktop), covering push opt-in on /pack/ and /beastle/, all quizzes, Beastle, Critter Keeper and /contact/.
findings.fix: Rewrite Privacy.jsx:66 to say anonymous scores and results are counted on the server with no identifier, add a 'Push Notifications' bullet (what the subscription stores, that it is deleted on opt-out, Supabase as host), and add Turnstile to the Cloudflare line at Privacy.jsx:96.

repro.correctedClaim: The core of the finding holds. The live /privacy/ page tells visitors that "favorite facts and quiz results" in local storage "stay on your device and are not sent to us". That is false. In the deployed build, quiz scores, Beastle daily results and Critter Keeper adoptions (with the pet name the visitor typed) are inserted into Supabase table site_events, and each row is relayed to the owner's phone through ntfy. Every finished daily Beastle also writes a row to beastle_results. Web push opt-ins (on /pack/, plus the Beastle reminder toggle on /beastle/) store the subscription endpoint and the p256dh and auth keys in push_subscriptions, with a beastle_reminder flag. Neither the Supabase bullet nor the ntfy bullet mentions any of this; both describe only comments, likes, shares, purchases and contact form messages. Cloudflare Turnstile is live, but the finding understates where. It runs on the /contact/ form and also on the visitor-facing care package library sign-in at /care-packages/library, and on /composer/login, which is owner-only. Cloudflare is listed only as host and analytics, and the Library Sign-In bullet does not mention the challenge. Two corrections. First, the proposed fix wording "deleted on opt-out" would itself be false. Opting out only unsubscribes in the browser, and the row stays until a later send gets a 404 or 410 from the push service and deletes it. Second, the Supabase and ntfy bullets also need updating. None of these flows can be seen by a visitor, and none of them concern Google: the policy text is visible on /privacy/ (mobile and desktop alike), and that page is noindex.

The toggle at about :248 (aria-label "Toggle navigation menu") has no md:hidden class, so it shows on mobile and desktop. The desktop top links at :39-43 are Guides, Articles, Facts, Beastle and Laws. The bottom tabs are Guides, Facts, Articles and My Pack. None of them is About.

8. **Footer.** src/components/layout/Footer.jsx:88-89 holds the About and "How guides are made" links. The footer renders on mobile too (its classes are pb-28 md:pb-12).

9. **Homepage JSON-LD.** The live homepage has 2 ld+json blocks. The second reads:
   {"@type": "Organization", "name": "Beastly Facts", "url": "https://beastlyfacts.com/", "logo": {...}, "sameAs": [4 URLs]}
   It has no founder and no contactPoint. The source is src/App.jsx:193-205, rendered in Helmet at :224-231. I also saw the same Organization on the live /guides/bearded-dragon/.

10. **About page copy.** Live /about/ text includes "It's just me. My name is Michael Ryan. I go by Mike. I built and maintain this whole site myself. I am not a veterinarian." (About.jsx:111-112) and "AI tools to help draft and organize. Nothing goes up until I have checked it against those sources myself" (About.jsx:168). It also has the section "How the site is funded" (About.jsx:182-186).

11. **About page schema.** The /about/ JSON-LD contains a ProfilePage whose mainEntity is {"@type":"Person","@id":"https://beastlyfacts.com/about/","name":"Michael Ryan","jobTitle":"Founder and writer, Beastly Facts", "worksFor":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Beastly Facts",...}}.

**Side note, outside this finding:** the live /guides/bearded-dragon/ JSON-LD has "author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Beastly Facts"}.

**Visibility:** the missing name and links in the hero affect real visitors on mobile and desktop. The Organization schema gap is seen only by Google, on every page.
repro.fix:
1. **Hero (visible change, mobile and desktop).** In HeroSection.jsx, add one short static byline under the subhead at line 208. Keep it plain prerendered text, not a motion wrapper, so it cannot add CLS, which the file's own comments are guarding. Name the owner and link both /about/ and /how-guides-are-made/, for example: "Researched and written by Michael Ryan, who keeps two rescued bearded dragons. How every guide is checked." Optionally, add "How guides are made" to the hamburger's "The site" group at Navbar.jsx:342.

2. **Schema (Google only).** In App.jsx:193-205, do not invent a new Person. Point the Organization at the Person that /about/ already publishes, by adding:
   `"founder": { "@type": "Person", "@id": "https://beastlyfacts.com/about/", "name": "Michael Ryan", "url": "https://beastlyfacts.com/about/" }`
   Optionally also add a contactPoint with url https://beastlyfacts.com/contact/.

findings.title: A first visit is never interrupted: no modals, push prompts, install prompts or login walls
findings.claim: Nothing fires on a first visit. The browser notification prompt only appears after a tap on an Enable or reminder toggle, there is no install-prompt hook, the newsletter is an inline form, achievement toasts are suppressed on first load, and no content is gated behind sign-in.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn beforeinstallprompt src public index.html`: 0 hits. Notification.requestPermission appears only in subscribeToPush (src/lib/pushNotifications.js:94), called from a click handler (src/components/pack/NotificationOptIn.jsx:57-65, mobile only per line 55) and from the Beastle reminder toggle (src/pages/Beastle.jsx:603). The launch-time restore (src/main.jsx:105) exits unless the device already opted in and permission is granted (pushNotifications.js:123-124). `grep -rn -E 'defaultOpen|open=\{true\}|showModal\(\)' src`: 0 hits. Newsletter is inline (src/components/shared/Newsletter.jsx:58). Achievements are seeded as already seen on first load (src/lib/FavoritesContext.jsx:243-251). The Critter Keeper bubble renders only if a game already exists (src/components/critterKeeper/CritterBubbleSlot.jsx:15). The AdSense FundingChoices consent popup was removed with the loader (index.html:17-25). The donate ask is a header button on desktop only (Navbar.jsx:240), not a modal. Auth guards only /composer/ (src/lib/AuthContext.jsx:6-7).
findings.scope: Site-wide, mobile and desktop.

findings.title: Contact reaches a human through two working channels
findings.claim: The contact form posts to a live Worker route that forwards the message to the owner's phone, with bot checks and an email fallback in the error message. The published address is on a domain with working mail exchangers. The page sets honest expectations on response time.
findings.evidence: src/components/shared/ContactForm.jsx:68 fetch('/api/contact', {method:'POST'}); public/_routes.json:3 includes '/api/contact'; public/_worker.js:597 handleContact validates, checks Turnstile, then posts to ntfy at _worker.js:646-656 ('From: ${email}' plus the message). Live probes that send nothing: `curl https://beastlyfacts.com/api/contact` -> {"error":"Method not allowed."} [405]; POST with body 'not-json' -> {"error":"Could not read the form."} [400]. ContactForm.jsx:161 error text adds 'You can also email hello@beastlyfacts.com.' DNS over HTTPS MX for beastlyfacts.com: '10 mx.zoho.com.', '20 mx2.zoho.com.', '50 mx3.zoho.com.'. Contact.jsx:238: 'This site is run by one person... responses may take a couple of days.'
findings.scope: /contact/, and the email link on /privacy/, /terms/ and /about/.

findings.title: Three medical-content articles lack the in-article vet disclaimer, one with medication doses
findings.claim: The vet disclaimer is consistently placed above the body on health articles, but 17 of 144 health-tagged articles have none. Three are medical in substance, including the ich treatment guide, which gives formalin and malachite green doses with only the small site footer line as a caveat.
findings.evidence: Script over 857 published MDX, health = slug contains 'health' or a tag containing 'Health': 144 articles, 127 with <VetDisclaimer>, every one of the 127 in the first 20% of the body, 17 without. Of the 17, 11 are enrichment guides; the medical ones: content/guides/aquarium-ich-treatment-guide.mdx:107 ('malachite green product at 5 ml per 10 gallons, dosed every 24 hours') and :109 ('Formalin... The dose is 25 mg/L'); content/guides/budgie-cere-color-guide.mdx:44 ('it can mean a testicular tumor') and :75 (scaly face mites); content/guides/cockatoo-screaming-feather-plucking-explained.mdx:76. Live https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/aquarium-ich-treatment-guide/ [200]: 'Not Veterinary Advice' count 0, only the footer line 'Not a substitute for professional veterinary advice.' By contrast, live /blog/bearded-dragon-health-issues-guide/ shows 'Not Veterinary Advice' directly under the H1, before the first paragraph.
findings.scope: 3 articles visibly, on mobile and desktop; the other 14 are low-risk enrichment, breeding-law or lighting pages.
findings.fix: Add <VetDisclaimer /> above the opener in the three files named, worded for fish on the ich guide (for example, 'confirm the diagnosis and dose with an aquatic vet or the product label').

findings.title: Contact email reads '[email protected]' in the served HTML on four trust pages
findings.claim: Cloudflare's email obfuscation rewrites hello@beastlyfacts.com in the static HTML of /contact/, /privacy/, /terms/ and /about/. Browsers with JavaScript decode it, but text-only readers, no-JS visitors, trust scanners and AI crawlers see '[email protected]' and a /cdn-cgi/ link instead of a mailto.
findings.evidence: Live /contact/: '[email protected]' inside the 'Email Me' card, href '/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#bcd4...'; the page loads 'email-decode.min.js'. Counts of 'cdn-cgi/l/email-protection' in live HTML: /contact/ 1, /privacy/ 2, /terms/ 3. Live /about/ text: 'Get in touch [a href=/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#224a...][email protected].' Source has the plain address (Contact.jsx:85-97, Privacy.jsx:106,119).
findings.scope: /contact/, /privacy/, /terms/, /about/. Visitors with JS on mobile and desktop see the real address; scanners and crawlers do not.
findings.fix: Turn off Email Address Obfuscation in Cloudflare (Scrape Shield) for beastlyfacts.com, since the contact form and Turnstile already absorb spam.

findings.title: Policy and Terms never name the operator, and 'Data Retention' gives no retention periods
findings.claim: The Privacy Policy calls the operator 'BeastlyFacts.com ("we")' yet speaks as 'me' in places without naming who that is. Its 'Data Retention & Your Rights' section states no retention period, although purchase emails, comments and push endpoints are kept with no stated end. The Terms name no operator and no governing law.
findings.evidence: Privacy.jsx:41 'BeastlyFacts.com ("we," "us," or "our")'; Privacy.jsx:48 and :98 'delivered to me'; Privacy.jsx:105-108 covers unsubscribe and access requests only. Privacy.jsx:54 stores purchase email 'so the purchase can be restored to you later' with no end date. src/pages/Terms.jsx:40-88 (9 sections) contain no person or entity name and no governing-law clause. The owner is named only on /about/ (About.jsx:111).
findings.scope: /privacy/ and /terms/, mobile and desktop.
findings.fix: Add 'BeastlyFacts.com is run by Michael Ryan' (with the contact email) to the opening of both pages, and add retention lines: purchases kept while the library runs, comments until deleted on request, push subscriptions until opt-out.

findings.title: Children's privacy line exists but does not fit a site with games and free-text forms
findings.claim: The policy has a standard under-13 statement, which is appropriate for a general-audience site. But the site's games and quizzes are the kind of features children use, and the comment, contact and newsletter forms (plus the Critter Keeper pet name that is sent to the owner) take free text with no age note. The policy also does not say a child's data will be deleted once found.
findings.evidence: Privacy.jsx:110-112: 'This Site is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. If you believe a child has provided personal data, please contact us immediately.' Kid-appealing features in primary nav and homepage: Beastle, Critter Keeper, personality quiz ('discover your animal spirit match', live homepage text). Forms collecting name and email: src/components/blog/PostEngagement.jsx:283-287 (author_email), ContactForm.jsx:110-127. Free text sent off-device: CritterKeeper.jsx:629. I found no child-directed marketing language: grep for 'for kids|for children|classroom|teachers' in src/pages and src/components returned 0 hits.
findings.scope: /privacy/, plus comment, contact and game surfaces, mobile and desktop.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to Privacy.jsx:111: 'If we learn we have collected personal information from a child under 13, we delete it,' and a short 'Ask a parent before posting your name or email' note under the comment form.

findings.title: Strong security headers on every page
findings.claim: The site sends a restrictive Content-Security-Policy, a Permissions-Policy that disables camera, microphone, geolocation, payment and USB, and a privacy-preserving Referrer-Policy. Header-based trust scanners score these. The CSP still allowlists AdSense and FundingChoices hosts that nothing loads now.
findings.evidence: `curl -sS -I https://beastlyfacts.com/` returned: 'permissions-policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=(), usb=()', 'referrer-policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin', and 'content-security-policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://www.googletagmanager.com ... https://pagead2.googlesyndication.com https://fundingchoicesmessages.google.com ... object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'; form-action 'self'; upgrade-insecure-requests;'. No set-cookie header on the homepage response.
findings.scope: Site-wide; seen by scanners and browsers, not by visitors directly.

store-donate.notCheckable: Stripe's hosted checkout and Payment Link pages load their content with JavaScript, so curl only gets an empty shell titled 'Stripe Checkout'. I could not see the business name, card statement descriptor, or Terms and Privacy links that Stripe shows buyers and donors. Those come from the Stripe account settings. I could not confirm that the seven donation Payment Links are active, or where they redirect after payment: a made-up buy.stripe.com URL returned the same 200, 593,022-byte shell. I could not see whether Stripe Climate is enabled. I did not test delivery after payment (webhook, thanks-page download, library sign-in code, receipt email) because that needs a real purchase. To confirm live mode I sent one checkout request for bearded-dragon, which created one unpaid live Stripe Checkout session; it charges nothing and expires on its own. The donor-return timings come from headless Chrome loading the live HTML and JS through a local proxy, because Chrome here cannot load external pages, so real-world timings will differ. I did not check trust-scanner scores (ScamAdviser and similar) or domain registration (WHOIS/RDAP); other lanes cover those. Every script and output is under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-beastlyfactss/c6c3a501-5606-5a8b-b8c9-191dbbf9547e/scratchpad/store-donate/; the repo was not modified (git status clean).

findings.title: Store never says who is selling
findings.claim: A buyer can pay without ever seeing the seller's name, location, or contact details. None of the store pages, the donate page, the Terms or the Privacy policy names the operator. None of those seven pages links to Contact, Terms, Privacy or About from the page body, so the only route is the site footer. The owner is named on /about/ only.
findings.evidence: I fetched 14 live pages with curl and extracted the visible text. 'Michael' or 'Ryan' appears 0 times on /care-packages/, /care-packages/store/, /care-packages/faq/, /care-packages/why-we-exist/, /care-packages/library/, /care-packages/thanks/, three product pages, /donate/, /terms/, /privacy/ and /contact/. It appears 2 times on /about/ ('It's just me. My name is Michael Ryan', src/pages/About.jsx:111). I counted href links to /contact/, /terms/, /privacy/ or /about/ in the HTML before <footer>: 0 on each of the 7 store and donate pages. In the Terms text, grep for governing|jurisdiction|located|operated by|LLC|state of matched nothing about the operator. Contact says only 'This site is run by one person', with no name. The live Product JSON-LD seller is {"@type":"Organization","name":"Beastly Facts"}, with no url, email or address. The checkout session at public/_worker.js:903-925 sets no custom_text and no consent_collection, so Stripe's page carries nothing from the site about who sells or the refund terms.
findings.scope: Visible to visitors on mobile and desktop on all 20 product pages, the store, the hub, the FAQ, thanks, the library and /donate/. Also the seller field in the Product structured data that Google reads.
findings.fix: Add a seller line under the final buy button in src/pages/CarePackageProduct.jsx (around line 462), for example 'Sold by Michael Ryan, Beastly Facts, [state], USA. Questions: Contact. Refunds: within 14 days, see Terms', with real links. Add a 'Who runs this site' sentence and a governing-law line to src/pages/Terms.jsx.

findings.title: Guide hubs lack the Amazon Associate statement
findings.claim: Species care guide hubs carry Amazon affiliate links, but none of them shows the program statement Amazon requires. Their disclosure is a generic 11px commission line placed after the link list, not before it.
findings.evidence: I fetched all 120 /guides/ URLs in the live sitemap. 84 of 120 contain amzn.to or www.amazon.com links. 0 of those 84 contain 'As an Amazon Associate'. 84 of 84 have the generic line, and on 84 of 84 it comes after the first Amazon link. Example from /guides/bearded-dragon/: 19 linked 'What to buy' items, then 'Underlined items are paid Amazon links. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you.' Source: src/pages/GuideDetail.jsx:541-544 (class text-[11px]). The footer does not carry the statement either. Amazon's Operating Agreement (affiliate-program.amazon.com/help/operating/agreement) says: 'You must clearly and prominently state the following ... on your Site ...: "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases."' The site does carry it on /privacy/, on articles and on /gear/.
findings.scope: 84 of 120 guide hub URLs, the site's main care pages. Visible to visitors on mobile and desktop.
findings.fix: Change GuideDetail.jsx:543 to 'As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases. Underlined items are paid Amazon links, at no extra cost to you.' and render it above the What to buy list (around line 520) at normal text size. Or add the statement to Footer.jsx so it appears on every page.

findings.title: Store is live, complete and has no dead ends
findings.claim: All 20 care packages can actually be bought. Before paying, a buyer can see price, format, page count, edition, the full contents, a free sample PDF and the payment processor. No page in the store is a coming-soon dead end.
findings.evidence: A Node run over CARE_PACKAGES found 20 entries: storefront 'stripe' 20 of 20, price '$8.99' 20 of 20, 42 to 54 pages, isCarePackageBuyable true for 20. On the live site, 20 of 20 product pages return 200. 20 of 20 /assets/care-packages/<id>/sample.pdf files return 200 application/pdf. 20 of 20 product pages carry Product JSON-LD with price 8.99 and the text 'Paid through Stripe'. One POST to /api/care-packages/checkout for bearded-dragon returned {"url":"https://checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/cs_live_..."}, which is a live-mode session. An unknown id returns 404 {"error":"This package is not sold here."}. The price is set server-side (public/_worker.js:893-906). The product page shows 'One time purchase · Instant PDF download', the full contents, edition history and a 'Coming in the next edition' list. No package has storefront 'soon', so CarePackageComingSoon.jsx never renders. No fetched page links to Gumroad (the old listing beastlyfacts.gumroad.com/l/beardeddragoncarepackage returns 404).
findings.scope: All 20 product pages, plus the store and hub. Visible on mobile and desktop.

findings.title: Donors land on a 404 page after paying
findings.claim: The page Stripe sends donors back to, /donate/success, is served with HTTP 404 and 'Page Not Found' markup. In a real browser the 404 page shows until JavaScript swaps in 'Thank You!'. On a cold mobile load that took about 1.5 to 3 seconds. The stated reason for not prerendering the page is wrong: the page reads no query parameters.
findings.evidence: curl -D - https://beastlyfacts.com/donate/success/ returned HTTP/2 404 with <title>Page Not Found | Beastly Facts</title> and body '404 - Page Not Found We couldn't find that page'. /donate/cancel returned the same. Headless Chrome cannot load external sites here, so I loaded that live HTML and the live JS through a local proxy. At 390px, cold cache: h1 was '404 - Page Not Found' at 50, 300, 800 and 1500 ms, then 'Thank You!' at 3000 ms. At 1280px, warm cache: the 404 heading at 50 ms, 'Thank You!' by 300 ms. prerender.mjs:160 and public/_redirects:209-216 skip these routes because they 'depend on Stripe redirect query params', but grep for useSearchParams|location.search|session_id in DonateSuccess.jsx and DonateCancel.jsx found nothing. The donation opens in a popup (Donate.jsx:74-78), so this is the popup's first screen.
findings.scope: Every completed or canceled donation. Visible to visitors on mobile and desktop. Google also sees 404s, but these pages are noindex anyway.
findings.fix: Add /donate/success and /donate/cancel to prerender.mjs's static routes so each ships its own noindex 200 page. Point the seven Stripe Payment Links' confirmation redirect at the trailing-slash URL.

findings.title: Donate page omits recipient, use and tax status
findings.claim: The donate page asks for one-time or monthly money without saying who receives it, what it pays for, that it is not tax-deductible, that it cannot be refunded, or how to cancel a monthly gift. Those terms exist only in the Terms page, which the donate page does not link.
findings.evidence: Live /donate/ visible text, in full: 'Support BeastlyFacts / Your contribution helps us keep sharing amazing animal facts. / Choose an amount: $1 $5 $10 Custom / Donation type: One-time Monthly / Donate / ...1%... / Payments are securely processed by Stripe. BeastlyFacts never stores your card details.' (src/pages/Donate.jsx:109-214). Terms.jsx:64 holds the rest: 'non-refundable unless applicable law requires otherwise. Monthly recurring donations can be canceled at any time by contacting us at hello@beastlyfacts.com.' The page has 0 body links to /terms/, /contact/ or /about/. Stripe is named, which is a reputable processor and is a plus.
findings.scope: /donate/ (noindex), visible to visitors on mobile and desktop.
findings.fix: Under the heading in Donate.jsx, add: 'Donations go to Michael Ryan, who runs Beastly Facts alone, and pay for hosting, research and photo licensing. Beastly Facts is not a charity, so donations are not tax-deductible. They are non-refundable; cancel a monthly gift any time from the Contact page.' Link Terms and Contact.

findings.title: Unverified 1% climate pledge on donate page
findings.claim: The donate page says 1% of every purchase or donation goes to CO2 removal. Nothing on the page backs this up, the store pages never mention it, and the owner's own storefront doc treats Stripe Climate as unconfirmed.
findings.evidence: src/pages/Donate.jsx:208 renders: 'BeastlyFacts.com will contribute 1% of every purchase or donation to removing CO₂ from the atmosphere'. There is no link. grep for '1% of' across src finds only that line, so none of the 20 product pages repeats it. docs/STOREFRONT.md:241 reads: 'Worth a look while in there: Settings -> Climate. If Stripe Climate is on, it takes 1% of gross revenue'.
findings.scope: /donate/. Visible to visitors on mobile and desktop.
findings.fix: Check Stripe Dashboard > Settings > Climate. If it is on, link Stripe's public Climate page for the account. If it is off, delete the box at Donate.jsx:205-210.

findings.title: Refund terms are two clicks away, with dead references
findings.claim: A product page never states the refund window. It links to a noindex FAQ, and the FAQ's refund answer points to 'the contact page' and 'the Terms' as plain text with no links.
findings.evidence:
'14 days' appears in the pre-footer body of 0 of 20 live product pages. The only path is the 'Format, printing and refunds' button (CarePackageProduct.jsx:497) to /care-packages/faq/ (robots noindex,follow). That answer, at CarePackagesFaq.jsx:43, says '...message me from the contact page ... The full refund policy is in the Terms.' It is rendered as a plain

at :114, and the live FAQ body has 0 links to /contact/ or /terms/. The store page sends buyers there too: 'Format, printing, and refunds are answered on the FAQ page.' (CarePackagesStore.jsx:144).
findings.scope: All 20 product pages and the FAQ. Visible to visitors on mobile and desktop.
findings.fix: Add 'Refunds on request within 14 days (Terms)' to the small print under the final buy button (CarePackageProduct.jsx:463). Render the FAQ refund answer as JSX with real links to /contact/ and /terms/, keeping the plain string for the JSON-LD.

findings.title: Affiliate disclosure is correct on articles and the gear page
findings.claim: Amazon Associates is the only active affiliate program. Articles and the gear page show the exact Amazon statement before the first link, and a build check enforces it. Links are marked sponsored, and Amazon prices and star ratings are deliberately not shown.
findings.evidence: src/lib/data/affiliateProducts.js has 126 amzn.to and 277 www.amazon.com links. Chewy is registered in RETAILERS but has 0 links. node scripts/check-affiliate-mdx.mjs (read-only) printed '2092 uses across 874 MDX files ... All clear.' I sampled 40 live blog posts: 15 had Amazon links, and 15 of 15 show 'As an Amazon Associate' before the first Amazon link. /gear/ shows 'As an Amazon Associate, we earn from qualifying purchases through the links below'. AffiliateLink.jsx:34 and ProductModal.jsx:124 use rel="noopener noreferrer sponsored". ProductCard.jsx:23-24 hides rating and price per the Associates policies. About has a 'How the site is funded' section (About.jsx:182-185) naming affiliate links, care packages and donations.
findings.scope: All articles with affiliate links and /gear/. Visible on mobile and desktop.

findings.title: Purchase terms and privacy are thorough
findings.claim: The Terms and Privacy policy spell out digital delivery, the 14-day refund window, the license, what a refund ends, donation refundability, chargebacks, and what purchase data goes to Stripe and Supabase. That is the content a cautious buyer or a scanner looks for, even though it is hard to reach from the store.
findings.evidence: Live /terms/ (Last updated October 12, 2026), section 4: 'Care packages are digital products: a downloadable PDF, sold as a one time purchase with no recurring charge... Refunds on care packages can be requested within 14 days of purchase...' Section 5 covers the license and library access (Terms.jsx:59-75). Live /privacy/ says: 'Purchase Data - if you buy a care package, Stripe collects your email address at checkout and passes it to us...' and lists Stripe and Supabase as processors.
findings.scope: /terms/ and /privacy/, both noindex.

findings.title: Return-policy markup overstates the refund promise
findings.claim: The Product structured data tells Google there is a 14-day free return window. The visible policy says refunds are reviewed case by case and may be declined.
findings.evidence: 20 of 20 live product pages carry hasMerchantReturnPolicy with returnPolicyCategory MerchantReturnFiniteReturnWindow, merchantReturnDays 14 and returnFees FreeReturn (CarePackageProduct.jsx:169-176). Terms.jsx:62 says: 'Each request is reviewed, and refunds are not automatic. We may decline a request made after 14 days, a request that does not name the package and a reason, or a request from anyone with a pattern of repeated refunds.'
findings.scope: Google only (structured data on 20 product pages).
findings.fix: Make the visible policy match the markup, for example 'refunds within 14 days are granted, declined only for repeat refund abuse', or soften the markup so it does not promise more than the Terms.

findings.title: Store page indexable but missing from sitemap
findings.claim: /care-packages/store/ can be indexed, but the sitemap leaves it out on the mistaken belief that it is noindex.
findings.evidence: generate-sitemap.js:199-201 says the three /care-packages/ subpages (store, why-we-exist, faq) each carry noindex,follow. Live /care-packages/store/ has no robots meta, and its only X-Robots-Tag header is 'max-image-preview:large'. /why-we-exist/ and /faq/ do have noindex,follow. CarePackagesStore.jsx:34-48 has no robots tag. The live sitemap has 1327 URLs, and 0 match care-packages/store/.
findings.scope: Google only, one URL.
findings.fix: Pick one: add <meta name="robots" content="noindex,follow" /> to CarePackagesStore.jsx, or list /care-packages/store/ in generate-sitemap.js and correct the comment.

claims.correctedClaim: Gridinsoft shows 63/100, "Trusted but Verify", from one automated check on Sept 27, 2026 at 5:14 (09:14 UTC). "First checked" and "Last checked" both carry that timestamp, and the HTTP Last-Modified header is Sun, 27 Sep 2026 09:14:06 GMT, so the score has not been refreshed since. The only live part is the radar's "Domain Maturity" day count, which is worked out each time the page is rendered. A cached desktop copy I fetched today said 151 days, which matches a render from about Oct 16. Fresh uncached renders today (one cache-busted, one with a mobile user agent) say 154 days. The second review was right that 151 days means about Oct 16, but wrong that the score updates live. Anyone who opens the Gridinsoft page sees this, on mobile and on desktop.
claims.evidence: curl https://gridinsoft.com/online-virus-scanner/url/beastlyfacts-com (Oct 19, 18:00 UTC). The title says "Beastlyfacts.com - Safe or Scam? (63/100 Trust Score)". The body has "Trusted but Verify", "First checked September 27, 2026 at 9:14 AM" and "Last checked September 27, 2026 at 9:14 AM". The JSON-LD has "dateModified":"2026-09-27T09:14:06Z" and "datePublished":"2026-09-27T09:14:06Z", and the response header is "last-modified: Sun, 27 Sep 2026 09:14:06 GMT". The first fetch came back with "cf-cache-status: HIT" and "cf-apo-via: tcache", and its SVG title read "Domain Maturity: 151 days". A refetch with ?nocache= ("cf-cache-status: BYPASS") and one with an iPhone UA ("cf-cache-status: MISS") both read "Domain Maturity: 154 days", and both still say "Last checked September 27, 2026 at 9:14 AM" and "(63/100 Trust Score)". Day counts from python: May 18 to Oct 16 = 151, to Oct 19 = 154, to Sep 27 = 132.

claims.correctedClaim: Gridinsoft's "Negative signals" list has one entry, "a relatively new domain (5 months)", and its radar says "Safety Level: 0 negative tags, 1 warning signal". claims.correctedClaim: The two back controls on a species hub behave differently. The mobile header 'Back' (under 768px) always calls navigate(-1). A visitor who arrived from Google in the same tab is sent back to Google, and in a fresh tab with no history the button does nothing. The in-page 'Back to Guides' button (all widths) first follows location.state.returnTo, then calls navigate(-1) when window.history.length > 1, and otherwise goes to /guides/. A same-tab Google landing therefore leaves the site, but a new-tab landing correctly reaches /guides/. Encyclopedia animal pages ('Back to Encyclopedia') use the same pattern. Deep dives do handle a cold landing correctly: they push the species hub URL instead of going back in history.

prior.missed:
1) A loop between hub and deep dive, visible on mobile and desktop. A visitor lands cold from Google on a deep dive and taps 'Back to Bearded Dragon'. That pushes /guides/bearded-dragon/ with no state (Blog.jsx:350). On the hub, both 'Back to Guides' (GuideDetail.jsx:81-82, since history.length > 1) and the mobile header Back (MobileBackButton.jsx:24) call navigate(-1), which returns to the article. The article is a POP landing again, so it offers 'Back to Bearded Dragon' again. The reader cycles between the two pages and never reaches /guides/. This was traced from code, not run in a browser.

2) Back labels that do not match where they go, visible on both. EncyclopediaAnimal.jsx:297 links to the hub with state returnTo '/encyclopedia/', and GuideDetail.jsx:75-78 honors it, so 'Back to Guides' lands on /encyclopedia/. In the other direction, GuideDetail.jsx:649 passes returnTo '/guides/', so 'Back to Encyclopedia' lands on /guides/.

3) The mobile header Back on hubs does nothing in a fresh tab or an installed app with no history: navigate(-1) is unguarded. useSwipeBack.js:31 guards the same case with window.history.length > 1, but this button does not. Mobile only.

4) /animal-facts/ ('Animal facts hub') is not a hub. It is 20 hardcoded bullets (AnimalFacts.jsx:8-53) with no sources, plus nine non-clickable 'keyword chips' rendered as spans (AnimalFacts.jsx:55-58, 94-100). Its CTA promises 'the animal personality quiz' (line 136) but links only /facts/ and /encyclopedia/. It contains a factual error at line 37: 'Cats have a specialized collarbone that lets them always land on their feet - it's called the \"righting reflex.\"' Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat_righting_reflex) says cats land on their feet because they have 'an unusually flexible backbone and no functional clavicle (collarbone)'. public/llms.txt:16 describes the page to AI crawlers as 'Fact browsing by animal', which it is not. Visible to visitors on both, and to Google.

5) Overlapping titles in the legal section, a Google issue that is also visible as H1s. /exotic-pet-laws/ ('Exotic Pet Laws by State: What Is Actually Banned'), /exotic-pet-laws/map/ ('Exotic Pet Laws by State: An Interactive US Map') and /exotic-pet-laws/state/ ('Exotic Pet Laws by State: All 50 States Ranked') are all self-canonical and indexable. The hub and the map share the identical H1 'Exotic pet laws, state by state' (live curl). This is a stronger case of the N7 problem than /facts/ vs /animal-facts/.

6) The menu and footer file and name the same items differently, visible on both. Feed is 'Feed' under Tools in the menu (Navbar.jsx:336) and 'The feed' under 'Learn something wild' in the footer (Footer.jsx:69). 'Is it legal?' and 'My Pack' are under Tools in the menu and 'The site' in the footer. 'Gear' in the menu is 'Recommended gear' in the footer. Glossary, How guides are made, All categories, My library, Terms, Privacy and Animal facts hub appear only in the footer.

7) Hub and Encyclopedia overlap. The menu lists 'Care guides' and 'Encyclopedia' as separate items, but /encyclopedia/ is titled 'Encyclopedia & Care Guides' and carries a two-tab toggle whose second tab is <a href=\"/guides/\">. Per-animal, /guides/<id>/ and /encyclopedia/animal/<id>/ are separate self-canonical URLs (live canonicals checked for bearded-dragon), and only the /guides/ one swaps the mobile logo for Back. CLAUDE.md describes these as 'one page with a toggle'.

8) The species hub's in-page back control and the deep dive's 'Back to <Species>' are <button> elements, not links (live HTML), so crawlers cannot follow them and they cannot be middle-clicked. On a mobile hub, the header Back and the in-page 'Back to Guides' also stack as two back controls with different logic.
